# sheetpane — the full public contract

> Everything llms.txt links to, inlined: the package READMEs, the docs, the laws and the component records. Version 0.0.0; links pinned to main.


---

<!-- source: README.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/main/README.md) -->

# sheetpane

**View, edit and review `.xlsx` and `.csv` files inside any web page.** Two web
components — the sheet and its error list — always in sync through one
in-memory workbook, and an export that writes every change into a copy of the
uploaded file. Nothing is uploaded: files are read in the browser tab.

```html
<script type="module">import '@sheetpane/grid';</script>
<sheetpane-excel pane="q3" src="holdings.xlsx" mode="edit"></sheetpane-excel>
<sheetpane-errors pane="q3"></sheetpane-errors>
```

**Start a new app:** `npm create sheetpane@latest` — vanilla, React, Next.js,
Vue, Angular or Svelte, with the sheet and its errors panel, a sample file and
rules file, one test and the agent skills ([`create-sheetpane`](packages/create-sheetpane/README.md)).

## Packages

| package | what it is |
|---|---|
| [`@sheetpane/grid`](packages/grid/README.md) | the web components `<sheetpane-excel>` and `<sheetpane-errors>`, the pane's workbook, the plugin host |
| [`@sheetpane/import`](packages/import/README.md) | `.xlsx` or `.csv` in, a plain JavaScript workbook out |
| [`@sheetpane/export`](packages/export/README.md) | a workbook in, `.xlsx` or `.csv` out — build, patch the original, CSV, `download()` |
| `@sheetpane/numfmt` · `formulas` · `styles` · `validation` · `condfmt` · `images` · `charts` · `comments` | optional plugins, each its own package |
| [`create-sheetpane`](packages/create-sheetpane/README.md) | `npm create sheetpane` — a working app to start from |

All are published at one version, ESM with types, with no runtime dependency
outside the project except the two engines two plugins use.

## Try it

```sh
pnpm install
just demo-html     # the plain index.html demo — http://127.0.0.1:5173
just demo-react    # the React 19 demo — http://127.0.0.1:5174
just demo-check    # both demos, used in Chromium: flag, resolve, edit, export, font, pop-up, CSV, refusal
just demo-packed   # the same, with both demos installed from `pnpm pack` tarballs
```

`HOST=0.0.0.0 just demo-html` serves the plain demo to other devices on your
network (e.g. a phone).

## Develop

| command | does |
|---|---|
| `just install` | `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` |
| `just check` | type-check, test (Node + Chromium, coverage) and build every package |
| `just test-pkg <name>` | one package's tests, e.g. `just test-pkg grid` |
| `just test-browsers` | the browser suites in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit |
| `just pack-check` | every package packed as npm would publish it, checked |
| `just create-check [template…]` | each `create-sheetpane` template scaffolded, installed from the tarballs, built and tested |
| `just release <version>` | bump every package together, check, tag, publish |

Requires Node 20+, pnpm 10 and [just](https://just.systems). How work is done
here — the records, the queue, the laws — starts at [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md);
the map is [`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md).

<!-- source: packages/grid/README.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/main/packages/grid/README.md) -->

# @sheetpane/grid

**View and edit `.xlsx` and `.csv` files inside any web page, and review them.**
Two web components, always in sync through one in-memory workbook:

- `<sheetpane-excel>` — the sheet. View or Edit; every change stays in memory;
  **Download** hands back the file — as opened when nothing changed, else a
  copy of the uploaded file with the changes in it.
- `<sheetpane-errors>` — the errors flagged on the sheet: what's wrong, what it
  should be. Put it anywhere — beside the sheet, in a side column, in another tab.

Nothing is uploaded: the file is read in the browser tab. No framework inside
or outside; no font of its own — yours is used.

```sh
pnpm add @sheetpane/grid      # or npm / yarn
```

Starting from nothing? `npm create sheetpane@latest` makes a working app —
vanilla, React, Next.js, Vue, Angular or Svelte — with both elements, a sample
file, a rules file and one test.

## Plain HTML

```html
<script type="module">import '@sheetpane/grid';</script>

<sheetpane-excel pane="q3" src="/files/holdings.xlsx" mode="edit" author="Arpit" style="height:640px"></sheetpane-excel>
<sheetpane-errors pane="q3" author="Arpit" style="height:640px"></sheetpane-errors>
```

The same `pane` id links them. Mount order does not matter, and they may sit
in different containers, tabs or dialogs.

## React 19

React 19 sets properties and listens to custom events on custom elements
natively:

```tsx
import '@sheetpane/grid';

export function Review({ file }: { file: File }) {
  return (
    <>
      <sheetpane-excel pane="q3" mode="edit" file={file} onsheetpane-change={(e) => console.log(e.detail)} />
      <sheetpane-errors pane="q3" onsheetpane-errors={(e) => save(e.detail.errors)} />
    </>
  );
}
```

**Typed JSX:** add `import type {} from '@sheetpane/grid/jsx';` once — e.g. in
a `sheetpane.d.ts` beside your sources — and both tags, their attributes,
properties and `onsheetpane-…` props are typed, payloads included
(`e.detail.ref`). See [Typings and editor support](#typings-and-editor-support).

**React 18** sets attributes only: use a `ref` for properties and events.

```tsx
const ref = useRef<HTMLElement & { file?: File }>(null);
useEffect(() => {
  const el = ref.current!;
  el.file = file;
  const on = (e: Event) => save((e as CustomEvent).detail.errors);
  el.addEventListener('sheetpane-errors', on);
  return () => el.removeEventListener('sheetpane-errors', on);
}, [file]);
return <sheetpane-excel ref={ref} pane="q3" />;
```

### React hooks (recipes)

Not a package (SR-LAW-4: no framework wrappers in v1) — copy
[`examples/react/src/sheetpane-hooks.ts`](../../examples/react/src/sheetpane-hooks.ts)
into your app. Each hook takes a `ref` to `<sheetpane-excel>`, is built on
`useSyncExternalStore` with a stable selector (a component re-renders only
when what it reads changes), removes its listeners on unmount, and is safe
under StrictMode. React 19 and 18.

```tsx
const sheet = useRef<SheetpaneExcel>(null);
const sel = useSelection(sheet);         // { sheet, ref, range, column: { index, letter, header }, value, text }
const edit = useCellEdit(sheet);         // { editing, ref, column, draft } while the user types
const { count, canUndo } = useChanges(sheet);
const { errors, open } = useErrors(sheet);
const wb = useWorkbook(sheet);           // the pane's store
const rules = useColumnRules(sheet, { Age: { type: 'integer', min: 18 } }); // { checking, done, total }
useSheetpaneEvent(sheet, 'sheetpane-beforechange', (e) => { if (Number(e.detail.now) < 0) e.preventDefault(); });
return <sheetpane-excel ref={sheet} pane="r1" mode="edit" src="people.xlsx" />;
```

The primitive under all of them, for a hook of your own:

```ts
const units = useSheetpane(sheet, (store) => store.value('Holdings', 'F3'), null);
```

## Vue, Svelte, Solid, Angular

The elements are standard custom elements, so every framework renders them
once `import '@sheetpane/grid'` has run in the browser. No wrapper package;
an `import type` line types them.

**Vue 3** — tell the compiler the tags are custom elements, then bind
properties with `.prop` and listen with `@`:

```js
// vite.config.js
vue({ template: { compilerOptions: { isCustomElement: (tag) => tag.startsWith('sheetpane-') } } })
```

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import '@sheetpane/grid';
import type {} from '@sheetpane/grid/vue';   // GlobalComponents: props and @sheetpane-… typed
</script>
<template>
  <sheetpane-excel pane="q3" mode="edit" :file.prop="file" @sheetpane-change="(e) => log(e.detail.ref)" />
  <sheetpane-errors pane="q3" @sheetpane-errors="(e) => save(e.detail.errors)" />
</template>
```

**Svelte** — `import type {} from '@sheetpane/grid/svelte';` once (e.g. in
`src/app.d.ts`); Svelte 5 listens with `onsheetpane-change={…}`, Svelte 4 with
`on:sheetpane-change={…}`; both set properties when the element has one.

```svelte
<sheetpane-excel pane="q3" mode="edit" file={file} onsheetpane-change={(e) => log(e.detail.ref)}></sheetpane-excel>
```

**Solid** — `import type {} from '@sheetpane/grid/solid';` once. Solid sets a
custom element's props as properties, so write an attribute that has no
property with `attr:`, and listen with `on:`:

```tsx
<sheetpane-excel attr:pane="q3" attr:header-row="2" mode="edit" prop:file={file()} on:sheetpane-change={(e) => log(e.detail.ref)} />
```

**Angular** — no package and no typings to import: add
`CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA` to the component that renders the tags, bind
properties with `[…]` and events with `(…)`:

```ts
import { Component, CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA } from '@angular/core';
import '@sheetpane/grid';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-review',
  standalone: true,
  schemas: [CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA],
  template: `
    <sheetpane-excel pane="q3" mode="edit" [file]="file" (sheetpane-change)="onChange($event)"></sheetpane-excel>
    <sheetpane-errors pane="q3" (sheetpane-errors)="save($event.detail.errors)"></sheetpane-errors>`,
})
export class ReviewComponent { file: File | null = null; onChange(e: Event) { console.log((e as CustomEvent).detail); } save(errors: unknown[]) {} }
```

**Next.js and other SSR** — the import is safe on the server (the elements
just do not register); render the tags in a client component.

## Typings and editor support

| file | for |
|---|---|
| `@sheetpane/grid/custom-elements.json` | the [Custom Elements Manifest](https://github.com/webcomponents/custom-elements-manifest) (schema 2.1.0): every attribute, property, method, event (with its payload type), slot, CSS part and `--sp-*` property; `package.json`'s `customElements` points at it |
| `@sheetpane/grid/jsx` | React 19 — `React.JSX.IntrinsicElements` |
| `@sheetpane/grid/vue` | Vue 3 — `GlobalComponents` (Volar / vue-tsc) |
| `@sheetpane/grid/svelte` | Svelte 4 and 5 — `SvelteHTMLElements` |
| `@sheetpane/grid/solid` | Solid — `JSX.IntrinsicElements` |
| `@sheetpane/grid/vscode.html-custom-data.json` | VS Code: tags, attributes and their values in `.html` |
| `@sheetpane/grid/vscode.css-custom-data.json` | VS Code: the `--sp-*` properties in `.css` |
| `@sheetpane/grid/web-types.json` | JetBrains IDEs (WebStorm, IntelliJ) — read automatically through `package.json`'s `web-types` |

Each typing entry is types only (`import type {} from '…'`); the framework is
never a dependency. Each also exports the element types it builds on —
`SheetpaneExcelEventMap`, `SheetpaneExcelAttributes`,
`SheetpaneExcelProperties` and the same for `SheetpaneErrors` — for typing
your own wrappers.

**VS Code** — point the workspace settings at the editor data:

```json
// .vscode/settings.json
{
  "html.customData": ["./node_modules/@sheetpane/grid/dist/vscode.html-custom-data.json"],
  "css.customData": ["./node_modules/@sheetpane/grid/dist/vscode.css-custom-data.json"]
}
```

All of it is generated from the element sources and their TSDoc
(`scripts/build-manifest.mjs`, run by the build); a test fails when the
committed manifest drifts from the elements.

## `<sheetpane-excel>`

| kind | name | what |
|---|---|---|
| attribute | `pane` | the shared id; the same on both elements |
| attribute | `src` | a URL (read with a GET), a `data:` URL or base64 |
| attribute | `mode` | `view` (default) or `edit` |
| attribute | `display` | `tab` (default; fills its container) or `popup` (a modal dialog; `open` shows it) |
| attribute | `open` | shows the pop-up |
| attribute | `author` | written on errors flagged here |
| attribute | `plugins` | the enabled plugin ids, e.g. `numfmt formulas` |
| attribute | `header-row` | the row holding column titles (default `1`) — every event names the column by it, and column rules match by it |
| attribute | `theme` | `light` (default), `dark` or `auto` (follows the page's `prefers-color-scheme`) |
| attribute / property | `on-invalid` / `onInvalid` | what a failing column rule does by default: `flag` (default) or `block` |
| attribute / property | `rules-src` / `rules` | a rules file by URL, or as an object — see [Rules file](#rules-file) |
| attribute / property | `flagging` | `on` (default) or `off`: no Flag issue, no composer, no pop-up card — errors are read in `<sheetpane-errors>` |
| property | `columns`, `validate` | column rules by title, and a check function — see [Column rules](#column-rules) |
| property | `file` | a `File`, `Blob`, `ArrayBuffer` or `Uint8Array` to read |
| property | `workbook` | the pane's store (get, or set your own from `createWorkbook()`) |
| property | `errors`, `errorTypes` | the review; the error-type catalog |
| method | `load(src, name?)` | read a file (any of the above) |
| method | `export(options?, { format? })` | `Promise<Blob>` — the upload with every change; `format: 'csv'` from an `.xlsx` is the current sheet, `'xlsx'` from a `.csv` one sheet |
| method | `select(sheet, ref)`, `getErrors()`, `setErrors(list)`, `undo()`, `redo()` | |
| event | `sheetpane-load`, `sheetpane-errors {errors, plugins}`, `sheetpane-mode {mode}`, `sheetpane-history`, `sheetpane-export {blob, kind, name, format, converted, original?}` (cancelable — prevent it to save the file yourself; `original: true` when Download hands back the untouched file, `converted` when ▾ chose the other format), `sheetpane-close` | bubbling, composed |

### Following an edit

Every edit fires these, in this order, on the element where it happened;
every payload names the column `{ index, letter, header }` (the title from
`header-row`):

| event | fires | detail | cancel it to |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sheetpane-select` | the selected cell moves | `{sheet, ref, column, value}` | — |
| `sheetpane-editstart` | the cell bar opens on a cell | `{sheet, ref, column, value}` | keep the cell read-only |
| `sheetpane-input` | each keystroke, before saving | `{sheet, ref, column, draft, was}` | — |
| `sheetpane-beforechange` | Enter, Tab, blur, Delete, or each cell of a paste | `{sheet, ref, column, was, now}` | refuse the value |
| `sheetpane-change` | after saving | `{sheet, ref, kind, was, now}` | — |
| `sheetpane-editcancel` | Esc, or a column rule set to `block` refused the value | `{sheet, ref}` (refused: `{sheet, ref, reason: 'blocked', message}`) | — |
| `sheetpane-sheet` | the sheet tab changes | `{sheet}` | — |

A refused value never reaches the change map, undo or a plugin.

```js
excel.addEventListener('sheetpane-beforechange', (e) => {
  if (e.detail.column.header === 'Units' && Number(e.detail.now) < 0) e.preventDefault();
});
```

**Keys:** arrows, Shift+arrows, Home/End, Ctrl+Home/End, PageUp/PageDown;
Enter or F2 edits; typing replaces; Delete clears; Ctrl/⌘+V pastes tab-separated cells; **F flags an issue**;
**right-click, Shift+F10 or the Menu key** opens the selection actions (Flag issue, Copy ref, Copy value and
plugin actions) under the cell — the same actions sit at the right end of the cell bar, never over the cells; Esc
cancels or closes the pop-up; Ctrl/⌘+Z undo, Ctrl+Y / ⌘+Shift+Z redo. The `?`
button lists them, plugins' shortcuts included.

**Selecting a range:** drag (the grid scrolls when the pointer reaches an edge), Shift+click, or click a
column header, row header or the corner — drag or Shift+click headers for several. Ctrl/⌘+arrow jumps to
the edge of the data (with Shift: selects to it); Ctrl+Space selects the column, Shift+Space the row,
Ctrl/⌘+A the data and then the sheet; Shift+Backspace goes back to the active cell; Enter and Tab move
inside a range. On a range, Ctrl/⌘+C copies it so Excel and Google Sheets paste a grid, Delete clears it
(Edit, one undo step), one pasted value fills it, and the status line shows **Count · Sum · Average**.
`sheetpane-select` carries `range` (`B3:D8`) and fires once a drag is released. On a touch screen a finger
scrolls, a tap selects, and a range shows two handles to extend it.

## Column rules

Check what a user types, by column title. Rules are plain JSON — save and load
them as a file if you like — and failures go into the one error list as
`author: "host"` errors that resolve themselves when the cell passes.

```js
excel.columns = {
  Name:   { required: true },
  Email:  { pattern: '^[^@\\s]+@[^@\\s]+\\.[a-z]{2,}$', unique: true },
  Age:    { type: 'integer', min: 18, max: 99, onInvalid: 'block' },
  Status: { oneOf: ['Active', 'Inactive'], severity: 'warning' },
};
excel.validate = async (ctx, signal) =>
  ctx.column.header === 'Email' && ctx.phase !== 'input' && (await api.taken(ctx.value, { signal }))
    ? { severity: 'error', message: 'Email already used' }
    : null;
```

| rule | passes when |
|---|---|
| `required` | the cell is not blank (every other rule skips a blank cell) |
| `type` | `text` · `number` · `integer` · `date` · `boolean` |
| `min`, `max` | a number in range; for `type: 'date'`, an ISO date or a serial |
| `minLength`, `maxLength` | the text's length |
| `pattern` | the text matches (values over 10,000 characters are not tested — **avoid patterns that backtrack catastrophically**: they run on the page) |
| `oneOf` | the value is one of the list (trimmed, case-insensitive) |
| `unique` | no other row of the column holds it |
| `message`, `severity`, `onInvalid` | replace the generated message; `error` (default) · `warning` · `note`; `flag` (default) · `block` |

- **Titles** match trimmed and case-insensitive (an exact title wins). A
  title the file lacks is one `note` error; a duplicated title checks the
  first column and adds one `note`. The file always loads.
- **`validate(ctx, signal)`** runs for every cell of a titled column, sync or
  async. `ctx` is `{phase, sheet, ref, row, column, value, was, original,
  rowValues}`, `rowValues` keyed by title, so a rule can read the row; editing
  any cell asks the row again. A newer edit to a cell aborts the older check
  (`signal`) and its result is dropped. Return `null` or `{severity, message,
  expected?}`.
- **Phases:** `input` — 150 ms after typing stops, an outline and a message
  at the cell bar, nothing stored; `commit` — on save, `flag` stores the value
  and adds an error, `block` refuses it (only a JSON rule or a synchronous
  result can block; an async result flags); `load` — every row, in slices,
  with the progress in the status line.
- Setting `columns`, `validate` or `onInvalid` again re-checks every row;
  host errors no longer produced are removed. People's errors are never
  touched, and a rule never edits a cell.
- Rules belong to the pane: `workbook.setColumnRules({ columns, validate,
  onInvalid, headerRow })` does the same without an element.

## Rules file

Ship the rules next to your code as JSON and point the sheet at them; every
cell they cover is checked on load and the failures are listed in
`<sheetpane-errors>`. With `flagging="off"` the sheet shows no Flag issue and
opens no pop-up — the errors panel is the one place errors are read.

```html
<sheetpane-excel pane="q3" src="./q3.xlsx" rules-src="./sheetpane.rules.json" flagging="off"></sheetpane-excel>
<sheetpane-errors pane="q3"></sheetpane-errors>
```

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://unpkg.com/@sheetpane/grid/rules.schema.json",
  "version": 1,
  "sheets": {
    "*": {
      "columns": { "Email": { "pattern": "^[^@\\s]+@[^@\\s]+\\.[a-z]{2,}$", "unique": true } }
    },
    "Accounts": {
      "headerRow": 2,
      "columns": {
        "Account ID": { "required": true, "pattern": "^AC-\\d{5}$", "message": "Account IDs are AC- and five digits" },
        "Units":      { "type": "integer", "min": 0 },
        "Status":     { "oneOf": ["Active", "Inactive"], "noneOf": ["TBD", "N/A"], "severity": "warning" }
      },
      "cells": {
        "B1":     { "equals": "Q3 review", "note": "the title cell the export pipeline reads" },
        "H3:H40": { "type": "number", "min": 0, "max": 1 }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

- **`sheets`** by name; `"*"` applies to every sheet and a named sheet's rule
  for the same title wins. Each sheet has `headerRow`, `columns` (by title,
  as [Column rules](#column-rules)) and `cells` (an A1 cell or range).
- **The words** are Column rules' plus `equals` (the one valid value; a blank
  cell fails it), `noneOf` (values never valid) and `note` (for whoever
  maintains the file — never shown as the message).
- **`$schema`** gives your editor autocomplete and red squiggles: the schema
  ships as `@sheetpane/grid/rules.schema.json`.
- **Never silent, never a throw:** an unknown key, word or version, a sheet,
  title or cell the workbook lacks, or a pattern that is not a regular
  expression becomes one `note` in the errors panel; the rest still applies.
- `rules-src` is read with a GET like `src`; `excel.rules = object` does the
  same without a fetch. Setting either checks every row again. The element's
  `columns` and `validate` still work beside it — the file's rule wins for the
  same title, with a note.
- **YAML or TOML:** parse it yourself and pass the object — the package reads
  JSON only, so it carries no parser:

  ```js
  import { parse } from 'yaml';      // or: import { parse } from 'smol-toml';
  excel.rules = parse(await (await fetch('./sheetpane.rules.yaml')).text());
  ```

## `<sheetpane-errors>`

| kind | name | what |
|---|---|---|
| attribute | `pane`, `author`, `plugins` | as above |
| attribute | `readonly` | hides the form, Resolve and Delete — a sign-off screen |
| property / method | `errors`, `errorTypes`, `getErrors()`, `setErrors(list, { plugins })` | |
| event | `sheetpane-errors {errors, plugins}`, `sheetpane-reveal {error}` | **Show in sheet**: switch to the sheet's tab or open the pop-up |

## Saving and restoring a review

Errors are plain JSON (`SheetpaneError`, schema `v: 1`). Listen to
`sheetpane-errors`, store `detail.errors` and `detail.plugins` where you like,
and give them back after the file loads:

```js
excel.addEventListener('sheetpane-load', () => errors.setErrors(saved.errors, { plugins: saved.plugins }));
```

An error whose cell no longer shows what was found is tagged *stale*, never
moved.

## Plugins

Features beyond review — every Excel number format, live formulas, cell
styles, data validation, conditional formatting, pictures, charts, comments —
are separate packages that plug into six hooks and six slots. With none
installed the grid is the plain review tool. **See each one on the same
workbook:** the demos' plugin gallery (`just demo-html` or `just demo-react`)
has a tab per plugin, plus Vanilla and All plugins.

```js
import '@sheetpane/numfmt';     // registers "numfmt"
```

```html
<sheetpane-excel pane="q3" plugins="numfmt"></sheetpane-excel>
```

Or build the store yourself: `el.workbook = createWorkbook({ plugins: [...] })`.

## Styling

Colours, spacing and radii are `--sp-*` custom properties on the elements
(`--sp-accent`, `--sp-ink`, `--sp-line`, …); `@sheetpane/grid/style.css`
lists the defaults, and `theme="dark"` swaps in the dark set. The font is yours: set it on the element or any ancestor.

The specs are the records [SR-GRID](../../records/0105_GRID.md) and
[SR-ERRORS](../../records/0106_ERRORS.md).

**Using an AI coding agent?** `npx sheetpane-skills install` puts sheetpane's skills for Claude Code, Kiro and Codex into your repository.

<!-- source: packages/export/README.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/main/packages/export/README.md) -->

# @sheetpane/export

**A plain JavaScript object in, an `.xlsx` or `.csv` file out.** No runtime
dependencies. Runs in evergreen browsers and Node 20+. Used by
`@sheetpane/grid`'s Export button; usable on its own.

```sh
pnpm add @sheetpane/export      # or npm / yarn
```

## The object

```ts
type Cell = string | number | boolean | null;
interface Sheet { name: string; rows: Cell[][]; merges?: string[]; columnWidths?: number[]; hidden?: boolean }
interface Workbook { sheets: Sheet[] }
interface Change { sheet: string; ref: string; value: Cell }
```

`rows[0][0]` is A1. `merges` are ranges like `'A1:J1'` — the top-left cell is
centred, the one format sheetpane keeps. `columnWidths` are Excel character
widths.

## Build a new `.xlsx`

```ts
import { toXlsx } from '@sheetpane/export';

const bytes = await toXlsx({
  sheets: [{ name: 'Sales', rows: [['Region', 'Total'], ['North', 1200], ['South', 950.5]], columnWidths: [14, 10] }],
});
```

Text is written as inline strings, numbers and booleans typed. `{ compression:
'store' }` gives byte-identical output on every engine (larger; the audit
mode); the default compresses with `CompressionStream` / `zlib`.

## Patch the uploaded `.xlsx` — keep everything else

```ts
import { patchXlsx } from '@sheetpane/export';

const out = await patchXlsx(originalBytes, [
  { sheet: 'Holdings', ref: 'G6', value: 268.4 },
  { sheet: 'Holdings', ref: 'A7', value: 'AC-10044' },
]);
```

Only the changed cells are rewritten (their style is kept); every other part
of the file — charts, pivot tables, comments, names, styles — is copied byte
for byte. Excel is asked to recalculate formulas on open, and pivot tables
whose source changed to refresh.

## Write CSV

```ts
import { toCsv } from '@sheetpane/export';

const { text, guarded } = toCsv(sheet);                 // comma, CRLF, UTF-8 BOM
const semi = toCsv(sheet, { delimiter: ';', bom: false });
```

**Formula injection guard — on by default.** A text cell that starts with `=`
`+` `-` `@`, a tab or a carriage return gets a leading `'`, so a spreadsheet
shows it instead of running it. Plain numerals such as `-150` are left alone.
**This changes the data**; `guarded` lists the cells it touched (`['A1', …]`)
so your app can say so. Turn it off with `{ guardFormulas: false }`.

`toCsv` writes one sheet; for a multi-sheet workbook, pick the one you mean.

## Errors

Every refusal is an `ExportError` with a `code` and the `sheet` / `ref` it is
about: a bad sheet name (1–31 characters, none of `[ ] : * ? / \`, unique
ignoring case), more than 1,048,576 rows or 16,384 columns, `NaN` or
`Infinity`, text over 32,767 characters, overlapping merges.

## Save the file — `download(data, filename, options?)`

One call turns export output into a file the browser saves. `.xlsx` and
`.csv` only; the bytes are never changed. The spec is
[SR-DOWNLOAD](../../records/0101_DOWNLOAD.md).

```ts
import { toXlsx, toCsv, download } from '@sheetpane/export';

download(await toXlsx(book), 'sales.xlsx');                 // 1 · bytes → sales.xlsx
download(toCsv(sheet, { bom: true }).text, 'sales.csv');    // 2 · text, BOM kept: Excel shows "José"
download(new Blob([bytes]), 'report.xlsx');                 // 3 · a Blob you already have
download(await toXlsx(book), 'Q3 report');                  // 4 · → Q3 report.xlsx (text → .csv)
download(bytes, 'FY26: North/South?.xlsx');                 // 5 · → FY26_ North_South_.xlsx
download(text, 'data.csv', { type: 'text/csv;charset=utf-8;header=present' }); // 6 · your own type
```

**7 · Errors are explicit, never silent.** Each names the file:

```ts
download(bytes, 'sales.pdf');            // ✗ "sales.pdf" — sheetpane saves .xlsx or .csv only
download(new Blob([bytes]), 'mystery');  // ✗ "mystery" — add .xlsx or .csv; the type can't be told from this Blob
download('a,b', 'sales.xlsx');           // ✗ "sales.xlsx" — text can't be saved as .xlsx; use .csv
download(bytes, 'sales.xlsx');           // in Node or a worker:
                                         // ✗ download() needs a browser page (no document); write the bytes yourself
```

**8 · After an `await` in a click handler** works — tested in Chromium and WebKit:

```ts
button.addEventListener('click', async () => download(await toXlsx(book), 'sales.xlsx'));
```

**9 · With the grid,** `<sheetpane-excel>`'s Export button calls `download` for you.

**10 · Inside an iframe** the host must allow downloads, or the browser blocks
the save silently:

```html
<iframe src="app.html" sandbox="allow-scripts allow-downloads"></iframe>
```

The spec is the record [SR-EXPORT](../../records/0103_EXPORT.md).

**Using an AI coding agent?** `npx sheetpane-skills install` puts sheetpane's skills for Claude Code, Kiro and Codex into your repository.

<!-- source: packages/import/README.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/main/packages/import/README.md) -->

# @sheetpane/import

**An `.xlsx` or `.csv` in, a plain JavaScript workbook out** — the same
`Workbook` shape [`@sheetpane/export`](../export/README.md) writes, so a file
round-trips: `toXlsx(await read(file))`. No runtime dependency but
`@sheetpane/export`. `@sheetpane/grid` reads every file through it; a host can
use it on its own.

```ts
import { read } from '@sheetpane/import';

const book = await read(file);            // a File, Blob, ArrayBuffer or Uint8Array
book.sheets[0].rows;                      // raw values: [['Account ID', …], ['AC-10021', 1200, 268.4, …]]
book.sheets[0].text;                      // display text: [['Account ID', …], ['AC-10021', '1,200', '268.40', …]]
```

## What you get

| field | what it is |
|---|---|
| `rows` | the stored values — text, numbers, booleans, `null`. Export writes these back. A formula cell holds its **saved** value. |
| `text` | what a cell shows: numbers through a small number-format subset (dates, times, percent, fixed decimals, thousands); anything outside it shows the raw stored text |
| `merges`, `columnWidths`, `hidden` | as `@sheetpane/export` takes them |
| `formulas`, `styleIndex`, `freeze`, `hiddenRows`, `hiddenCols`, `rowHeights` | per sheet, for the grid and the plugins |
| `dataValidations`, `conditionalFormats`, `drawings`, `notes`, `threadedComments`, `pivotTables` | per sheet, parsed, for the plugins |
| `styles`, `themeColors`, `persons`, `definedNames`, `date1904` | per workbook |
| `part(path)` | any part of the package (a picture, a chart) without re-reading the ZIP |

## CSV

```ts
import { fromCsv } from '@sheetpane/import';
const book = await fromCsv(text, { name: 'sales.csv' });   // delimiter , ; or tab detected; book.delimiter says which
```

UTF-8 with or without a BOM; CRLF, LF or CR; RFC 4180 quotes. Every cell is
text, as stored. The one sheet is named after the file.

## What it refuses

Every refusal is an `ImportError` with a `code`:

| code | when |
|---|---|
| `unsupported-format` | any other extension — `.xls`, `.xlsm`, `.xlsb`, `.ods`, `.numbers`, `.tsv`…; a macro-enabled workbook renamed `.xlsx`; a ZIP named `.csv` |
| `password-or-legacy` | an OLE compound file: a password-protected `.xlsx` or a legacy `.xls` |
| `not-workbook` | a ZIP without `xl/workbook.xml`, or bytes named `.xlsx` that are not a ZIP |
| `too-large` | ZIP64; more than 512 MB inflated in one part or 1 GB in all; past 1,048,576 rows or 16,384 columns |
| `corrupt` | broken DEFLATE, a CRC mismatch, XML that does not parse |

The spec is the record [SR-IMPORT](../../records/0104_IMPORT.md).

**Using an AI coding agent?** `npx sheetpane-skills install` puts sheetpane's skills for Claude Code, Kiro and Codex into your repository.

<!-- source: packages/numfmt/README.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/main/packages/numfmt/README.md) -->

# @sheetpane/numfmt

**Excel number formats for sheetpane — currency, dates, fractions, elapsed time, conditional sections, locales — as a plugin on the `format` hook.**

A plugin: it registers against the one in-memory workbook of `@sheetpane/grid`
(`createWorkbook({ plugins: [...] })`, or `plugins="numfmt"` on the element), so
`<sheetpane-excel>` and `<sheetpane-errors>` both see its effect. Versioned in
lockstep with `@sheetpane/grid`. Without it, the grid shows the small number-format
subset it ships with; with it, every format Excel can store.

- `@sheetpane/numfmt` — the headless plugin. Safe to import in Node (no DOM at import).
- `@sheetpane/numfmt/ui` — the controls it adds to the grid's `format-row`: a number-format dropdown and ± decimals. Opt-in.

Engine: [`numfmt`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/numfmt) 4.0.1 (MIT, zero dependencies), pinned.

## Install

```bash
npm install @sheetpane/grid @sheetpane/numfmt
```

## Use

By attribute — importing the package registers it under the id `numfmt`:

```html
<script type="module">
  import '@sheetpane/grid';
  import '@sheetpane/numfmt/ui'; // the format plugin *and* its controls; import '@sheetpane/numfmt' for the format alone
</script>
<sheetpane-excel plugins="numfmt" mode="edit"></sheetpane-excel>
```

By code:

```ts
import { createWorkbook } from '@sheetpane/grid';
import { numfmt } from '@sheetpane/numfmt';
import { ui } from '@sheetpane/numfmt/ui';

const workbook = createWorkbook({ plugins: [numfmt(), ui()] });
element.workbook = workbook;               // the element and <sheetpane-errors> share it
await workbook.load(bytes, 'holdings.xlsx');
workbook.text('Holdings', 'G3');           // '$1,234.50 '
```

`numfmt({ locale })` pins a locale; `ui({ locale, ask })` does the same for the controls and lets a host replace the
`window.prompt` that "Custom…" uses (return the code, or `null` to cancel).

## What it does

- **Display.** Every numeric cell's text comes from the library for every built-in id (0–49) and every custom code in the
  file's `<numFmts>`. `General` follows Excel's rule (11 characters, then scientific). A cell with no `s` uses xf 0.
- **1904.** `<workbookPr date1904>` is honoured: the library has no 1904 mode, so a date format's serial is shifted by 1,462
  days first. Elapsed-time formats (`[h]:mm`) are not dates and are not shifted.
- **Dates out of range** show `########`, as Excel does, not the bare number.
- **Fallback.** If the library rejects a code, the plugin says nothing and the core subset shows its text for that cell.
  `plugin.fallbacks()` lists those cells (`['Sheet1!B4']`).
- **Padding.** Accounting and `?` formats pad with spaces; the plugin also provides `decorate` with `white-space: pre` on
  those cells so HTML does not collapse them. It sets no font (SR-LAW-5).
- **Edits.** A format chosen in the UI is a change of kind `numFmt` (key `sheet!ref`, `now` = the code, `was` = the
  file's code). Choosing the file's own code again removes the change. Undo and redo work.
- **Export.** `exportPatch` appends the new `<numFmt>` entries and `<xf>` rows to `xl/styles.xml` — deduplicated, the base
  xf's font, fill, border and alignment kept — and repoints each changed cell's `s`. An en-US built-in code is written as its id.
  Cells nobody touched keep their `s`. A CSV has no styles; its export carries values only.

## The controls

`format-row`, Edit mode only:

- **Dropdown** — General · Number · Currency · Accounting · Date · Time · Percentage · Fraction · Scientific · Text · Custom…
  Number is `0.00`, Percentage `0.00%`, Fraction `# ?/?`, Scientific `0.00E+00`; Currency, Accounting, Date and Time are the
  locale's (`$#,##0.00_);($#,##0.00)` in English, `#,##0.00 €;-#,##0.00 €` in German).
- **Decrease / Increase decimals** — one `0` fewer or more after the point in every section of the code; on `General` it
  starts from the decimals the value shows. Dates, times, fractions and text are left alone.

A selection range applies to every **numeric** cell in it, within the sheet's data. Blank and text cells are skipped. So are
cells with a pending **value** edit: the grid keeps one change per cell, and a format would replace the edit. At most 10,000
cells are changed in one go (each is one change and one undo step) — the plugin warns when it stops.

The cell bar keeps showing the raw value (`1234.5`) while the cell shows the formatted text.

## Locales

The locale is `numfmt({ locale })`, else the page's `<html lang>`, read when a cell is formatted (a cell's text is cached
until it changes, so set `lang` before loading). An unknown tag means English. Tags may be written `de-DE` or `de_DE`.

- `de-DE`: `1.234.567,89`, `15 März 2023`, `12,3%`, `General` 1234,5; built-in ids 14–22 and 5–8, 41–44 become the locale's
  (id 14 → `15.03.2023`), as they do in Excel.
- `en-IN`: Indian grouping, `12,34,567.89` (any `-IN` territory).
- The library's other locales (about 70) are available by tag.

Note: a format that names its own locale, `[$€-407]#,##0.00`, is formatted with that locale's separators by the library
(`€1.234,50`). Excel may keep the reader's; this is unverified (see the record).

## Tests

`pnpm exec vitest run --project numfmt` — a real browser. The fixture table (`test/fixtures/table.ts`) holds the expected text
for every built-in id and 50 custom codes. **It was written from Excel's documented behaviour, not captured from Excel** —
there is no Excel on the build machine; regenerating the `expected` column with `TEXT()` is owed.

Spec: [`work/open/W-15-numfmt.md`](../../work/open/W-15-numfmt.md).
How plugins plug in: [`work/compare/plugins.compare.md`](../../work/compare/plugins.compare.md).

**Using an AI coding agent?** `npx sheetpane-skills install` puts sheetpane's skills for Claude Code, Kiro and Codex into your repository.

<!-- source: packages/formulas/README.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/main/packages/formulas/README.md) -->

# @sheetpane/formulas

**Formula recalculation for sheetpane — edit a cell and every dependent formula updates — as a plugin on the `derive` hook, backed by IronCalc (WASM, lazy-loaded).**

A plugin: it registers against the one in-memory workbook of `@sheetpane/grid`
(`createWorkbook({ plugins: [...] })`, or `plugins="formulas"` on the element), so
`<sheetpane-excel>` and `<sheetpane-errors>` both see its effect. Versioned in
lockstep with `@sheetpane/grid`.

- `@sheetpane/formulas` — the headless plugin (`derive`, `exportPatch`).
- `@sheetpane/formulas/ui` — the controls it adds to the grid's slots; opt-in.

```js
import '@sheetpane/grid';
import '@sheetpane/formulas/ui'; // registers "formulas" with its controls
// <sheetpane-excel plugins="formulas" src="book.xlsx"></sheetpane-excel>

// or, headless / your own store:
import { createWorkbook } from '@sheetpane/grid';
import { formulas } from '@sheetpane/formulas';
const store = createWorkbook({ plugins: [formulas({ preload: true })] });
```

## What it does

- **Live recalculation.** Edit B3 and every formula that reads it — on any
  sheet, through defined names — gets its new value. Recalculated cells are
  *derived*: drawn with a mark, never in the change map or the change count.
- **Typed formulas.** With the plugin installed, a value typed starting `=` is a
  change of kind `formula` (SR-GRID 21b); it evaluates, and export writes it as
  a real formula.
- **Errors as Excel shows them.** `#DIV/0!`, `#REF!`, `#N/A`, `#VALUE!` are
  values, never exceptions. A circular reference shows `0`, as Excel does, and
  is listed by `cycles()` (the UI names it in the status line).
- **Honest about gaps.** A formula from the file that IronCalc cannot calculate
  (`#NAME?` for a function it lacks, a parse error, `#SPILL!` over a legacy
  array formula) keeps the value Excel saved and is listed by `unsupported()`
  (the UI marks it `≈`); Excel recalculates it on open.
- **Export.** `exportPatch` writes `<f>` and a cached `<v>` for each typed
  formula, a new `<v>` for each recalculated formula cell (its `<f>` — shared
  or not — is kept as written), and keeps `fullCalcOnLoad="1"` so Excel
  re-verifies every value.

## The engine is a cache (SR-LAW-9)

The JavaScript workbook is the only source of truth. The IronCalc model is built
from it — the file's values and formulas overlaid with the user's changes — and
rebuilt whenever the workbook object changes. On a change the plugin reads the
cell's state from the store and writes it into the model; it never reads state
back out of the model, only computed values.

Only what formulas can reach goes into the model: every formula cell, plus the
cells its references (and the defined names') cover. A formula with `INDIRECT`
or `OFFSET` can reach anywhere, so then every cell goes in. A new formula over
cells not yet in the model feeds them on demand.

## Loading: nothing until a formula needs it

`@ironcalc/wasm` 0.9.0 (MIT / Apache-2.0) is a 2 MB `.wasm`. It is reached only
by a dynamic `import()` on the first `derive` that has a formula to calculate:

- importing the package (in Node too) touches no `WebAssembly`;
- a workbook with no formulas never loads it — until a formula is typed;
- `formulas({ preload: true })` warms it when the plugin is created;
- `formulas({ wasm })` says where the `.wasm` is (a URL, a `Response`, the bytes
  or a compiled module) — for a CDN, a strict CSP, or Node. By default the
  bundler emits it beside `@ironcalc/wasm`'s `wasm.js` (`new URL(…, import.meta.url)`;
  Vite, webpack 5, Rollup and esbuild handle it).

## The plugin's own API

| member | what |
|---|---|
| `ready()` | resolves when every queued recalculation is done and merged |
| `cycles()` | formula cells in a circular reference |
| `unsupported()` | file formula cells IronCalc cannot calculate (saved value kept) |
| `stateOf(sheet, ref)` | `'cycle'`, `'unsupported'` or `undefined` |
| `built()` | whether a model exists for the current workbook |

## The UI (`@sheetpane/formulas/ui`)

| slot | control |
|---|---|
| `cellbar` | View: `fx =B3*C3`, the selected cell's formula as read-only text. Edit: the grid's own cell input holds the formula, editable (retyping the file's formula restores the cell) |
| `status` | `Sum · Avg · Count` of the selection (formatted as the active cell); `⟳ N cells recalculated` (Edit); `Circular reference: B2` |
| `cell` | `⟳` recalculated · `↻` in a cycle · `≈` not calculable |
| `overlay` | in Edit, the ranges the selected formula reads, outlined and labelled in colour (`--sp-ref-1` … `--sp-ref-6`), following the formula as it is typed |

No font family is named anywhere (SR-LAW-5).

## Known limits (IronCalc 0.9.0)

- Values are read back at 15 significant digits (IronCalc has no raw-value
  getter); comparisons with Excel's 17-digit cache use a 1e-14 relative tolerance.
- The function probe in `test/parity.test.ts` lists where IronCalc disagrees
  with Excel: `AGGREGATE` (missing), `XLOOKUP` over array constants, and
  `TEXTJOIN` ignoring an empty *literal*.
- 1904-date workbooks: date functions over serial numbers are off by 1,462 days
  (IronCalc knows only the 1900 system).
- A half-typed formula evaluates to IronCalc's `#ERROR!`; Excel would refuse it.
- Typed formulas are exported as typed: a newer function needs Excel's `_xlfn.`
  prefix, which is not added.

Spec: [`work/open/W-16-formulas.md`](../../work/open/W-16-formulas.md).
How plugins plug in: [`work/compare/plugins.compare.md`](../../work/compare/plugins.compare.md).

**Using an AI coding agent?** `npx sheetpane-skills install` puts sheetpane's skills for Claude Code, Kiro and Codex into your repository.

<!-- source: packages/styles/README.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/main/packages/styles/README.md) -->

# @sheetpane/styles

**Cell styles for sheetpane — fill, bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, colour, size, borders, alignment, wrap — as a plugin on the `decorate` hook. Never a font family (SR-LAW-5): the host's font is the font.**

A plugin: it registers against the one in-memory workbook of `@sheetpane/grid`,
so `<sheetpane-excel>` and `<sheetpane-errors>` both see its effect. Versioned in
lockstep with `@sheetpane/grid` (a peer). No runtime dependencies.

| entry | what it gives |
|---|---|
| `@sheetpane/styles` | `styles()` — the headless plugin: `decorate` draws each cell as the workbook formats it, plus the reviewer's changes; `exportPatch` writes those changes into the file |
| `@sheetpane/styles/ui` | `ui()` — the format row and selection-bar controls; opt-in, Edit mode only |

```js
import { createWorkbook } from '@sheetpane/grid';
import { styles } from '@sheetpane/styles';
import { ui } from '@sheetpane/styles/ui';

el.workbook = createWorkbook({ plugins: [styles(), ui()] });
```

Or by attribute: `import '@sheetpane/styles/ui'` (it registers `styles` with its
controls; `import '@sheetpane/styles'` alone registers the headless plugin), then
`<sheetpane-excel plugins="styles">`.

## What a cell shows

`decorate(cell)` reads `cellXfs[s]` → `fonts`, `fills`, `borders`, `alignment`
and returns only these CSS properties:
`background-color`, `color`, `font-weight`, `font-style`, `font-size`,
`text-decoration`, `text-align`, `vertical-align`, `white-space`,
`border-top` / `-right` / `-bottom` / `-left`. Nothing else, ever.

- **Colours:** `rgb` (ARGB), theme colours with Excel's tint, indexed colours
  (the default 64-colour palette, or the file's `<indexedColors>`), `auto`.
- **The default font's size and colour are the host's**: only a size or colour
  that differs from the workbook's default font is drawn, so a plain cell stays
  plain (and dark themes keep their ink). Size scales the grid's own size by
  `sz / default`.
- A filled cell with automatic text is drawn in the workbook's default ink.
- Patterns blend by density; a gradient shows its midpoint; diagonal borders,
  indent and rotation are not drawn.

`styles({ fileStyles: false })` draws only the reviewer's own changes.

## The format row (`ui()`)

Groups, in order: **text** (Bold `Mod+B`, Italic `Mod+I`, Underline `Mod+U`,
Strikethrough `Mod+5`) · **colour** · **fill** · **border** (all, outside, one
side, thick or double bottom, none) · **align** (left `Mod+Shift+L`, centre
`Mod+Shift+E`, right `Mod+Shift+R`; top, middle, bottom; Merge / Unmerge) ·
**wrap** · **clear** (`Mod+\`). The selection bar adds Bold, Fill and
Merge / Unmerge. Every control restyles the whole selection as **one** undo step.
Merges are core: the merge control only calls `store.setMerge()`.

`ui({ colours, fills, highlight })` picks the swatch sets (`{ value: 'RRGGBB', label }`).
The default fills each keep the grid's changed-corner mark at 3:1 contrast.

## The change it makes

A change of kind `style` at the key `sheet!#style:A1` (not `sheet!A1`, which a
value change owns). Its `now` is a plain object, `StylePatch`:

```ts
{ clear?: true; b?: boolean; i?: boolean; u?: boolean; strike?: boolean;
  color?: 'RRGGBB' | null; fill?: 'RRGGBB' | null;
  border?: { top?, right?, bottom?, left?: { style, color? } | null };
  align?: 'left' | 'center' | 'right' | null; valign?: 'top' | 'middle' | 'bottom' | null;
  wrap?: boolean }
```

Fields the file already shows are dropped; a cell back to its file look has no
change. `clear` drops the file's font, fill, border and alignment; the number
format stays.

## Export

`exportPatch` appends deduplicated `<font>`, `<fill>`, `<border>` and `<xf>`
entries to `xl/styles.xml` (counts updated, every existing entry and every other
byte kept) and repoints `s` on each style-changed cell — adding `<c r s/>` where
the cell had no element. Untouched cells keep their `s`. A CSV carries no
styles, so a CSV is never restyled.

## For `@sheetpane/condfmt`

Exported for reuse: `resolveColor`, `applyTint`, `paletteOf`, `DEFAULT_THEME`,
`DEFAULT_INDEXED`, `ALLOWED_PROPS`, `allowListed`, `fontCss`, `fillCss`
(`{ dxf: true }` reads a dxf's solid `bgColor`), `borderCss`, `alignmentCss`,
`dxfCss`.

Spec: [`work/open/W-17-styles.md`](../../work/open/W-17-styles.md).
How plugins plug in: [`work/compare/plugins.compare.md`](../../work/compare/plugins.compare.md).

**Using an AI coding agent?** `npx sheetpane-skills install` puts sheetpane's skills for Claude Code, Kiro and Codex into your repository.

<!-- source: packages/validation/README.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/main/packages/validation/README.md) -->

# @sheetpane/validation

**The workbook's own data-validation rules, checked when the file loads and after every edit. Each cell that breaks a rule shows up as a warning in `<sheetpane-errors>`.**

A plugin for `@sheetpane/grid`. It reads the `<dataValidations>` the file's
author saved, including the x14 form Excel uses for lists on another sheet,
and runs them through the `validate` hook. `<sheetpane-excel>` and
`<sheetpane-errors>` on the same pane both see the result. No runtime
dependencies; `@sheetpane/grid` is a peer. Versioned in lockstep with it.

- `@sheetpane/validation`: the headless plugin (`validate` only).
- `@sheetpane/validation/ui`: opt-in. Adds the list arrow and the status-line count.

## Use

```html
<script type="module">
  import '@sheetpane/grid';
  import '@sheetpane/validation/ui'; // registers "validation" = rules + controls
</script>

<sheetpane-excel pane="q3" plugins="validation" src="/files/holdings.xlsx" mode="edit"></sheetpane-excel>
<sheetpane-errors pane="q3"></sheetpane-errors>
```

Without a page, or without the controls:

```ts
import { createWorkbook } from '@sheetpane/grid';
import { validation, skippedRules } from '@sheetpane/validation';

const store = createWorkbook({ plugins: [validation({ severity: 'warning' })] });
await store.load(bytes, 'holdings.xlsx');
store.getErrors();      // one error per failing cell
skippedRules(store);    // { rules, checked, skipped: [{ sheet, sqref, type, reason, detail }] }
```

Importing `@sheetpane/validation` registers `validation` as the rules plugin
alone. Importing `/ui` re-registers it as the rules plus the controls.

## What a broken rule looks like

One error per failing cell. If a cell breaks two rules, the first one counts.

| field | value |
|---|---|
| `type` | `validation` |
| `severity` | `warning` (set another with `validation({ severity })`) |
| `author` | `workbook` |
| `range` | the cell, e.g. `B4` |
| `found` | the cell's current display text, or `(blank)` |
| `expected` | the rule in words (table below) |
| `message` | the rule's own `errorTitle: error`, or either one alone; otherwise the rule in words |

A workbook error resolves itself when its cell passes again and reopens if
the cell fails again (it keeps the same id). This is the only automatic
resolve in sheetpane; the store does it. `showErrorMessage="0"` rules are
still checked, because that flag only turns off Excel's popup.

## The rules, and the words a reviewer reads

| rule | passes when | `expected` |
|---|---|---|
| `whole` | the value is an integer and the operator holds | `whole number > 0` |
| `decimal` | the value is a number and the operator holds | `decimal between 0.00% and 2.00%` (operands in the cell's own number format) |
| `date` | the value is a date serial and the operator holds | `date between 01-Jul-2026 and 30-Sep-2026` |
| `time` | the value is a number (a fraction of a day) and the operator holds | `time between 09:00 and 18:00` |
| `textLength` | the length of the text holds against the operator | `text length ≤ 5 characters` |
| `list` | the text matches a choice (case-insensitive; a number also matches its number) | `list — Core, Income, Cap` (the first 8, then `… (n more)`) |
| `custom` | the formula is true at the cell | `custom — =A1>0` |

Operators: `between` (the default), `notBetween`, `equal` (`=`), `notEqual`
(`≠`), `greaterThan` (`>`), `lessThan` (`<`), `greaterThanOrEqual` (`≥`),
`lessThanOrEqual` (`≤`). `between` includes both ends.

What an operand can be:

- a number
- `DATE(y,m,d)` or `TIME(h,m,s)` with number arguments
- a quoted string
- a cell: `$G$1`, `Sheet2!B1`, or a relative `D1`, which shifts with each cell the same way it does in Excel
- a defined name that resolves to one of these

A cell operand is read live, so changing the limit re-checks the rule. An
empty operand cell reads as 0.

A `list` source can be:

- a literal list: `"a,b,c"`
- a range: `$H$1:$H$9`, `Lists!$A$1:$A$9`, `$A:$A`
- a defined name that resolves to a range

A range source is read live from the store, and the arrow's menu re-reads it
each time it opens.

Blank cells pass when the rule has `allowBlank`. Without it, they fail.
Cells are checked only inside the sheet's used range: its data plus any cell
the user changed. A rule on `B:B` therefore does not produce a million rows.

## What is not checked, and why (`skippedRules`)

| reason | what |
|---|---|
| `custom` | a `custom` rule when no formula plugin offers `evaluate()` (see below) |
| `operand` | an operand the subset above does not cover, e.g. `SUM(...)` or `INDIRECT(...)` |
| `operator` | an operator outside the eight above |
| `type` | an unknown rule type |
| `source` | a list source that is neither a list, a range nor a name, or that names a missing sheet |

`skippedRules(store)` counts `custom` as checked when the pane has a formula
evaluator. `skippedRules(book)` has only the workbook to go on, so it counts
every `custom` rule as skipped. The status line adds `· n rules not checked`.

### Custom rules need a formula engine

`custom` rules run only when the pane's `derive` plugin (`@sheetpane/formulas`)
also exposes:

```ts
evaluate(formula: string, at: { sheet: string; ref: string }): boolean | number | string | null | undefined
```

The plugin passes the formula with its relative references already shifted to
the cell. `true` or a non-zero number passes. `false` or `0` fails. Anything
else counts as unknown, and the cell is not flagged.

## The controls (`/ui`)

- **List arrow** (`cell` slot, Edit only): appears in every cell a `list` rule
  covers. It opens the rule's current choices, and picking one sets the cell
  with `store.setCell`, which can be undone.
- **Status** (`status` slot, View and Edit): `3 validation warnings`, plus
  `· 1 rule not checked` when rules were skipped.

`<sheetpane-errors>` lists the rule rows with the reviewer's own errors. Its
author filter (Anyone · People · Workbook rules · File comments) shows only
the rule rows when you need them.

## Known limits

- A list whose source is on another sheet is re-checked when its own sheet
  changes, not when the source sheet changes. The arrow's menu is always
  current.
- A cell holding a formula is checked against its saved value. If the user
  typed the formula, the plugin uses the value the formula plugin derived. The
  check runs on the edit, before the formula plugin has finished deriving.
- `found` is fixed when the error is first made. If an error reopens, it shows
  the first failing value.

**Using an AI coding agent?** `npx sheetpane-skills install` puts sheetpane's skills for Claude Code, Kiro and Codex into your repository.

<!-- source: packages/condfmt/README.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/main/packages/condfmt/README.md) -->

# @sheetpane/condfmt

**Conditional formatting for sheetpane — the file's own `<conditionalFormatting>` rules drawn as Excel draws them: value and text rules, duplicates, top / bottom, averages, colour scales, data bars and formula rules — as a plugin on the `decorate` hook, after `@sheetpane/styles`. Render only: nothing here writes a rule.**

A plugin: it registers against the one in-memory workbook of `@sheetpane/grid`,
so `<sheetpane-excel>` and `<sheetpane-errors>` both see its effect. Versioned in
lockstep with `@sheetpane/grid` and `@sheetpane/styles` (peers). No runtime
dependencies.

| entry | what it gives |
|---|---|
| `@sheetpane/condfmt` | `condfmt()` — the headless plugin: `decorate`, ordered after `styles`, draws each cell the rules hold for |
| `@sheetpane/condfmt/ui` | `ui()` — the legend and the count: the rule named on hover and in the cell bar, the rules counted in the status line |

```js
import { createWorkbook } from '@sheetpane/grid';
import { styles } from '@sheetpane/styles';
import { condfmt } from '@sheetpane/condfmt';
import { ui } from '@sheetpane/condfmt/ui';

el.workbook = createWorkbook({ plugins: [styles(), condfmt(), ui()] });
```

Or by attribute: `import '@sheetpane/condfmt/ui'` (it registers `condfmt` with
its UI; `import '@sheetpane/condfmt'` alone registers the headless plugin), then
`<sheetpane-excel plugins="styles condfmt">`.

## The rules it draws

| type | holds when |
|---|---|
| `cellIs` | the value compares to its operand(s) — `equal`, `notEqual`, `greaterThan`, `lessThan`, `greaterThanOrEqual`, `lessThanOrEqual`, `between`, `notBetween` (bounds in either order) |
| `containsText` · `notContainsText` · `beginsWith` · `endsWith` | the value as text, without case |
| `containsBlanks` · `notContainsBlanks` · `containsErrors` · `notContainsErrors` | the value is blank (or only spaces) / an error |
| `duplicateValues` · `uniqueValues` | the value appears more than once / once in the rule's range (text without case; blanks never count) |
| `top10` | in the top or bottom *n* (or *n* %) numbers of the range, ties included |
| `aboveAverage` | above (or, with `aboveAverage="0"`, below) the range's average |
| `colorScale` | 2 or 3 colours, interpolated in sRGB between thresholds |
| `dataBar` | a bar sized to the value |
| `expression` | its formula is TRUE or non-zero — with a formula engine only (below) |

Comparisons follow Excel: numbers < text < logicals, text without case, a blank
reads as 0 or empty text. Operands are numbers, `"text"`, `TRUE` / `FALSE`, or a
cell — absolute parts stay, relative parts shift with the cell from the
range's top-left. Any other operand is a formula, read through the engine.

**Priority** is one order per sheet, across every `<conditionalFormatting>`
block. A higher-priority rule wins each property it sets; a lower one fills in
the rest; a matching rule with `stopIfTrue` ends the walk. A rule with several
`sqref` areas is one range.

## What a cell shows

A rule's `dxf` goes through `@sheetpane/styles`' `dxfCss` and its allow-list:
`background-color`, `color`, `font-weight`, `font-style`, `font-size`,
`text-decoration`, the four borders. Because `condfmt` runs **after** `styles`,
the rule wins per property and the static style keeps the rest — a bold cell
with a yellow fill and a rule's red fill is bold and red.

- **Colour scale:** `background-color`. Thresholds: `min`, `max`, `num`,
  `percent` (of the range from min to max), `percentile` (`PERCENTILE.INC`),
  `formula`. Values beyond the end thresholds take the end colours; text and
  blanks take none.
- **Data bar:** `background-image`, a gradient from the bar's colour to a
  lighter tint, `minLength` (default 10 %) … `maxLength` (default 90 %) of the
  cell, linear between the low and high thresholds.
- A rule's fill with no text colour of its own takes the cell's static colour,
  else the workbook's default ink: the file's colours are data, drawn as saved
  in both themes.
- **Edit marks stay on top:** an error's ring is an inset shadow and its tint a
  `::before` overlay above the fill, so a flagged cell keeps its rule's fill.

Statistics a range rule needs (sorted numbers, sum, duplicate counts) are
computed once per range and kept; per-cell results are kept too. A change drops
only what depends on it: the changed cell, every cell of a range whose
statistics hold it, and — for rules that read other cells (a formula, a cell
operand) — their results. `evaluations(store)` counts both, for profiling.

## Formula rules

An `expression` rule — or a `cellIs` operand or a threshold that is a formula —
is read through the `derive` provider's synchronous `evaluate(formula, { sheet,
ref })`, which `@sheetpane/formulas` offers. Without one, the rule is **skipped
and counted**, never guessed. So are icon sets (`iconSet`, out of v1),
`timePeriod` and any other type outside the table above.

`skippedRules(storeOrWorkbook)` → `{ rules, shown, skipped: [{ sheet, sqref,
type, priority, reason, detail }] }`, `reason` one of `iconSet`, `formula`,
`type`, `malformed`.

## The legend and the count (`ui()`)

- **Hover:** a rule-coloured cell shows *Conditional: greater than 1000* and its
  range in a tooltip under the cell (an overlay that lets pointer events through
  to the cells).
- **Cell bar:** the selected cell's rules, in the same words — the legend a
  keyboard or a screen reader reaches.
- **Status:** *4 conditional rules from the file · 1 not shown*.

Colour never carries meaning alone.

## Also exported

`rulesOf(book, sheet)` (compiled, priority order), `ruleWords(rule, row, col)`,
`cellResult(store, sheet, row, col)`, `legendAt(store, sheet, row, col)`,
`shiftFormula`, `parseOperand`, `compareCells`, `percentile`, `scaleColor`,
`lerpColor`, `barLength`, `barImage`, `dxfStyle`.

Spec: [`work/open/W-19-condfmt.md`](../../work/open/W-19-condfmt.md).
How plugins plug in: [`work/compare/plugins.compare.md`](../../work/compare/plugins.compare.md).

**Using an AI coding agent?** `npx sheetpane-skills install` puts sheetpane's skills for Claude Code, Kiro and Codex into your repository.

<!-- source: packages/images/README.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/main/packages/images/README.md) -->

# @sheetpane/images

**Images for sheetpane — pictures anchored in the sheet drawn in sheet space through the `overlay` hook; view only, kept on export.**

A plugin: it registers against the one in-memory workbook of `@sheetpane/grid`
(`createWorkbook({ plugins: [...] })`, or `plugins="images"` on the element), so
`<sheetpane-excel>` and `<sheetpane-errors>` both see its effect. Versioned in
lockstep with `@sheetpane/grid`.

```ts
import { createWorkbook } from '@sheetpane/grid';
import { images } from '@sheetpane/images';

el.workbook = createWorkbook({ plugins: [images()] });
// or: import '@sheetpane/images'  and  <sheetpane-excel plugins="images">
```

No runtime dependencies. Importing is safe in Node (no DOM until a picture renders).

## What it draws

Every `picture` in a sheet's drawing part, at its anchor, in the overlay layer: it scrolls,
zooms and clips with its cells, under the pins and above the cells. `alt` is the picture's
description (`descr`), else its name.

| format | shown as |
|---|---|
| PNG, JPEG, GIF, BMP, WebP | an `<img>` over an object URL |
| SVG | an `<img>` too — never inline markup, so no script in the file can run |
| EMF, WMF, TIFF, anything else | a dashed frame the size of the anchor: `logo.emf — preview unavailable` |

The format is told from the bytes' header first and the file name second.

Charts and shapes are not pictures and are skipped (the charts plugin draws charts). The status
bar adds `2 pictures · 1 preview unavailable` for the sheet in view.

**View only.** In Edit a click on a picture selects the cell under the click, so that cell can
still be flagged; pictures cannot be moved, resized, added or deleted.

## Anchors (`src/anchors.ts`, exported)

EMU become pixels at 9,525 EMU per pixel (914,400 per inch, 96 px per inch), then are placed in
the grid's own geometry (`Geometry` — pixels at 100 % zoom from A1's top-left):

| anchor | rectangle |
|---|---|
| `twoCell` | `from` to `to`, each corner plus its offset |
| `oneCell` | `from` plus its offset, sized by `ext` |
| `absolute` | `pos` from the sheet origin, sized by `ext` |

An offset never reaches past its own cell, as in Excel. `anchorRect(anchor, geometry)`,
`pointToPx`, `cellAt`, `emuToPx` and `refOf` are plain functions with no DOM, so
`@sheetpane/charts` reuses them as they are.

**Excel's own row heights and hidden rows or columns are not used.** The grid draws every row at
its fixed height and shows what is stored, hidden or not; a picture anchored C4:F9 covers C4:F9
on screen, whatever size those cells are in Excel. A `oneCell` or `absolute` picture keeps its
`ext` in pixels, so beside tall Excel rows it can look smaller than it did there.

## Memory

Nothing is read from the file's media until a picture comes near the screen (a 20 MB photo costs
nothing until scrolled to). One object URL is made per media part however many pictures show it,
and all are revoked when the pane loads another workbook (or a load fails). A decode that
finishes after the workbook went makes no URL.

## Export

Patch-mode export leaves the drawing and media parts as they were (the fidelity ruling), so a
workbook's pictures survive a round trip. **A deleted row does not re-anchor pictures in v1**:
the file keeps the anchors it had.

## Tests

`pnpm exec vitest run --project images` — anchor arithmetic against geometry, rectangles against
the rendered cells (oneCell, twoCell, absolute, zoom), every format, laziness, object-URL
revocation. Fixtures are hand-written packages and the ExcelJS 2×2 PNG; files saved by Excel and
LibreOffice are owed by W-30.

**Using an AI coding agent?** `npx sheetpane-skills install` puts sheetpane's skills for Claude Code, Kiro and Codex into your repository.

<!-- source: packages/charts/README.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/main/packages/charts/README.md) -->

# @sheetpane/charts

**Charts for sheetpane — each chart in a workbook shown at its anchor: a frame with its title, type, series count and Show source cells (stage 1), drawn as our own SVG for bar, column, line, pie and scatter (stage 2) — through the `overlay` hook.**

A plugin: it registers against the one in-memory workbook of `@sheetpane/grid`
(`createWorkbook({ plugins: [...] })`, or `plugins="charts"` on the element), so
`<sheetpane-excel>` and `<sheetpane-errors>` both see its effect. Versioned in
lockstep with `@sheetpane/grid`.

```ts
import { createWorkbook } from '@sheetpane/grid';
import { charts } from '@sheetpane/charts';
import { ui } from '@sheetpane/charts/ui';

el.workbook = createWorkbook({ plugins: [charts(), ui()] });
// stage 1 only (frames, no plot):  charts({ draw: false })
// or: import '@sheetpane/charts/ui'  and  <sheetpane-excel plugins="charts">
```

- `@sheetpane/charts` — the headless plugin: the `overlay` provider.
- `@sheetpane/charts/ui` — the status line and a keyboard shortcut; opt-in.

No runtime dependencies, no chart library. Importing is safe in Node: nothing touches the DOM
until a chart renders.

## The frame (stage 1)

Every `graphicFrame` in a sheet's drawing that holds a chart (`c:chart r:id` → the chart part)
becomes one overlay item at its anchor, scrolling and zooming with its cells. The frame shows:

- the **title** — `c:title` rich text (runs joined, paragraphs joined by a space), a title
  reference's cached text, the only series' name when the title has no text, else `Chart`;
- the **type and series count** — `column · 2 series`, `stacked bar · 3 series`,
  `100% stacked column`, `line`, `pie`, `doughnut`, `scatter`, `area`, `radar`, `3-D column`,
  `column + line` (a combination) …;
- **Show source cells** — selects the plotted cells (see below), in View and in Edit;
- **data changed — Excel will redraw**, once a user change (`value` or `formula`) lands in a
  cell the chart reads — a series' values, categories or name. Undo takes it away again.

A chart that is not drawn lists `Not drawn here: area chart.` and, per series, the cells it
reads: `Sales — Data!A2:A5, Data!B2:B5`.

**Show source cells** selects the union of the series' `c:f` ranges when they tile one
rectangle (categories in A, values in B and C → `A2:C5`). The grid's selection is one
rectangle, so ranges that do not tile one (categories in E, values in H) select the first
series' values. A chart whose data is literal (`c:numLit`, no `c:f`) has nothing to select and
its button is disabled.

In Edit, a click on the chart away from its button selects the cell under the click, so that
cell can be flagged — as pictures do.

## The drawing (stage 2)

| type | drawn |
|---|---|
| `c:barChart`, `c:barDir="col"` | column — clustered, stacked or 100 % stacked |
| `c:barChart`, `c:barDir="bar"` | bar — the same groupings; the first category at the bottom, as in Excel |
| `c:lineChart` | line — standard, stacked or 100 % stacked; a missing point breaks the line |
| `c:pieChart`, `c:doughnutChart` | pie and doughnut — the first series, clockwise from `c:firstSliceAng` (12 o'clock) |
| `c:scatterChart` | scatter — x from `c:xVal` (text x values plot at 1, 2, 3 … as in Excel); lines when the style and the series' line say so |

Everything else — area, radar, stock, surface, bubble, 3-D, pie-of-pie, combination charts and
pivot charts — stays a stage-1 frame.

The SVG has a title band, a value axis with "nice" ticks (1, 2, 2.5 or 5 × 10ⁿ; zero included
unless the data sit in a narrow band far from it, as Excel does), category labels thinned so
they do not overlap, and a legend where the chart has one (`c:legend`: right, or bottom when
`legendPos` is top or bottom, or the chart is narrow). A negative bar is drawn in the error red
(the design board). Percent axes follow a `%` in the value axis' number format.

**Colours** come from the series' explicit fill (`c:spPr/a:solidFill` — `a:srgbClr`,
`a:schemeClr` through the workbook theme, `a:sysClr`, with `lumMod`, `lumOff`, `tint`,
`shade`), a line chart's line colour, per-point fills (`c:dPt`), else Excel's default style:
the theme's accents 1–6 by series index (`c:idx`) — or by point for `varyColors` pies — then
darker and lighter rounds. A workbook without a theme gets Office's accents.

**Values** are the series' cached points (`c:numCache`, `c:strCache`): what Excel drew when the
file was saved. With a `derive` plugin on the pane (`@sheetpane/formulas`), the chart reads the
live cells instead (`store.value`, `store.text` for labels) and redraws as they change; the SVG
carries `data-values="live"` or `"cache"`. Without one, an edit leaves the drawing as Excel
saved it, and the tag says so.

The SVG uses a `viewBox` the size of the anchor at 100 % and fills the item, so it scales with
zoom exactly as the cells do. Every mark carries what it stands for (`data-series`,
`data-point`, `data-value`; slices `data-start`/`data-end` in degrees), so tests compare the
drawing with the values rather than with pixels. No font is named anywhere (SR-LAW-5): the text
is the host's. Text from the file is escaped; colours from the file are validated `#RRGGBB`.

## Names

The item is `role="img"`; its `aria-label` is the chart's title once the part is read (the
drawing's description or name before that), and the SVG carries the same `role`, `aria-label`
and `<title>`.

## `@sheetpane/charts/ui`

- **Status line:** `Chart source: Data!A2:A5, Data!B2:B5, Data!C2:C5` while the selection lies in
  a chart's plotted cells or under its frame; otherwise `2 charts` on a sheet that has some.
- **Mod+Shift+U** shows the source of the chart over the active cell, or of the sheet's only
  chart — listed in the grid's keyboard help. The frame's own button sits inside the grid's
  `role="img"` overlay wrapper, where assistive technology does not reach it; the shortcut is the
  accessible route to the same action.

There is no `selbar` button: a selbar control has no "applies here" test, so it would show on
every selection, chart or not.

## Export

Nothing. Patch-mode export copies the chart parts byte for byte, so Excel redraws each chart
from the (possibly changed) cells when the file is opened.

## Limits

- **Placement uses the grid's geometry** (28 px rows, every row and column shown), as pictures
  do — not Excel's row heights. Past the last column the grid draws, columns count 64 px each.
- One rectangle per selection (above). Data labels, trendlines, error bars, axis titles,
  secondary axes, log scales and date axes are not drawn.
- Only charts on worksheets; chartsheets hold no cells and are not read.
- No chart is ever edited: no type switcher, no series editor, no resize.

## Dependencies

Anchors are placed with `@sheetpane/images`' `anchorRect` and `cellAt` (SR-IMAGES decision 3); `@sheetpane/images` is a peer.

Spec: [`work/open/W-21-charts.md`](../../work/open/W-21-charts.md).
How plugins plug in: [`work/compare/plugins.compare.md`](../../work/compare/plugins.compare.md).

**Using an AI coding agent?** `npx sheetpane-skills install` puts sheetpane's skills for Claude Code, Kiro and Codex into your repository.

<!-- source: packages/comments/README.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/main/packages/comments/README.md) -->

# @sheetpane/comments

**Excel's comments and sheetpane's errors, in both directions. When a file loads, its notes and threaded comments show up in `<sheetpane-errors>`. When you export, every error in the review goes into the file as an Excel threaded comment on its cell.**

A plugin for `@sheetpane/grid`. It works through the `validate` and
`exportPatch` hooks of the one in-memory workbook, so `<sheetpane-excel>` and
`<sheetpane-errors>` on the same pane both see it. No runtime dependencies;
`@sheetpane/grid` is a peer. Versioned in lockstep with it. There is no
`/ui` entry, because the plugin adds no controls.

## Use

```html
<script type="module">
  import '@sheetpane/grid';
  import '@sheetpane/comments'; // registers "comments"
</script>

<sheetpane-excel pane="q3" plugins="comments" src="/files/holdings.xlsx" mode="edit" author="Arpit"></sheetpane-excel>
<sheetpane-errors pane="q3"></sheetpane-errors>
```

Without a page:

```ts
import { createWorkbook } from '@sheetpane/grid';
import { comments } from '@sheetpane/comments';

const plugin = comments();                  // comments({ write: false }) reads only
const store = createWorkbook({ plugins: [plugin] });
await store.load(bytes, 'holdings.xlsx');
store.getErrors();                          // the file's notes and threads, as `file` notes
const { blob } = await store.exportFile();  // the review written in as threaded comments
plugin.lastExport;                          // { written: [ids], skipped: [{ id, reason }] }
```

## What is read

The plugin reads every legacy note (`xl/comments*.xml`) and every threaded
comment (`xl/threadedComments/*`). Each commented cell becomes one entry in
the error list:

| field | value |
|---|---|
| `type` | `comment` (shown as "Comment") |
| `severity` | `note` |
| `author` | `file`. The pane filters these as "File comments". |
| `range` | the cell |
| `found` | the cell's display text from the upload, or `(blank)` |
| `expected` | `''` |
| `message` | the note, or the whole thread: the first comment, then each reply in order, one per line, each starting with its author's name (`R. Mehta: …`). Thread names come from the file's person list; note names come from its authors list. |
| `status` | `open` |

File notes are read-only in both elements: they show **Show in sheet** but no
Resolve or Delete. They never resolve themselves.

For each thread, Excel also writes a legacy note with the author `tc={id}`.
That note is not listed a second time.

## What is written

On export, every error that did **not** come from the file is written:
people's errors, workbook-rule errors and host-rule errors. Each one is
anchored at the top-left cell of its range.

- **The thread.** The first comment holds a header line (`ERR-0003 · Error · Wrong value · Found: 7.5%`) followed by the `message`. If the error has an `expected`, it follows as a reply (`Should be: 0.75%`). The thread is marked `done="1"` when the error is resolved.
- **One comment per cell.** If several errors share a cell, they form one thread: the first error opens it and the rest follow as replies. It is marked done only when all of them are resolved.
- **A cell that already holds someone's thread.** The errors are added to that thread as replies.
- **A cell that already holds a legacy note.** Nothing is written there, because a cell holds one comment and the note stays untouched. The error appears in `plugin.lastExport.skipped` with the reason `note-at-cell`.

Each sheet with errors gets four parts:

| part | what |
|---|---|
| `xl/threadedComments/threadedCommentN.xml` | the threads (Excel 365) |
| `xl/commentsN.xml` | a legacy comment per thread (author `tc={thread id}`). Its text is Excel's `[Threaded comment]` placeholder, followed by the comment and its replies, so Excel 2019 and older can show something. |
| `xl/drawings/vmlDrawingN.vml` | the hidden note shape Excel needs before it shows any comment, plus `<legacyDrawing>` in the sheet |
| `xl/persons/person.xml` | one person per author, for the whole workbook |

The plugin also adds the four relationships and content types. **A part the
file already has is extended, never replaced:** its notes, threads, shapes,
persons and anything else it holds are kept. If a part cannot be read, that
sheet's parts are left exactly as they were and its errors are reported as
`unreadable-part`.

No font is written. The legacy comment text is a plain `<t>`, and the VML
shape copies the one Excel writes, which names no font (SR-LAW-5).

### Ids: export twice, get one thread

Each thread entry's `id` is a version-5 UUID made from the error's `id` and
`createdAt`. Here is how that plays out:

1. You export a review.
2. You load the exported file and restore the same review with `setErrors(saved)`.
3. You export again.

The second export **replaces** the review's own threads instead of adding
copies. Replies that someone added in Excel stay attached to the thread.
After the review is restored, its own threads are no longer listed as file
notes. Without the restore, the threads come back as `file` notes, which is
how a reviewer sees an earlier review. `createdAt` is part of the name
because error ids restart at `ERR-0001` every session.

### Author names go into the file

Each error's `author` is written into the file as a person's `displayName`
and `userId`, with `providerId="None"`. An empty author is written as
**"Reviewer"**. The `author` attribute is the only source. If the names are
personal data the file should not carry, either set `author` to something
neutral or switch writing off.

## Switching writing off

- `comments({ write: false })`: never write. Notes and threads are still read.
- `export({ comments: false })` on `<sheetpane-excel>` (or `store.exportFile({ options: { comments: false } })`): skip the parts for that one export.

There is no menu item for this. The host decides, and a host that wants an
end-user toggle can put one in its own `format-row` slot.

## Not yet checked

Whether **Excel 365, Excel 2019 and LibreOffice** open an exported file and
show every error at its cell is checked by the decider, on fixtures saved
from Excel (W-30). The parts follow the shapes Excel writes, but these tests
check the parts sheetpane writes and reads, not Excel itself.

Spec: [`work/open/W-22-comments.md`](../../work/open/W-22-comments.md).

**Using an AI coding agent?** `npx sheetpane-skills install` puts sheetpane's skills for Claude Code, Kiro and Codex into your repository.
