<!-- source: packages/fixtures/README.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/main/packages/fixtures/README.md) -->

# @sheetpane/fixtures

**Known workbooks for testing a sheetpane host — and a manifest that says what is in each.**

```js
import { bytes, url, path, info, MANIFEST } from '@sheetpane/fixtures';

excel.file = new Blob([await bytes('showcase.xlsx')]);     // browser or Node
excel.src = url('showcase.xlsx').href;                     // a URL your bundler copies
fs.readFileSync(path('csv/semicolon.csv'));                // Node
info('showcase.rules.json').errors;                        // the cells the rules sample fails
```

| file | what it holds |
|---|---|
| `showcase.xlsx` | one sheet per plugin: Numbers, Styles, Formulas, Validation, CondFmt, Images, Charts, Comments |
| `showcase.rules.json` | a rules file (SR-GRID 22d) that fails six cells of the showcase |
| `edge/*.xlsx` | an empty sheet, a hidden sheet, non-ASCII names, a merged range, the 1904 date system, cached formula errors |
| `edge/legacy.xls`, `edge/not-a-zip.xlsx` | files sheetpane refuses (SR-LAW-3) |
| `csv/*.csv` | comma, semicolon, tab, BOM, quoted fields with newlines, cells the formula guard escapes |

`hugeCsv(rows)` makes the 250,000-row case on demand — it is a generator, not a file.

Every file is **hand-built** by `scripts/make.mjs` (parts written as XML and
zipped by `@sheetpane/export`'s `writeZip`; `just fixtures` rewrites them,
byte for byte the same). Hand-built files prove behaviour, not Excel
compatibility: files saved by Excel, Google Sheets, LibreOffice and Numbers
join with the app named in `appSaved` (W-30). No dependencies.

The spec is the record [SR-FIXTURES](../../records/0115_FIXTURES.md).

**Using an AI coding agent?** `npx sheetpane-skills install` puts sheetpane's skills for Claude Code, Kiro and Codex into your repository.

<!-- source: packages/testing/README.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/main/packages/testing/README.md) -->

# @sheetpane/testing

**Test helpers for apps that embed sheetpane — Playwright and Vitest browser mode, one API.**

```ts
// Playwright
import { sheetpane } from '@sheetpane/testing/playwright';
import { matchers } from '@sheetpane/testing';
expect.extend(matchers);

test('a reviewer edits and downloads', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/review');
  const sp = sheetpane(page);                       // the first <sheetpane-excel>, or { excel: 'css' }
  await sp.waitForLoad();
  await sp.edit({ column: 'Units', row: 4 }, '42');  // by title and row, or 'Sheet1!B4'
  await sp.flag('B5', { expected: '101.20', message: 'Stale price' });
  expect(await sp.errors()).toHaveError({ ref: 'B5', status: 'open' });
  expect(await sp.readDownload()).toHaveCell('Sheet1!F4', 42);
});
```

```ts
// Vitest browser mode: the same API on the element
import { sheetpane } from '@sheetpane/testing/dom';
const sp = sheetpane(document.querySelector('sheetpane-excel')!);
```

| helper | does |
|---|---|
| `waitForLoad()` | until `sheetpane-load` (ready) and the rule checks have finished |
| `ref(at)`, `select(at)`, `value(at)`, `text(at)` | a cell by `B3`, `Sheet1!B3` or `{ column, row }` (the title from `header-row`) |
| `edit(at, text)`, `paste(at, rows)`, `undo()`, `switchSheet(name)` | as a person would: the cell bar, a paste, the toolbar, the tabs |
| `flag(at, { type, severity, message, expected })`, `resolve(at \| index)` | the form in `<sheetpane-errors>` (or inline when none is connected) |
| `download()`, `readDownload()` | presses Download; the file, or its values |
| `readFile(bytes, name)`, `changesBetween(a, b)`, `valueAt(book, 'Sheet1!B2')` | `.xlsx` / `.csv` as values — in Node too (no DOM needed) |
| `matchers.toHaveCell`, `matchers.toHaveError` | for `expect.extend` (Vitest and Playwright) |

The helpers find things only by roles, labels and the grid's committed
`data-sp-*` hooks (SR-GRID decision 9a), never CSS classes — so a host's tests
survive restyling. Known files to test with: `@sheetpane/fixtures`.

The spec is the record [SR-TESTING](../../records/0118_TESTING.md).

**Using an AI coding agent?** `npx sheetpane-skills install` puts sheetpane's skills for Claude Code, Kiro and Codex into your repository.

<!-- source: packages/skills/README.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/main/packages/skills/README.md) -->

# @sheetpane/skills

**sheetpane's agent skills for Claude Code, Kiro and Codex — and the installer that puts them in your repository.**

```sh
npx sheetpane-skills install            # for every tool whose folder already exists here
npx sheetpane-skills install --all      # .claude/, .kiro/ and .agents/
npx sheetpane-skills uninstall          # removes exactly what install wrote
```

Every `@sheetpane/*` package depends on this one, and `@sheetpane/grid` exposes
the same `sheetpane-skills` command, so it is there once sheetpane is.

| what | where it lands |
|---|---|
| 23 skills — embed, react, load-export, errors, events, column-rules, rules-file, plugins, theming, testing, troubleshoot, … and the `sheetpane` router | `.claude/skills/`, `.kiro/skills/`, `.agents/skills/` |
| a short block saying what sheetpane is and which skill to start with | between `<!-- sheetpane:start -->` and `<!-- sheetpane:end -->` in `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` — nothing outside it is touched |
| a Kiro steering file and a `sheetpane-integrator` agent for Claude and Kiro | `.kiro/steering/`, `.claude/agents/`, `.kiro/agents/` |

- Nothing is written on `npm install` (no `postinstall`); only when you run it.
- A file you changed since it was installed is never overwritten without
  `--force`; `--dry-run` lists every path first. What was written is listed in
  `.sheetpane-skills.json`.
- `--skip contributor` leaves out the two skills for contributing to sheetpane
  itself; `--only`, `--skills-only` narrow further.
- Re-run it after upgrading `@sheetpane/*` so the skills match the version.

Each skill points to the sheetpane record it summarises and never restates a
rule as its own; a test fails if a skill names an attribute, member or event
the elements do not have. The spec is the record
[SR-SKILLS](../../records/0116_SKILLS.md).

<!-- source: packages/create-sheetpane/README.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/main/packages/create-sheetpane/README.md) -->

# create-sheetpane

**A working sheetpane app in one command.**

```sh
npm create sheetpane@latest               # asks: folder, template, skills, MCP server
npm create sheetpane@latest my-app -- --template react --skills host --yes
pnpm create sheetpane my-app --template vue
```

| template | what you get |
|---|---|
| `vanilla` | Vite + TypeScript, no framework |
| `react` | React 19 on Vite; `onsheetpane-…` props typed by `@sheetpane/grid/jsx` |
| `next` | Next.js App Router; the sheet loads on the client only (`next/dynamic`, `ssr: false`) |
| `vue` | Vue 3 on Vite; `isCustomElement` set, typed by `@sheetpane/grid/vue` |
| `angular` | Angular, a standalone component with `CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA` (needs Node ^22.22.3 or ^24.15.0) |
| `svelte` | Svelte 5 on Vite; typed by `@sheetpane/grid/svelte` |

Every template has the same app: `<sheetpane-excel>` and `<sheetpane-errors>`
on one `pane`, side by side, and the sheet again behind an **Open in a pop-up**
button (`display="popup"`); the showcase workbook and its rules file from
`@sheetpane/fixtures`; one Playwright test on `@sheetpane/testing` (the file
loads, the rules flag a cell, an edit reaches the download); and a README.
Framework versions are pinned exactly — the ones CI built and tested — and
every `@sheetpane/*` package at this package's version (they are released
together).

| option | does |
|---|---|
| `--template <t>` | one of the six above |
| `--skills all \| host \| none` | runs `sheetpane-skills install --all` after installing — `host` leaves out the two skills for contributing to sheetpane itself; `none` skips it |
| `--mcp`, `--no-mcp` | register the sheetpane MCP server (`@sheetpane/mcp`) with Claude Code, Kiro and Codex, or not |
| `--pm npm \| pnpm \| yarn` | the package manager (default: the one that ran `create`) |
| `--no-install` | copy the files only |
| `-y`, `--yes` | no questions; defaults: `sheetpane-app`, `vanilla`, `host`, MCP on |

The folder must be new or empty; nothing outside it is written. No
dependencies, no `postinstall`.

The spec is the record SR-CREATE; the repo checks every template on each push
with `just create-check` (scaffold, install from the packed tarballs, build,
test).

<!-- source: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) -->

# sheetpane — architecture

**In one sentence:** a host web page installs one npm package, `@sheetpane/grid`,
drops two custom elements anywhere it likes, and both of them read and write a single
JavaScript object — the workbook — which an export package turns back into an
`.xlsx` or `.csv` file. Nothing leaves the browser tab.

**What this document is.** The map. The *rules* are the laws in
[`records/`](../records/README.md); the *decisions* are the four verdicts in
[`work/compare/`](../work/compare/README.md); the *work* is in
[`work/OPEN-WORK.md`](../work/OPEN-WORK.md). This page restates none of them
in full — it shows how they fit and links to each. If this page and a record
disagree, the record wins and this page gets fixed.

## The picture

![sheetpane architecture — host application on top, the sheetpane package with two elements and one in-memory workbook in the middle, the export package and browser APIs below](architecture.svg)

The same picture as a flow:

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph host["YOUR APPLICATION — React 19, plain index.html, anything"]
        T["a tab · a pop-up · different tabs"]
        C["your code: listens to events, saves errors, receives files"]
    end
    subgraph pkg["npm package: @sheetpane/grid"]
        X["&lt;sheetpane-excel&gt;<br/>View · Edit<br/>reader · grid · cell bar · Flag issue"]
        W[("in-memory workbook<br/>one per pane<br/>cells · changes · errors · selection · mode")]
        E["&lt;sheetpane-errors&gt;<br/>list · New error form"]
    end
    subgraph exp["npm package: @sheetpane/export"]
        P["toXlsx · patchXlsx · toCsv · download<br/>zip · crc32 · xml · csv"]
    end
    B["built into the browser: DecompressionStream · CompressionStream · DOMParser · customElements · Blob"]
    T -->|places, gives a file| X
    T -->|places| E
    X <-->|read / write| W
    E <-->|read / write| W
    X -->|Export: workbook + every change| P
    P -.->|new file, original untouched| C
    X -.->|sheetpane-* events| C
    E -.->|sheetpane-* events| C
    X --- B
    P --- B
```

<details>
<summary><b>ASCII twin</b> — the same picture, for terminals and diffs</summary>

```text
  YOUR APPLICATION  (React 19 · plain index.html · anything)
  [ a tab ] [ a pop-up ] [ different tabs ]            [ your code: events, saves, files ]
        |                   |                                   ^            ^
        | places it         | places it                 events |            | new file
        v                   v                                   |            |
  +-- npm: @sheetpane/grid ---------------------------------------------------+   |
  |  <sheetpane-excel>  <--->  ( in-memory workbook )  <--->  <sheetpane-errors> |   |
  |  View · Edit                one per pane                   list · form      |   |
  |  reader · grid              cells · changes · errors                        |   |
  |  cell bar · Flag issue      selection · mode                                |   |
  +----------|----------------------------------------------------------------+   |
             | Export: the workbook + every change held in memory                 |
             v                                                                    |
  +-- npm: @sheetpane/export ---------------------------------+                   |
  |  toXlsx · patchXlsx · toCsv · download(data, filename)    |-------------------+
  +-----------------------------------------------------------+
  built into the browser: DecompressionStream · CompressionStream · DOMParser · customElements · Blob
```

</details>

## The pieces

| piece | what it is | where it lives | decided in |
|---|---|---|---|
| **host application** | any web page; installs `@sheetpane/grid` from npm; places the elements; listens to events | the host's codebase; demos in `examples/` (W-09) | [SR-LAW-4](../records/0006_LAW-4-web-component.md), [SR-LAW-8](../records/0010_LAW-8-npm-package.md) |
| **`<sheetpane-excel>`** | the sheet: the **view** component and the **edit** component as two modes of one element; reader, virtualised grid, cell bar with the docked selection actions (Flag issue, ⋯, right-click), pins and callouts, one Download button | `packages/grid/src/excel/` (W-01) | [grid verdict](../work/compare/grid-rendering.compare.md) |
| **`@sheetpane/import`** | the reader: turns an `.xlsx` or `.csv` into the same `Workbook` object export takes in: ZIP walk + inflate + XML, or a CSV state machine; display text through a small number-format subset; usable without the UI | `packages/import/` (W-13) | [reading verdict](../work/compare/xlsx-csv-reading.compare.md), decision 5 overridden by Arpit 2026-10-18 |
| **in-memory workbook** | the one shared object — sheets and cells, cell **changes**, **errors**, selected cell, mode; a store with `subscribe` / `getSnapshot`; one instance per `pane` id | `packages/grid/src/pane/` (W-01) | [contract verdict](../work/compare/workbook-and-error-contract.compare.md) |
| **`<sheetpane-errors>`** | the **error** component: the list (filter, resolve, delete) and the New error form; always on the same workbook as the sheet | `packages/grid/src/errors/` (W-02) | [contract verdict](../work/compare/workbook-and-error-contract.compare.md) |
| **`@sheetpane/export`** | a plain object or the original file plus changes → `.xlsx` or `.csv` bytes; `download()` to save it (W-12, [SR-DOWNLOAD](../records/0101_DOWNLOAD.md)); ZIP read and write, CRC-32, XML, CSV; zero dependencies; also usable without the UI | `packages/export/` (W-03, W-12) | [export verdict](../work/compare/export-shape.compare.md) |
| **plugins** | eight separate packages that register against the one workbook through six hooks (`format`, `decorate`, `derive`, `validate`, `overlay`, `exportPatch`) and add controls to six slots the grid draws; the grid with none installed is unchanged | `packages/numfmt/` `formulas/` `styles/` `validation/` `condfmt/` `images/` `charts/` `comments/` (W-15–W-22); the host in `packages/grid/src/plugins/` (W-14) | [plugins verdict](../work/compare/plugins.compare.md) |
| **browser APIs** | `DecompressionStream` / `CompressionStream` (`deflate-raw`), `DOMParser`, `customElements`, `Blob` | the browser; Node 20+ uses `zlib` for export | the reading and export verdicts |

**Dependency direction:** host → plugins → `@sheetpane/grid` → `@sheetpane/import` → `@sheetpane/export` → browser.
Nothing points the other way. `@sheetpane/export` has no runtime dependencies;
`@sheetpane/grid` depends on `import` and `export`; every plugin lists
`@sheetpane/grid` as a peer at the exact version. Two plugins carry the only
third-party runtime dependencies in the project — `numfmt` (MIT) and
`@ironcalc/wasm` (MIT / Apache-2.0), both pinned. Everything is versioned in
lockstep and published together.

## The four flows

**1 · Load.** The host gives the element a file (`src` URL or base64, or the
`file` property). The reader inflates the parts it needs, parses the XML,
resolves shared strings and merges, formats typed cells once, and writes the
sheets into the workbook store. The grid draws the visible window. Anything
that is not `.xlsx` or `.csv` is refused before parsing (L3).

**2 · Edit.** In Edit mode the cell bar is a text box. A new value becomes a
`change` in the store — `sheet!ref → { was, now }` — never a write to the file.
Every element on the same `pane` re-renders from the store: the sheet shows a
corner mark and "Changed · was X"; the error list shows "matches suggestion"
if the new value equals an error's correction. A reload loses unexported
changes (L6, L9), so the sheet warns on `beforeunload` while changes are held.

**3 · Flag and review.** **Flag issue** on a cell sets `composing` on the
store. If a `<sheetpane-errors>` is connected to the pane it shows the form;
otherwise the sheet shows a small inline form. **Add error** writes a
`SheetpaneError` into the store: `found` is frozen as the uploaded value; the
sheet pins the cell; the list gains a row. Resolve, reopen and delete work from
either element. **Show in sheet** dispatches `sheetpane-reveal` so the host can
switch to the tab that holds the sheet.

**4 · Export.** The sheet asks `@sheetpane/export` for the file: for an `.xlsx`
source, `patchXlsx(originalBytes, changes)` rewrites only the changed cells and
copies every other part byte for byte — charts, styles, comments and defined
names survive; for a `.csv` source, `toCsv(activeSheet)` with BOM and the
formula guard. The result is a `Blob`, dispatched as `sheetpane-export` and
returned from `export()`; the Download button hands it to `download()` from the
same package — or, when nothing changed, the original bytes untouched. The
uploaded file is never modified.

## The public contract (working names)

Settled in the [contract verdict](../work/compare/workbook-and-error-contract.compare.md); W-01's record makes it final.

| kind | names |
|---|---|
| elements | `<sheetpane-excel>`, `<sheetpane-errors>` |
| link | `pane="…"` on both — same id, same workbook; or set the `workbook` property |
| attributes | `src`, `mode` (`view` \| `edit`), `display` (`tab` \| `popup`), `open`, `author`, `readonly` |
| properties | `file`, `workbook`, `errors`, `errorTypes` |
| methods | `load()`, `export()`, `select()`, `getErrors()`, `setErrors()` |
| events | `sheetpane-load` · `-change` · `-errors` · `-select` · `-mode` · `-close` · `-export` · `-reveal` — bubbling, composed |
| styling | `--sp-*` custom properties on the element for colour, spacing, radius; **no font** — the host's font is inherited through the shadow root |

Plain HTML:

```html
<script type="module" src="/node_modules/@sheetpane/grid/dist/index.js"></script>
<sheetpane-excel pane="q3" src="/files/holdings.xlsx" mode="edit"></sheetpane-excel>
<sheetpane-errors pane="q3"></sheetpane-errors>
```

React 19 renders the same tags; React 18 sets properties through a `ref`
(no wrapper ships — ruled in [SR-LAW-4](../records/0006_LAW-4-web-component.md) Consequences).

## Where each law lands

| law | what it fixes | where you see it in the shape |
|---|---|---|
| [L2](../records/0004_LAW-2-foss-dependencies.md) FOSS dependencies | every dependency OSI-licensed; no copyleft at runtime | export, import and grid have **no** third-party runtime dependency; the licence check is B-008 |
| [L3](../records/0005_LAW-3-xlsx-and-csv-only.md) XLSX and CSV only | no other parser, reader or writer | the reader refuses by extension and magic bytes; `.csv` dialects (`,` `;` tab) are read; `download()` refuses other extensions |
| [L4](../records/0006_LAW-4-web-component.md) always a web component | DOM-only contract; no framework peer | two custom elements; plain DOM inside; the host's framework is its own business |
| [L5](../records/0007_LAW-5-host-font.md) the host's font | no font ships; every part inherits | shadow root with inherited `font`; `font: inherit` on controls; `--sp-*` tokens carry no font |
| [L6](../records/0008_LAW-6-edits-in-memory-export-with-changes.md) edits in memory, export carries them | memory is the only store; export applies every change; original untouched | the `changes` map; `patchXlsx`; `beforeunload` warning |
| [L7](../records/0009_LAW-7-surfaces-always-in-sync.md) always in sync | one workbook, no private copies | the store registry by `pane`; both elements subscribe; selection syncs |
| [L8](../records/0010_LAW-8-npm-package.md) an npm package | one distribution; safe to import in Node every package under `packages/`, lockstep versions; elements register only when `customElements` exists; `download()` throws cleanly without a `document` |
| [L9](../records/0011_LAW-9-memory-is-a-javascript-object.md) memory is a JavaScript object | no IndexedDB or storage, for now | the store is objects in the page; IndexedDB waits on B-025 |

## Package layout

```text
pnpm-workspace.yaml       packages/*  (W-10: pnpm replaces npm workspaces)
justfile                  install · build · test · typecheck · check · release
packages/
  export/                 @sheetpane/export — zero dependencies (SR-EXPORT)
    src/
      zip.ts deflate.ts crc32.ts   read (central directory) + write; CompressionStream / zlib
      xml.ts refs.ts formula.ts    escaping, A1 helpers, shiftFormula
      xlsx.ts patch.ts validate.ts toXlsx (build), patchXlsx (rewrite changed <c> only), input rules
      csv.ts                       toCsv — RFC 4180, BOM, formula guard
      download/                    download(data, filename) — SR-DOWNLOAD
  import/                 @sheetpane/import — depends only on @sheetpane/export (SR-IMPORT)
    src/                  read.ts (detect + refuse), xlsx.ts, csv.ts, numfmt.ts (the subset), styles.ts, dom.ts
  grid/                   @sheetpane/grid — depends on @sheetpane/import and @sheetpane/export (workspace:)
    src/
      pane/               the workbook store, the pane registry, the error schema
      excel/              <sheetpane-excel>: grid (virtualiser), toolbar, cell bar, pins, callout, inline form, popup
      errors/             <sheetpane-errors>: list, filters, New error form
      tokens.css          --sp-* custom properties (no font)
      plugins/            W-14 — hooks, slots, control descriptors, the plugins attribute
      index.ts            registers both elements when customElements exists
  numfmt/                 @sheetpane/numfmt — W-15; dep: numfmt 4.0.1
  formulas/               @sheetpane/formulas — W-16; dep: @ironcalc/wasm 0.9.0 (lazy-loaded)
  styles/                 @sheetpane/styles — W-17
  validation/             @sheetpane/validation — W-18
  condfmt/                @sheetpane/condfmt — W-19; peer: @sheetpane/styles
  images/                 @sheetpane/images — W-20
  charts/                 @sheetpane/charts — W-21; peer: @sheetpane/images
  comments/               @sheetpane/comments — W-22
    (each: package.json · README.md · tsconfig.json · src/index.ts, and src/ui.ts where it adds controls)
examples/                 W-09 — html/ (one index.html) and react/ (Vite + React 19)
```

## Build order

```text
W-10 pnpm + just ✓ ──► W-04 build · test · CI ✓ ──► W-03 export ✓ ──► W-13 import ✓ ──► W-01 excel + workbook ──► W-02 errors ──► W-09 demos
                                                     W-12 download ✓ (inside export's package)
```

Then the plugins, in this order (each waits on the plugin host and the reader):

```text
W-14 plugin host ──► W-15 numfmt ──► W-16 formulas ──► W-23 undo ──► W-17 styles ──► W-18 validation ──► W-19 condfmt ──► W-20 images ──► W-21 charts ──► W-22 comments
W-24 freeze panes runs beside W-01 (core, not a plugin)
```

Every research question that gated this order was ruled on 2026-10-18; the
five verdicts and their reopen-triggers are in [`work/compare/`](../work/compare/README.md).
How it is all tested — Vitest, real browsers, fixtures, goldens — is the
[testing verdict](../work/compare/testing.compare.md).

## Still open, on purpose

- **IndexedDB** (B-025) — the decider's deferred request; needs L6 and L9 rewritten.
- **Largest workbook the tab can hold** (B-026) — unmeasured until W-01 lands.
- **The mechanical check still owed:** B-008 (licences over the whole tree). The
  font, framework-peer, publishable, refusal, round-trip and sync checks run
  today ([SR-BUILD](../records/0102_BUILD.md), [SR-GRID](../records/0105_GRID.md)).
- **SR-LAW-6's veto command flags the `src` loader's read** (B-030) — the decider's ruling.

<!-- source: docs/GLOSSARY.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/main/docs/GLOSSARY.md) -->

# Glossary

| term | meaning |
|---|---|
| Standing Record (SR) | a maintained specification in `records/`, cited by name; see the register |
| Law | a rule that outranks every other record; `SR-LAW-n` |
| memory | JavaScript objects held in the page; not IndexedDB, browser storage or a server — see SR-LAW-9 |
| error component | the review surface that marks incorrect data and states the correction; one of the three components SR-LAW-7 keeps in sync |
| web component | a custom element registered through the Custom Elements standard, usable from any framework or plain HTML; see SR-LAW-4 |
| FOSS | free and open source software — here, a licence on the OSI-approved list; see SR-LAW-2 |
| W-nn | an open work item — a queue row plus a detail file |
| B-nnn | a backlog row — named, unclaimed, no file |
| ball | the one marker every queue row opens with: 🔴 🟣 🟡 🟢 |
| blocker | `work/BLOCKED.json` with a decision other than `PROCEED` |
| veto condition | the checkable condition under which a decision reopens |
| pane | the one in-memory workbook a set of sheetpane elements share, named by their `pane` attribute; see `work/compare/workbook-and-error-contract.compare.md` |
| change (sheetpane) | one edited cell held in the workbook as `sheet!ref → { was, now }`; export applies every change, the file is never modified |
| sheetpane-excel | working name of the web component that is both the view and the edit component |
| sheetpane-errors | working name of the web component that is the error component |
| justfile | the root file of recipes for `just`, a command runner; `just --list` shows every repo command (W-10) |
| column rules | checks a host supplies per column header title (`columns`, `validate`); failures become errors with `author: "host"` that resolve themselves when the cell passes (SR-GRID decision 22) |
| skill | a Markdown file an AI coding agent reads to learn a task; `npx sheetpane-skills install` copies sheetpane's into a repository (SR-SKILLS) |
| SP code | a permanent `SP-xxxx` code on every error, warning, note and refusal sheetpane shows, listed in `docs/ERRORS.md` (SR-CODES) |
| rules file | a JSON document of column, cell and range rules per sheet (`"*"` for every sheet), given as `rules` or `rules-src`; checked by the same engine as column rules (SR-GRID decision 22d) |
| flagging | whether people can flag issues on the sheet; `flagging="off"` removes Flag issue, the composer and the callout card, leaving the errors panel as the one place errors are read (SR-GRID decision 22e) |
| Proof | the colour and spacing tokens sheetpane shares with PDF Suite — `work/reference/design/boards/proof.css`; its fonts do not ship (SR-LAW-5) |
| plugin (sheetpane) | a separate npm package that registers against the one in-memory workbook through named hooks and adds controls to named slots; enabled per `pane` by `createWorkbook({ plugins })` or the `plugins` attribute — `work/compare/plugins.compare.md` |
| hook | one of six named functions on the workbook store a plugin may provide: `format`, `decorate`, `derive`, `validate`, `overlay`, `exportPatch` |
| slot | one of six named places in the grid a plugin's control descriptor may target: `format-row`, `selbar`, `cellbar`, `status`, `cell`, `overlay`; the grid draws the control, the plugin describes it |
| derived cell | a cell whose value a plugin computed (`derive`) rather than the user typed; marked in the grid, never in the change map |


---

<!-- source: docs/ERRORS.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/main/docs/ERRORS.md) -->

# Error codes

**Every message sheetpane shows a host carries a stable code.** A thrown
error, a console line, a rules-file note, a refused load or a blocked edit
reads `SP-3012: Plugin derive failed — … (…/ERRORS.md#sp-3012)`.

**A code is permanent.** It is never renumbered and never reused. A code no
longer raised stays in the registry, marked *retired*.

**The registry is code.** `CODES` in
[`packages/export/src/codes.ts`](../packages/export/src/codes.ts) holds each
code's title and severity; this page holds the long text. The repo test
`test/error-codes.test.ts` fails when the two disagree.

## Where the code is

| surface | where to read it |
|---|---|
| a thrown error | `err.spCode` on every one; `err.code` too, except on `ExportError` and `ImportError`, whose `code` stays the typed reason (`corrupt`, `password-or-legacy`, …) |
| a console warning or error | the text starts with the code and ends with the link to this page |
| a rules-engine note (`SheetpaneError`) | `error.code` — optional, so a v1 error without it stays valid |
| `sheetpane-load` with `status: 'error'` | `detail.spCode` (`detail.code` stays the reader's reason) |
| `sheetpane-editcancel` with `reason: 'blocked'` | `detail.code` |
| anything above | `codeOf(x)` from `@sheetpane/export` (or `@sheetpane/grid`) returns the code, or `undefined` |

## Ranges

| range | package |
|---|---|
| 1xxx | `@sheetpane/import` — reading a file |
| 2xxx | `@sheetpane/export` — writing a file, the ZIP walk, `download()` (21xx) |
| 3xxx | `@sheetpane/grid` — the store, the plugin host, `<sheetpane-excel>` |
| 4xxx | `<sheetpane-errors>` — none raised yet |
| 5xxx | plugins — 5100 numfmt · 5200 formulas · 5300 styles · 5400 validation · 5500 condfmt · 5600 images · 5700 charts · 5800 comments |
| 6xxx | column rules and the rules file |
| 7xxx | `@sheetpane/mcp` — reserved |

---

## 1xxx · import

Raised by `read()`, `fromXlsx()` and `fromCsv()` as an `ImportError`; the
grid shows it as "Can't open this file" (or the password state) and fires
`sheetpane-load` with `status: 'error'`.

### SP-1001

**Not an .xlsx or .csv file** · error · [SR-IMPORT](../records/0104_IMPORT.md) · [SR-LAW-3](../records/0005_LAW-3-xlsx-and-csv-only.md) · `code: 'unsupported-format'`

- **Meaning:** sheetpane opens `.xlsx` and `.csv` only, and this file is neither.
- **Likely cause:** a `.xls`, `.xlsm`, `.xlsb`, `.ods`, `.numbers` or `.tsv` file; a ZIP named `.csv`; binary bytes with no name.
- **Fix:** save the file as `.xlsx` or `.csv` in the program that made it, then open it again.

### SP-1002

**Password-protected workbook** · error · [SR-IMPORT](../records/0104_IMPORT.md) · `code: 'password-or-legacy'`, `detail: 'password'`

- **Meaning:** the file is an encrypted `.xlsx` (an OLE file holding an `EncryptedPackage`).
- **Likely cause:** the workbook was saved with a password to open.
- **Fix:** remove the password in Excel (File → Info → Protect Workbook), save, and open it again.

### SP-1003

**Legacy .xls workbook** · error · [SR-IMPORT](../records/0104_IMPORT.md) · `code: 'password-or-legacy'`, `detail: 'legacy'`

- **Meaning:** the file is an OLE compound file without an encrypted package — the pre-2007 `.xls` format.
- **Likely cause:** an old workbook, or a `.xls` renamed to `.xlsx`.
- **Fix:** open it in Excel and save it as `.xlsx` or `.csv`.

### SP-1004

**Encrypted or OLE file** · error · [SR-IMPORT](../records/0104_IMPORT.md) · `code: 'password-or-legacy'`

- **Meaning:** the file is encrypted, but which kind cannot be told.
- **Likely cause:** a ZIP whose entries are encrypted (ZIP-level password).
- **Fix:** remove the password and save the workbook as a plain `.xlsx`.

### SP-1005

**Not a workbook** · error · [SR-IMPORT](../records/0104_IMPORT.md) · `code: 'not-workbook'`

- **Meaning:** the bytes are not an `.xlsx` workbook.
- **Likely cause:** a ZIP with no `xl/workbook.xml`, text named `.xlsx`, a workbook with no worksheets, or a file cut short in transfer.
- **Fix:** check the file opens in Excel; re-download or re-export it.

### SP-1006

**File too large** · error · [SR-IMPORT](../records/0104_IMPORT.md) · `code: 'too-large'`

- **Meaning:** the file is past a limit the reader keeps.
- **Likely cause:** a ZIP64 archive; a part over 512 MB or 1 GB in all inflated; more than 1,048,576 rows or 16,384 columns (Excel's own limits).
- **Fix:** split the workbook, or remove unused rows and columns, and save it again.

### SP-1007

**Damaged file** · error · [SR-IMPORT](../records/0104_IMPORT.md) · `code: 'corrupt'`

- **Meaning:** the file is a workbook, but part of it cannot be read.
- **Likely cause:** bad DEFLATE data, a CRC mismatch, XML that is not well-formed, a sheet pointing at a missing part.
- **Fix:** open and re-save it in Excel, which repairs most damage; then open it again.

### SP-1008

**Reading .xlsx needs a DOM** · error · **retired** · [SR-IMPORT](../records/0104_IMPORT.md) decision 8

- **Meaning:** no longer raised. `.xlsx` once needed `DOMParser`; since W-39 the reader carries its own XML parser for runtimes without one, so `.xlsx` reads in Node, workers and server renders.
- **Likely cause:** an older `@sheetpane/import`.
- **Fix:** upgrade `@sheetpane/import`. The code is kept so it is never reused.

---

## 2xxx · export

Raised by `toXlsx()`, `patchXlsx()`, `toCsv()` and the ZIP walk as an
`ExportError` (`sheet` and `ref` name where); `download()` errors (21xx) are
plain `Error`s or `TypeError`s.

### SP-2001

**Invalid sheet name** · error · [SR-EXPORT](../records/0103_EXPORT.md) · `code: 'sheet-name'`

- **Meaning:** a sheet name breaks Excel's rules.
- **Likely cause:** empty or over 31 characters; contains `[ ] : * ? / \`; starts or ends with `'`; used twice (case is ignored).
- **Fix:** rename the sheet; `checkSheetName()` tells you before you export.

### SP-2002

**No visible sheet** · error · [SR-EXPORT](../records/0103_EXPORT.md) · `code: 'sheet-count'`

- **Meaning:** a workbook needs at least one sheet, and at least one visible.
- **Likely cause:** `sheets: []`, or every sheet `hidden: true`.
- **Fix:** add a sheet, or un-hide one.

### SP-2003

**Sheet past Excel’s limits** · error · [SR-EXPORT](../records/0103_EXPORT.md) · `code: 'too-large'`

- **Meaning:** a sheet has more than 1,048,576 rows or a row more than 16,384 columns.
- **Likely cause:** data larger than a worksheet holds; `ref` names the first cell past the limit.
- **Fix:** split the data across sheets, or export CSV.

### SP-2004

**Not a cell reference** · error · [SR-EXPORT](../records/0103_EXPORT.md) · `code: 'bad-ref'`

- **Meaning:** a change names a `ref` that is not an A1 cell.
- **Likely cause:** `A0`, a range, or a typo in a `patchXlsx` change.
- **Fix:** pass one A1 cell per change (`B7`).

### SP-2005

**Value a workbook cannot store** · error · [SR-EXPORT](../records/0103_EXPORT.md) · `code: 'bad-value'`

- **Meaning:** a cell holds something a workbook cell cannot.
- **Likely cause:** `NaN` or `Infinity`; text over 32,767 characters; an object or `undefined`; `rows` not an array of arrays.
- **Fix:** store text, a finite number, a boolean or `null`; the message names the cell.

### SP-2006

**No such sheet** · error · [SR-EXPORT](../records/0103_EXPORT.md) · `code: 'no-sheet'`

- **Meaning:** a change, merge or freeze names a sheet the workbook lacks.
- **Likely cause:** a renamed sheet, or a typo in the sheet name.
- **Fix:** use the exact sheet name from the workbook.

### SP-2007

**Invalid merge** · error · [SR-EXPORT](../records/0103_EXPORT.md) · `code: 'bad-merge'`

- **Meaning:** a merge is not a range of two or more cells, or overlaps another merge.
- **Likely cause:** a single cell given as a merge; two merges that share a cell.
- **Fix:** give `A1:C1`-style ranges that do not overlap.

### SP-2008

**Not a ZIP archive** · error · [SR-EXPORT](../records/0103_EXPORT.md) · `code: 'not-zip'`

- **Meaning:** no end-of-central-directory record was found.
- **Likely cause:** the bytes are not a ZIP (not an `.xlsx`), or were cut short.
- **Fix:** pass the original `.xlsx` bytes, unmodified.

### SP-2009

**ZIP64 archive refused** · error · [SR-EXPORT](../records/0103_EXPORT.md) · `code: 'zip64'`

- **Meaning:** the archive uses ZIP64, which sheetpane does not read.
- **Likely cause:** a package over 4 GB or 65,534 entries, or a tool that always writes ZIP64.
- **Fix:** re-save the workbook in Excel, which writes plain ZIP for normal sizes.

### SP-2010

**Encrypted ZIP entry** · error · [SR-EXPORT](../records/0103_EXPORT.md) · `code: 'encrypted'`

- **Meaning:** a ZIP entry is encrypted.
- **Likely cause:** the package was zipped with a password.
- **Fix:** re-save the workbook without a password.

### SP-2011

**Unsupported ZIP compression** · error · [SR-EXPORT](../records/0103_EXPORT.md) · `code: 'unsupported-compression'`

- **Meaning:** an entry uses a method other than store or DEFLATE.
- **Likely cause:** a tool that re-zipped the package with BZIP2, LZMA or similar.
- **Fix:** re-save the workbook in Excel.

### SP-2012

**Damaged archive** · error · [SR-EXPORT](../records/0103_EXPORT.md) · `code: 'corrupt'`

- **Meaning:** the archive or a part in it is damaged.
- **Likely cause:** a broken central directory or local header, an entry past the end, bad DEFLATE data, a CRC-32 mismatch, an unclosed row or `<sheetData>`.
- **Fix:** re-save the workbook in Excel; re-download it if it came over a network.

### SP-2013

**Archive over the size limit** · error · [SR-EXPORT](../records/0103_EXPORT.md) · `code: 'over-limit'`

- **Meaning:** reading would inflate past a cap, or writing would need ZIP64.
- **Likely cause:** a part over `maxEntrySize` (512 MB) or the whole over `maxTotalSize` (1 GB); a written archive over 4 GB or 65,534 entries.
- **Fix:** split the workbook; when calling `readZip` / `inflateEntry` yourself, raise their `limits` only for files you trust.

### SP-2014

**Not a workbook package** · error · [SR-EXPORT](../records/0103_EXPORT.md) · `code: 'not-workbook'`

- **Meaning:** `patchXlsx` was given a ZIP with no `xl/workbook.xml`.
- **Likely cause:** the upload was not an `.xlsx`, or the wrong bytes were passed.
- **Fix:** pass the original workbook's bytes.

### SP-2101

**download() needs a file name** · error · [SR-DOWNLOAD](../records/0101_DOWNLOAD.md) · `TypeError`

- **Meaning:** the second argument of `download()` is not a string.
- **Likely cause:** `download(bytes)` with no name.
- **Fix:** `download(bytes, 'report.xlsx')`.

### SP-2102

**Only .xlsx or .csv can be saved** · error · [SR-DOWNLOAD](../records/0101_DOWNLOAD.md) · [SR-LAW-3](../records/0005_LAW-3-xlsx-and-csv-only.md)

- **Meaning:** the file name ends in an extension other than `.xlsx` or `.csv`.
- **Likely cause:** `report.pdf`, `data.xls`.
- **Fix:** name the file `.xlsx` or `.csv`, or leave the extension off.

### SP-2103

**File type cannot be told** · error · [SR-DOWNLOAD](../records/0101_DOWNLOAD.md)

- **Meaning:** no extension was given and the Blob's type is neither `.xlsx` nor CSV.
- **Likely cause:** a Blob made without a `type`.
- **Fix:** add `.xlsx` or `.csv` to the name.

### SP-2104

**Text cannot be saved as .xlsx** · error · [SR-DOWNLOAD](../records/0101_DOWNLOAD.md)

- **Meaning:** a string was passed with an `.xlsx` name.
- **Likely cause:** `toCsv()` output saved under an `.xlsx` name.
- **Fix:** save text as `.csv`, or pass `toXlsx()` bytes.

### SP-2105

**File name is empty once cleaned** · error · [SR-DOWNLOAD](../records/0101_DOWNLOAD.md)

- **Meaning:** removing unsafe characters, spaces and dots left no name.
- **Likely cause:** a name like `  .xlsx`.
- **Fix:** give a name with letters or digits.

### SP-2106

**download() needs a browser page** · error · [SR-DOWNLOAD](../records/0101_DOWNLOAD.md)

- **Meaning:** there is no `document` to click a download link in.
- **Likely cause:** `download()` called in Node, a worker or a server render.
- **Fix:** write the bytes yourself there (`fs.writeFile`); call `download()` only in a page.

### SP-2107

**download() data type not accepted** · error · [SR-DOWNLOAD](../records/0101_DOWNLOAD.md) · `TypeError`

- **Meaning:** the first argument is not a `Uint8Array`, a `Blob` or a string.
- **Likely cause:** an `ArrayBuffer`, a number, or a `Promise` not awaited.
- **Fix:** pass `await toXlsx(…)`, `toCsv(…).text`, or a `Blob`.

---

## 3xxx · grid

The store, the plugin host and `<sheetpane-excel>`.

### SP-3001

**Nothing is loaded to export** · error · [SR-GRID](../records/0105_GRID.md) decision 6

- **Meaning:** `exportFile()` (or the element's `export()`) ran with no workbook in the pane.
- **Likely cause:** export called before `load()` settled, or after a refused load.
- **Fix:** wait for `sheetpane-load` with `status: 'ready'` before exporting.

### SP-3002

**Unknown plugin** · error · [SR-GRID](../records/0105_GRID.md) decision 18

- **Meaning:** the `plugins` attribute names an id no package has registered.
- **Likely cause:** the plugin's package was not imported, or was imported after the element connected; a typo in the id.
- **Fix:** `import '@sheetpane/<plugin>'` before the element is in the page.

### SP-3003

**Not a plugin** · error · [SR-GRID](../records/0105_GRID.md) decision 17

- **Meaning:** an entry in the plugin list is not `{ id, provides: [...] }`.
- **Likely cause:** a factory called twice, a missing `provides` array, `undefined` in the list.
- **Fix:** pass plugin objects — `numfmt()`, not `numfmt`.

### SP-3004

**Plugin listed twice** · error · [SR-GRID](../records/0105_GRID.md) decision 17

- **Meaning:** two plugins in one pane share an id.
- **Likely cause:** the same plugin passed twice to `createWorkbook({ plugins })`.
- **Fix:** list each plugin once.

### SP-3005

**Plugin hook without its function** · error · [SR-GRID](../records/0105_GRID.md) decision 17

- **Meaning:** a plugin's `provides` names a hook it does not implement.
- **Likely cause:** `provides: ['format']` with no `format()` method.
- **Fix:** implement the hook, or remove it from `provides`.

### SP-3006

**Hook has one provider per pane** · error · [SR-GRID](../records/0105_GRID.md) decision 17

- **Meaning:** two plugins provide `format` or `derive`, which have one provider per pane.
- **Likely cause:** two number-format or two formula plugins in one pane.
- **Fix:** keep one; the message names both.

### SP-3007

**Duplicate control id** · error · [SR-GRID](../records/0105_GRID.md) decision 19

- **Meaning:** two controls in one pane share an id.
- **Likely cause:** two plugins (or one plugin listed twice) adding the same control.
- **Fix:** give each control a unique id.

### SP-3008

**Unknown control slot** · error · [SR-GRID](../records/0105_GRID.md) decision 19

- **Meaning:** a control names a slot the grid does not have.
- **Likely cause:** a typo, or a slot from a newer grid.
- **Fix:** use one of `SLOTS` (`format-row`, `selbar`, `cellbar`, `status`, `cell`, `overlay`).

### SP-3009

**Decorate order loops** · error · [SR-GRID](../records/0105_GRID.md) decision 17

- **Meaning:** the `after` lists of `decorate` plugins form a cycle.
- **Likely cause:** plugin A runs after B and B after A.
- **Fix:** break the cycle in one plugin's `after`; the message shows the loop.

### SP-3010

**Plugin set a font family** · error · [SR-LAW-5](../records/0007_LAW-5-host-font.md) · [SR-GRID](../records/0105_GRID.md) decision 17

- **Meaning:** a `decorate` result named `font-family`; the host's font is the font.
- **Likely cause:** a plugin copying a workbook's font into the cell style.
- **Fix:** drop `font-family` from the plugin's `decorate` result.

### SP-3011

**Plugin set fixed per pane** · warning · [SR-GRID](../records/0105_GRID.md) decision 18

- **Meaning:** a later element named a different plugin set for a pane that already exists; it is ignored.
- **Likely cause:** `<sheetpane-errors pane="q3" plugins="…">` disagreeing with the sheet's `plugins`.
- **Fix:** give every element of one pane the same `plugins`, or set it on the first only.

### SP-3012

**Plugin derive failed** · error · [SR-GRID](../records/0105_GRID.md) decision 17

- **Meaning:** a plugin's `derive` threw or rejected; derived values were not updated.
- **Likely cause:** a bug in the plugin, or a cell it did not expect.
- **Fix:** read the error logged after this line; report it to the plugin's author.

### SP-3013

**Plugin validate failed** · error · [SR-GRID](../records/0105_GRID.md) decision 17

- **Meaning:** a plugin's `validate` threw for a sheet; that sheet's errors from it were not updated.
- **Likely cause:** a bug in the plugin, or a rule it cannot read.
- **Fix:** read the error logged after this line; report it to the plugin's author.

### SP-3014

**Plugin overlay failed** · error · [SR-GRID](../records/0105_GRID.md) decision 19a

- **Meaning:** a plugin's `overlay` threw; its items are not drawn.
- **Likely cause:** a bug in the plugin, or a drawing it cannot place.
- **Fix:** read the error logged after this line; report it to the plugin's author.

### SP-3015

**Source could not be read** · error · [SR-GRID](../records/0105_GRID.md) decision 9 · `code: 'unreadable'`

- **Meaning:** the `src` URL (or `load(url)`) could not be fetched; the pane shows "Can't open this file".
- **Likely cause:** a 404 or 403; a cross-origin URL without CORS; invalid base64.
- **Fix:** check the URL opens in the browser and is same-origin or CORS-enabled.

---

## 4xxx · the errors element

`<sheetpane-errors>` raises no code yet; the range is held for it.

---

## 5xxx · plugins

### SP-5101

**Selection too large to format** · warning · [SR-NUMFMT](../records/0109_NUMFMT.md)

- **Meaning:** a number-format action reached its cell cap; only the first cells were formatted.
- **Likely cause:** a format applied to whole columns or a very large range.
- **Fix:** select the cells that hold data, and apply again.

### SP-5102

**Not a style sheet** · error · [SR-NUMFMT](../records/0109_NUMFMT.md)

- **Meaning:** `xl/styles.xml` holds no `<styleSheet>`, so number formats cannot be written.
- **Likely cause:** a damaged workbook, or a tool that wrote an empty styles part.
- **Fix:** re-save the workbook in Excel and export again.

### SP-5103

**Workbook has no style sheet** · error · [SR-NUMFMT](../records/0109_NUMFMT.md)

- **Meaning:** the package lacks its styles part, so number formats cannot be written.
- **Likely cause:** a minimal workbook written by a script.
- **Fix:** re-save the workbook in Excel, which adds the part.

### SP-5201

**Recalculation failed** · error · [SR-FORMULAS](../records/0111_FORMULAS.md)

- **Meaning:** the formula engine failed while recalculating; the saved values stay until the next workbook.
- **Likely cause:** a formula or function the engine cannot evaluate.
- **Fix:** read the error logged after this line; reload the workbook.

### SP-5202

**Formula engine did not load** · error · [SR-FORMULAS](../records/0111_FORMULAS.md)

- **Meaning:** the WASM engine could not be fetched or started (with `preload`).
- **Likely cause:** the `.wasm` file is not served, a wrong `wasm` option, or a CSP blocking WebAssembly.
- **Fix:** serve the engine's `.wasm`, pass its URL as `wasm`, and allow `wasm-unsafe-eval` in the CSP.

### SP-5701

**Chart part is not well-formed XML** · error · [SR-CHARTS](../records/0113_CHARTS.md)

- **Meaning:** a chart part cannot be parsed; the chart is not drawn.
- **Likely cause:** a damaged workbook.
- **Fix:** re-save the workbook in Excel.

### SP-5702

**Chart part holds no chart** · error · [SR-CHARTS](../records/0113_CHARTS.md)

- **Meaning:** a chart part has no `c:chart` element; the chart is not drawn.
- **Likely cause:** a chart type sheetpane does not read, or a damaged part.
- **Fix:** re-save the workbook in Excel; check the chart opens there.

### SP-5801

**Comment part has no container** · error · [SR-COMMENTS](../records/0112_COMMENTS.md)

- **Meaning:** a comments part the file already has lacks its root element, so it cannot be extended.
- **Likely cause:** a damaged comments or threaded-comments part.
- **Fix:** re-save the workbook in Excel; that sheet's comments are skipped (`unreadable-part`).

### SP-5802

**Not a worksheet** · error · [SR-COMMENTS](../records/0112_COMMENTS.md)

- **Meaning:** a sheet part has no `<worksheet>`, so comments cannot be anchored in it.
- **Likely cause:** a chart sheet or a damaged sheet part.
- **Fix:** comments live on worksheets only; that sheet's comments are skipped.

### SP-5803

**Comments not written for a sheet** · error · [SR-COMMENTS](../records/0112_COMMENTS.md)

- **Meaning:** writing one sheet's comments failed; the export goes on without them.
- **Likely cause:** SP-5801 or SP-5802 on that sheet, or an unexpected part.
- **Fix:** read the error logged after this line; the export report lists the skipped ids.

---

## 6xxx · column rules and the rules file

The rules engine (`packages/grid/src/pane/rules.ts`). A rules file never
throws: each problem is one `note` error, `author: 'host'`, with its `code`.

### SP-6001

**Column rule pattern is not a regular expression** · error · [SR-GRID](../records/0105_GRID.md) decision 22a · `TypeError`

- **Meaning:** a `pattern` in the element's `columns` does not compile.
- **Likely cause:** an unbalanced bracket or bad escape.
- **Fix:** test the pattern with `new RegExp(…)`; escape `\` once more inside a JS string.

### SP-6002

**Column-rules validate function failed** · error · [SR-GRID](../records/0105_GRID.md) decision 22c

- **Meaning:** the host's `validate(ctx, signal)` threw or rejected; that cell has no result.
- **Likely cause:** a bug in the host function, or a network call that failed.
- **Fix:** read the error logged after this line; return `null` rather than throw.

### SP-6003

**Value refused by a rule** · warning · [SR-GRID](../records/0105_GRID.md) decision 22b

- **Meaning:** a rule with `onInvalid: 'block'` refused a typed value; it is never stored. `sheetpane-editcancel` fires with `reason: 'blocked'` and this code.
- **Likely cause:** the value breaks the rule — the event's `message` says how.
- **Fix:** type a value the rule accepts, or set `onInvalid: 'flag'` to keep it as an error instead.

### SP-6010

**Rules file is not a JSON object** · note · [SR-GRID](../records/0105_GRID.md) decision 22d

- **Meaning:** the rules document is not an object; no rule from it is checked.
- **Likely cause:** an array, a string, or a number given as `rules`.
- **Fix:** give `{ "version": 1, "sheets": { … } }`.

### SP-6011

**Rules file could not be read** · note · [SR-GRID](../records/0105_GRID.md) decision 22d

- **Meaning:** `rules-src` could not be fetched or parsed; no rule from it is checked.
- **Likely cause:** a 404, CORS, or JSON that does not parse.
- **Fix:** open the URL in the browser and validate it against `@sheetpane/grid/rules.schema.json`.

### SP-6012

**Unknown rules file version** · note · [SR-GRID](../records/0105_GRID.md) decision 22d

- **Meaning:** `version` is not one this grid reads (1); no rule from it is checked.
- **Likely cause:** a missing `version`, or a file for a newer grid.
- **Fix:** set `"version": 1`.

### SP-6013

**Unknown key in the rules file** · note · [SR-GRID](../records/0105_GRID.md) decision 22d

- **Meaning:** a top-level or sheet-level key is not one the file defines; it is ignored.
- **Likely cause:** a typo (`colums`), or a key for a newer grid.
- **Fix:** top level: `$schema`, `version`, `sheets`; per sheet: `headerRow`, `columns`, `cells`.

### SP-6014

**Rules file has no sheets** · note · [SR-GRID](../records/0105_GRID.md) decision 22d

- **Meaning:** the file has no `sheets` object; no rule is checked.
- **Likely cause:** rules written at the top level.
- **Fix:** put them under `"sheets": { "*": { "columns": { … } } }`.

### SP-6015

**Rule is not an object** · note · [SR-GRID](../records/0105_GRID.md) decision 22d

- **Meaning:** a column rule, a cell rule or a sheet's rules is not an object; it is skipped.
- **Likely cause:** `"Age": 18` instead of `"Age": { "min": 18 }`.
- **Fix:** write each rule as an object of rule words.

### SP-6016

**Unknown rule word** · note · [SR-GRID](../records/0105_GRID.md) decision 22a

- **Meaning:** a rule names a word the vocabulary lacks; it is ignored.
- **Likely cause:** a typo (`requird`), or a word for a newer grid.
- **Fix:** use `required`, `type`, `min`, `max`, `minLength`, `maxLength`, `pattern`, `oneOf`, `noneOf`, `equals`, `unique`, `message`, `note`, `severity`, `onInvalid`.

### SP-6017

**Unknown rule type** · note · [SR-GRID](../records/0105_GRID.md) decision 22a

- **Meaning:** `type` is not one the engine checks.
- **Likely cause:** `"type": "string"` or `"float"`.
- **Fix:** use `text`, `number`, `integer`, `date` or `boolean`.

### SP-6018

**Rules file pattern is not a regular expression** · note · [SR-GRID](../records/0105_GRID.md) decision 22a

- **Meaning:** a `pattern` in the rules file does not compile; it is not tested.
- **Likely cause:** an unbalanced bracket, or a JSON escape eaten (`"\d"` must be `"\\d"`).
- **Fix:** escape backslashes twice in JSON.

### SP-6019

**Rule list is not a list** · note · [SR-GRID](../records/0105_GRID.md) decision 22a

- **Meaning:** `oneOf` or `noneOf` is not an array.
- **Likely cause:** `"oneOf": "Active"`.
- **Fix:** `"oneOf": ["Active", "Inactive"]`.

### SP-6020

**Header row is not a row number** · note · [SR-GRID](../records/0105_GRID.md) decision 22d

- **Meaning:** a sheet's `headerRow` is not a number of 1 or more; the default applies.
- **Likely cause:** `"headerRow": "2"` or `0`.
- **Fix:** `"headerRow": 2` (1-based).

### SP-6021

**Not a cell or a range** · note · [SR-GRID](../records/0105_GRID.md) decision 22d

- **Meaning:** a key under `cells` is not an A1 cell or range; its rule is skipped.
- **Likely cause:** `"A"`, `"1:1"`, or a typo.
- **Fix:** use `"B2"` or `"B2:B200"`.

### SP-6022

**Rules name a missing sheet** · note · [SR-GRID](../records/0105_GRID.md) decision 22d

- **Meaning:** the rules file names a sheet the workbook lacks; its rules are not checked.
- **Likely cause:** a renamed sheet, or rules written for another workbook.
- **Fix:** match the sheet's exact name, or use `"*"` for every sheet.

### SP-6023

**No column has this title** · note · [SR-GRID](../records/0105_GRID.md) decision 22a

- **Meaning:** a rule names a column title no sheet has in its header row; it is not checked.
- **Likely cause:** a renamed column, a different `header-row`, or a typo.
- **Fix:** match the title (trimmed, any case) or set `headerRow` / `header-row` to the row that holds it.

### SP-6024

**Two columns share a title** · note · [SR-GRID](../records/0105_GRID.md) decision 22a

- **Meaning:** a ruled title appears twice in the header row; only the first column is checked.
- **Likely cause:** a duplicated column, or two blank-looking titles.
- **Fix:** rename one column, or accept that the first is the one checked.

### SP-6025

**Rules file rule replaces the element’s** · note · [SR-GRID](../records/0105_GRID.md) decision 22d

- **Meaning:** the element's `columns` and the rules file both rule a title; the file's rule wins.
- **Likely cause:** rules kept in two places.
- **Fix:** keep the rule in one place.

---

## 7xxx · mcp

### SP-7001

**Tool input is missing or malformed** · error · [SR-MCP](../records/0119_MCP.md) decision 7

- **Meaning:** a tool was called without an argument it needs, or with one of the wrong kind.
- **Likely cause:** the agent left out `path`, `rules`, `code` or `task`, passed an empty string, or a task with no searchable words.
- **Fix:** call the tool again with the argument its input schema names (`tools/list` shows it).

### SP-7002

**No file at that path** · error · [SR-MCP](../records/0119_MCP.md) decision 7

- **Meaning:** the path given to `inspect_workbook`, `draft_rules` or `check_rules` names nothing.
- **Likely cause:** a typo, or a path relative to a different folder — relative paths are read from where the server runs.
- **Fix:** pass an absolute path, or one relative to the server's working directory.

### SP-7003

**File too large for the tool** · error · [SR-MCP](../records/0119_MCP.md) decision 7

- **Meaning:** the file is over the 256 MB the server reads.
- **Likely cause:** a very large export.
- **Fix:** inspect a smaller extract, or read it with `@sheetpane/import` in your own script.

### SP-7004

**Workbook could not be read** · error · [SR-MCP](../records/0119_MCP.md) decision 7

- **Meaning:** the import package failed on the file without one of its own SP-10xx codes.
- **Likely cause:** an internal failure while reading.
- **Fix:** report it with the file if you can share it; the reader's own refusals (SP-1001…SP-1007) are passed through with their codes.

### SP-7005

**No sheet by that name** · error · [SR-MCP](../records/0119_MCP.md) decision 7

- **Meaning:** `draft_rules` was asked for a sheet the workbook does not have.
- **Likely cause:** a misspelt or renamed sheet; names are matched exactly.
- **Fix:** use a name from the list in the message, or leave `sheet` out for every sheet.

### SP-7006

**Not a sheetpane code** · error · [SR-MCP](../records/0119_MCP.md) decision 7

- **Meaning:** `explain_code` was given something that is not in the registry.
- **Likely cause:** a typo, or a code from another library.
- **Fix:** codes look like `SP-1002`; the message lists nearby codes when there are any.

### SP-7007

**Server data file missing** · error · [SR-MCP](../records/0119_MCP.md) decision 7

- **Meaning:** the server could not find `ERRORS.md` beside it.
- **Likely cause:** an incomplete install, or a build run without its copy step.
- **Fix:** reinstall `@sheetpane/mcp`; from the repository, run `pnpm --filter @sheetpane/mcp build`.

<!-- source: records/0001_LAWS.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/main/records/0001_LAWS.md) -->

# SR-LAWS — the laws have exactly one home each

## §1 — For humans

Every law is stated in exactly one record, `SR-LAW-n`. This record assigns the
handle and points at the record; it carries none of the text, so there is
nothing here that can drift.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    H["handle Ln"] --> R["records/00NN_LAW-n-*.md"]
    R --> C["CLAUDE.md links, never restates"]
```

<details>
<summary><b>ASCII twin</b></summary>

```text
   handle Ln ---> records/00NN_LAW-n-*.md ---> CLAUDE.md links, never restates
```

</details>

## §2 — For agents

### Context

A law restated in two places is two laws the moment one is edited.

### Decision

1. **The handles and their homes:**

   | handle | record | one line |
   |---|---|---|
   | **L0** | [SR-LAW-0](0002_LAW-0-authority.md) | records are the only source of truth; Law records outrank every other record |
   | **L1** | [SR-LAW-1](0003_LAW-1-retired-records-archived.md) | a retired record is archived, never deleted |
   | **L2** | [SR-LAW-2](0004_LAW-2-foss-dependencies.md) | every dependency is free and open source |
   | **L3** | [SR-LAW-3](0005_LAW-3-xlsx-and-csv-only.md) | sheetpane supports XLSX and CSV only |
   | **L4** | [SR-LAW-4](0006_LAW-4-web-component.md) | sheetpane is always a web component |
   | **L5** | [SR-LAW-5](0007_LAW-5-host-font.md) | the font is the browser's default unless the host sets one |
   | **L6** | [SR-LAW-6](0008_LAW-6-edits-in-memory-export-with-changes.md) | every change is held in memory and export carries it |
   | **L7** | [SR-LAW-7](0009_LAW-7-surfaces-always-in-sync.md) | the view, edit and error components are always in sync |
   | **L8** | [SR-LAW-8](0010_LAW-8-npm-package.md) | sheetpane is consumed as an npm package |
   | **L9** | [SR-LAW-9](0011_LAW-9-memory-is-a-javascript-object.md) | memory means a JavaScript object, for now |

2. **A new law** takes the next handle and the next free number in the law
   range, on the decider's ruling named in its record; this table gains its row and
   `CLAUDE.md` §The laws its line, in the same change.
3. **A retired law** is written `ex-Ln`; the handle is never reused; the record
   is archived under L1.

### Consequences

Precedence is judgment, never a gate: no parser reads *does this contradict L0*.

### Alternatives considered

- One record holding every law's text — rejected: a change to one law would
  reopen all of them, and the record would be the longest file every session
  reads.

### Reference (required)

- [SR-LAW-0](0002_LAW-0-authority.md) decision 1 — one home per rule.

### Veto condition

**Reopen this decision if:** any live document other than a law's own record
carries a law's normative text.

**How to check it:** `grep -rn "L0 ·\|L1 ·\|L2 ·\|L3 ·\|L4 ·\|L5 ·\|L6 ·\|L7 ·\|L8 ·\|L9 ·" --include=*.md . | grep -v records/000`

---

## References

**Records** — [SR-LAW-0](0002_LAW-0-authority.md) · [SR-LAW-1](0003_LAW-1-retired-records-archived.md) · [SR-LAW-2](0004_LAW-2-foss-dependencies.md) · [SR-LAW-3](0005_LAW-3-xlsx-and-csv-only.md) · [SR-LAW-4](0006_LAW-4-web-component.md) · [SR-LAW-5](0007_LAW-5-host-font.md) · [SR-LAW-6](0008_LAW-6-edits-in-memory-export-with-changes.md) · [SR-LAW-7](0009_LAW-7-surfaces-always-in-sync.md) · [SR-LAW-8](0010_LAW-8-npm-package.md) · [SR-LAW-9](0011_LAW-9-memory-is-a-javascript-object.md)

<!-- source: records/0002_LAW-0-authority.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/main/records/0002_LAW-0-authority.md) -->

# SR-LAW-0 — L0, the records are the only source of truth

## §1 — For humans

**Every rule has one home: a record in `records/`.** `CLAUDE.md`, READMEs,
comments and skills link to that record and never restate it. A rule changes
in its record first.

**The restatement test:** *could this artifact and the record disagree while
both still look correct?* If yes, it is a restatement, and it is forbidden.

**Laws outrank every other record.** A sentence in a lower document that
conflicts with a Law is void, and is deleted on contact.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    R["a rule"] --> H["its one record in records/"]
    H --> A["CLAUDE.md · READMEs · comments: link, never restate"]
    L["Law records"] -. outrank .-> H
```

<details>
<summary><b>ASCII twin</b> — the same diagram, for terminals and diffs</summary>

```text
   a rule ---> its one record in records/ ---> CLAUDE.md, READMEs, comments
                     ^                          (link, never restate)
   Law records ......| outrank
```

</details>

---

## §2 — For agents

### Context

Rules copied into `CLAUDE.md` and READMEs drift from the records they copy:
one copy is edited, the other is not, and both still read as correct.
sheetpane starts with no code, so the authority is fixed before the first copy
can exist.

### Decision

1. **Source.** Every rule has exactly one home, a record. Every other artifact
   — `CLAUDE.md`, a README, a comment, a skill, a diagram — **links to it and
   never restates it**. A change is made in the record first.
1a. **The records are always up to date — in the change that makes them
   wrong.** Three obligations: (i) no behaviour change lands without its record
   updated in the **same commit**; (ii) a change that touches no recorded
   decision says so — `no SR affected`, on its own line of the commit message;
   (iii) before a session ends, re-read every record you changed code under.
   (i) and (ii) are enforced by the guard; (iii) is judgment and is the only
   thing covering coherence — a record can be amended into self-contradiction
   and every check passes.
2. **Precedence.** Law records outrank every other record. A record that
   conflicts with a Law is **void in the conflicting part** — a defect, never a
   trade-off.
2a. **On contact, the conflicting sentence is deleted from the lower document**
   — never softened, footnoted, or left beside a pointer.
3. **Amendment is entrenched.** A Law changes only on the decider's ruling, named in
   the record. An ordinary record a session may accept.
4. **The restatement test:** *could this artifact and the record disagree
   while both still look correct?* If yes it is a restatement and forbidden.
   If it would simply fail, it is an implementation (code naming a key) or an
   enforcement (a test, a hook) and permitted. Prose explaining *how* or *why*
   beside the code is permitted; a second statement of the rule is not.
5. **A generated view is permitted only while a test binds it byte-equal.**
   Remove the test and the view is an illegal restatement. (Not used by this
   bootstrap — tests are deferred — so `CLAUDE.md` links to the laws and
   carries none of their text.)

### Consequences

- **Enforced today:** obligations 1a (i)–(ii), by `scripts/sr-guard.sh` once
  the decider installs it as the `commit-msg` hook.
- **Judgment today:** obligation 1a (iii) — the only cover for coherence
  (backlog B-006, `cost`); precedence (2); the restatement test (4).
- `CLAUDE.md` carries pointers only; a generated law block waits for a test
  that binds it (decision 5).

### Alternatives considered

- Rules in `CLAUDE.md`, records as commentary — rejected: that is the drift
  this law ends.

### Reference (required)

- [`scripts/sr-guard.sh`](../scripts/sr-guard.sh) — the executable form of
  decision 1a (i)–(ii).

### Veto condition

**Reopen this decision if:** a rule's text is found in two live files.

**How to check it:** `grep -rln 'Every rule has exactly one home' --include=*.md . | grep -v '^./archive/'  # only records/0002 should print`

---

## References

*Every source this record cites, gathered in one place. An archived document
is never listed here.*

**Records** — [SR-LAWS](0001_LAWS.md) · [SR-WORK-OWNERSHIP](0058_WORK-ownership.md)

**Code**

- [`scripts/sr-guard.sh`](../scripts/sr-guard.sh)

<!-- source: records/0003_LAW-1-retired-records-archived.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/main/records/0003_LAW-1-retired-records-archived.md) -->

# SR-LAW-1 — L1, a retired record is archived, never deleted

## §1 — For humans

**A retired record is moved, never deleted.** It goes to `archive/records/` in
the same change, with a row in `archive/README.md`, `status: archived` and a
dated banner.

**Archived means named, never cited.** It may be mentioned with a link; it
never grounds a live claim.

**Superseded is different.** A superseded record is rewritten or deleted, and
its successor says what it replaced.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    R["records/NNNN_x.md"] -->|retired| A["archive/records/NNNN_x.md + map row"]
    R -->|superseded| S["rewritten in place, or deleted"]
```

<details>
<summary><b>ASCII twin</b> — the same diagram, for terminals and diffs</summary>

```text
   records/NNNN_x.md --retired----> archive/records/NNNN_x.md + map row
                     --superseded-> rewritten in place, or deleted
```

</details>

---

## §2 — For agents

### Context

Deleting a retired record loses why something was once true; leaving it in
`records/` lets it be cited as if live. Moving it keeps both the history and
the boundary.

### Decision

1. When a record's subject, rule or law is retired, the record is **moved** to
   `archive/records/`, mirroring its path, **in the same change** — with a row
   in `archive/README.md`, `status: archived`, and a top banner
   `ARCHIVED <date> — retired by <ruling>`.
2. An archived record may be **named, never cited** as grounding for a live
   claim.
3. A **superseded** record is different: it is rewritten or deleted in the
   change that supersedes it, and the successor says in prose what it replaced.
4. A retired law is written `ex-L<n>` in live text; its handle is never reused.

### Consequences

- **Judgment today:** all of it — nothing mechanical checks this law; the veto
  command is the manual check.
- A retired law's handle is never reused (decision 4).

### Alternatives considered

- Delete retired records — rejected: the reasoning is lost.
- Keep them in `records/` marked `archived` — rejected: they get cited as live.

### Reference (required)

- [`archive/README.md`](../archive/README.md) — the map every archived record
  gets a row in.
- [SR-WORK-ARCHIVE](0057_WORK-archive.md) — the archive's rules.

### Veto condition

**Reopen this decision if:** `archive/records/` holds a file without an `archive/README.md` row, or `records/` holds a `status: archived` file.

**How to check it:** `ls archive/records/; grep -l '^status: archived' records/*.md`

---

is never listed here.*

**Records** — [SR-LAW-0](0002_LAW-0-authority.md) · [SR-WORK-ARCHIVE](0057_WORK-archive.md)

**Project docs**

- [`archive/README.md`](../archive/README.md)

<!-- source: records/0004_LAW-2-foss-dependencies.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/main/records/0004_LAW-2-foss-dependencies.md) -->

# SR-LAW-2 — L2, every dependency is free and open source

## §1 — For humans

**Every dependency is FOSS.** Nothing enters sheetpane's dependency tree unless
the exact version resolved is released under a free and open source licence.

**"Every" means every.** Runtime, peer, optional and dev dependencies, and
every transitive one under them. Vendored or copied third-party code counts as
a dependency.

**Not FOSS, not allowed.** Source-available, "fair source", Commons Clause,
BSL, SSPL, freeware, and code with no licence at all are all out.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    D["a candidate dependency"] --> Q{"resolved version under an OSI-approved licence?"}
    Q -->|yes| A["allowed"]
    Q -->|no| R["refused — find a FOSS alternative or build it"]
```

<details>
<summary><b>ASCII twin</b> — the same diagram, for terminals and diffs</summary>

```text
   a candidate dependency ---> resolved version under an OSI-approved licence?
                                   |-- yes --> allowed
                                   '-- no ---> refused: find a FOSS alternative or build it
```

</details>

---

## §2 — For agents

### Context

sheetpane is an npm package other teams ship inside their own apps. A
non-free licence anywhere in its tree becomes their legal problem. The
decider ruled on 2026-10-18 that every dependency is free and open source.

### Decision

1. **Every dependency is FOSS** — runtime, peer, optional, dev, and every
   transitive dependency of each.
2. **FOSS means** the exact version resolved is released under a licence on
   the OSI-approved list. A dual-licensed package qualifies only if one of its
   licences for that version is on the list.
3. **Not FOSS:** source-available, "fair source", Commons Clause, BSL, SSPL,
   freeware, proprietary, and no licence at all (`UNLICENSED`, or no licence
   file).
4. **Vendored or copied third-party code is a dependency** under this law — a
   copied file, a CDN script, a pasted snippet.
5. **A licence that changes** to non-FOSS in a later version: the dependency
   is pinned below that version or removed, in the change that notices.

### Consequences

- **Judgment today:** nothing checks this law yet — the
  `package.json` files exist (W-04) but run no licence check. The licence check is backlog B-008 (`ungated`).
- **Copyleft (ruled 2026-10-18, "resolve all the blockers"):** GPL, AGPL and
  LGPL are not allowed in `dependencies` or `peerDependencies` of either
  package — a copyleft runtime dependency would bind every host app; they are
  allowed in `devDependencies`. Today both packages have no runtime
  dependencies at all, so the rule costs nothing.

### Alternatives considered

- Permissive licences only, everywhere — rejected: dev tooling may be copyleft
  without binding a host; the ruling draws the line at runtime and peer.
- Allow source-available packages case by case — rejected by the ruling.

### Reference (required)

- The decider's ruling, 2026-10-18 session — `work/WORKLOG.md`, the entry of
  that date titled "laws L2 and L3 filed".
- The OSI-approved licence list — https://opensource.org/licenses

### Veto condition

**Reopen this decision if:** any resolved dependency carries a licence that is
not on the OSI-approved list.

**How to check it:** `test -f pnpm-lock.yaml && pnpm licenses list --prod || echo "no dependencies yet"`

---

*Every source this record cites, gathered in one place. An archived document
is never listed here.*

**Records** — [SR-LAWS](0001_LAWS.md) · [SR-LAW-0](0002_LAW-0-authority.md)

**Project docs**

- [`work/BACKLOG.md`](../work/BACKLOG.md) — B-008
- [`work/WORKLOG.md`](../work/WORKLOG.md)

**External**

- OSI-approved licences — https://opensource.org/licenses

<!-- source: records/0005_LAW-3-xlsx-and-csv-only.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/main/records/0005_LAW-3-xlsx-and-csv-only.md) -->

# SR-LAW-3 — L3, sheetpane supports XLSX and CSV only

## §1 — For humans

**Two formats, no more.** sheetpane reads and writes `.xlsx` and `.csv`.
Nothing else.

**Everything else is out** — `.xls`, `.xlsm`, `.xlsb`, `.ods`, `.numbers`,
Google Sheets. Not parsed, not written, not half-supported.

**"Right now" is the point.** This is a scope law. Adding a format is a ruling
by the decider that rewrites this record — never a quiet addition in code.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    F["a file"] --> Q{"XLSX or CSV?"}
    Q -->|yes| S["open · view · edit · save"]
    Q -->|no| O["not accepted — out of scope"]
```

<details>
<summary><b>ASCII twin</b> — the same diagram, for terminals and diffs</summary>

```text
   a file ---> XLSX or CSV?
                 |-- yes --> open, view, edit, save
                 '-- no ---> not accepted: out of scope
```

</details>

---

## §2 — For agents

### Context

A spreadsheet library can grow a parser per format and support none of them
well. The decider ruled on 2026-10-18 that sheetpane supports XLSX and CSV,
and only those, for now.

### Decision

1. **Supported formats are exactly two:**

   | format | extension | standard |
   |---|---|---|
   | XLSX | `.xlsx` | Office Open XML spreadsheet (ECMA-376) |
   | CSV | `.csv` | comma-separated values (RFC 4180) |

2. **Supported means both directions** — open and view, edit, save and export.
3. **Every other format is out of scope:** no parser, no writer, no partial
   path, no "best effort". That includes `.xls`, `.xlsm`, `.xlsb`, `.ods`,
   `.numbers` and Google Sheets.
4. **A new format is a ruling, not a commit.** It enters only by the decider
   rewriting decision 1 (L0 decision 3).

### Consequences

- How an unsupported file is refused (error shape, message) is a component
  decision, owed by the first record that owns the file-loading code.
- **Checked today:** `@sheetpane/import` refuses every other extension and an
  OLE or mismatched file before parsing, with a typed error (SR-IMPORT
  decision 6, `edge.test.ts`); the grid shows the refusal (SR-GRID tests).
- **Delimiter variants (ruled 2026-10-18, "resolve all the blockers"):** a
  `.csv` file may use `,` `;` or tab and is read with the delimiter detected;
  export defaults to `,` with `;` and tab as options. The `.tsv` extension stays
  refused — CSV is the format, the delimiter is a dialect. Detail:
  [`work/compare/xlsx-csv-reading.compare.md`](../work/compare/xlsx-csv-reading.compare.md).

### Alternatives considered

- Support every format the parsing library offers — rejected by the ruling:
  each format is a surface to test and maintain.
- XLSX only — rejected by the ruling: CSV is in.

### Reference (required)

- The decider's ruling, 2026-10-18 session — `work/WORKLOG.md`, the entry of
  that date titled "laws L2 and L3 filed".
- RFC 4180 — https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4180

### Veto condition

**Reopen this decision if:** live code names a spreadsheet extension other than
`.xlsx` or `.csv`.

**How to check it:** `grep -rnE '\.(xls|xlsm|xlsb|ods|numbers|tsv)\b' --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=archive --exclude-dir=records --exclude-dir=work . || echo clean`

is never listed here.*

**Project docs**

- [SR-GRID](0105_GRID.md) · [SR-IMPORT](0104_IMPORT.md) · [SR-ERRORS](0106_ERRORS.md) — the checks
- [`work/WORKLOG.md`](../work/WORKLOG.md)

**External**

- RFC 4180 — https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4180
- ECMA-376 — https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-376/
