<!-- source: records/0105_GRID.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/main/records/0105_GRID.md) -->

# SR-GRID — @sheetpane/grid

## §1 — For humans

**One workbook per pane, shared by every element.** `<sheetpane-excel
pane="q3">` and `<sheetpane-errors pane="q3">` find the same in-memory
workbook by the `pane` id, wherever they sit on the page. Everything — the
cells, every change, every error, the selected cell, the mode — lives there,
so the two are always in step (L7).

**The sheet shows the file as stored and edits it in memory.** View or Edit,
in a tab or a pop-up; every change is held in memory and Export writes it
into a copy of the uploaded file, which is never touched (L6). It draws only
the rows on screen, so a 250,000-row file scrolls at full frame rate.

**Plugins add features through named doors, not by reaching in.** Six hooks
(format, decorate, derive, validate, overlay, exportPatch) and six slots
(format row, selection bar, cell bar, status line, cell, overlay). With no
plugin the grid is the plain review tool the design shows.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    H["host page"] -->|"pane=\"q3\""| X["&lt;sheetpane-excel&gt;"]
    H -->|"pane=\"q3\""| E["&lt;sheetpane-errors&gt;"]
    X <--> S[("WorkbookStore<br/>book · changes · errors · selection · mode · undo")]
    E <--> S
    S -->|read| I["@sheetpane/import"]
    S -->|"patchXlsx · toCsv"| O["@sheetpane/export"]
    P["plugins: six hooks"] --> S
    P -->|"controls in six slots"| X
```

<details>
<summary><b>ASCII twin</b> — the same diagram, for terminals and diffs</summary>

```text
   host page --pane="q3"--> <sheetpane-excel>  <-->  ( WorkbookStore )  <-->  <sheetpane-errors> <--pane="q3"-- host
                                                     book · changes · errors · selection · mode · undo
                             reads files through @sheetpane/import; exports through @sheetpane/export
   plugins --six hooks--> store ; --controls in six slots--> the sheet
```

</details>

---

## §2 — For agents

### Context

W-01 asked for the sheet and the workbook it shares; W-14 for the plugin
host; W-23 for undo; W-24 for freeze panes. The decisions they build on are
the grid, contract, plugins and testing verdicts in `work/compare/`.

### Decision — the store

1. **`createWorkbook({ plugins })` → `WorkbookStore`**, framework-free:
   `subscribe(fn)`, `getSnapshot()` (immutable; a new object per change, with
   a `version`), `on(fn)` for store events. One store per `pane` id from a
   module registry, created by the first element that names it and released
   when the last one disconnects; an element with no `pane` gets its own; a
   host may assign a store to `el.workbook`.
2. **Snapshot:** `load` (`empty` · `loading` · `ready` · `error` with the
   reader's code and `detail`), `source` (name, kind, size, the uploaded bytes
   — never modified — and the read time), `book` (the `ImportedWorkbook`),
   `changes`, `derived`, `errors`, `selection`, `mode`, `composing`,
   `canUndo`, `canRedo`. Selection and mode are shared (contract decision 2);
   scroll, zoom, find and form drafts are per element.
3. **Changes:** a map `sheet!ref → { kind, was, now }` with kinds `value`,
   `style`, `numFmt`, `formula`, `merge`, `freeze` (freeze keys are
   `sheet!#freeze`). `setCell` parses typed text as the cell stores it (a
   number stays a number in `.xlsx`; a `.csv` cell stays text); typing the
   uploaded value back removes the change. `setChange` serves plugin kinds
   and `setChanges` a batch as one undo step; `revert` removes every kind at
   a cell. **`style` and `numFmt` have their own slot**
   (`sheet!#style:A1`, `sheet!#numFmt:A1` — `kindRef`, `baseRef`), so a value
   edit, a style and a format on one cell are three changes; `changeOf(sheet,
   ref, kind?)` and `changesAt` read them. The change count is the map's size.
4. **Every mutation goes through one commit:** the undo entry, `matchesExpected`
   recomputed, one notification, then `validate` for the touched sheets and
   `derive` for the touched cells.
5. **Errors** are SheetpaneError v1, exactly the contract verdict's schema:
   ids `ERR-0001…`, never reused in a session (a restored review moves the
   counter past its highest id); `found` frozen from the uploaded display text
   (`(blank)` when empty; `row N` for a row range); a matching edit sets
   `matchesExpected`, never resolves; deleting an error keeps a cell change it
   made; "Also change the cell" writes `expected` in as a change in the same
   undo step; `isStale` flags a saved error whose cell no longer shows `found`.
6. **Export:** `exportFile({ options })` — `options` (from the element's
   `export(options)`, e.g. `{ comments: false }`) reach every `exportPatch`
   hook as `ctx.exportOptions`; `.xlsx`: `patchXlsx(upload, value changes,
   { exportPatch: plugin hooks, freeze })`; `.csv`: `toCsv` of the sheet with
   its changes, in the detected delimiter. `exportChanges()` and
   `currentRows()` are public.
7. **Undo / redo (W-23):** one stack per pane, 500 entries; an entry holds the
   state of `changes` and `errors` before and after; typing in one cell is one
   entry (coalesced until Enter, Tab, Esc or blur); selection and mode are not
   undone; ids stay reserved; undo re-runs `derive` and `validate`;
   `setErrors()` is a host restore, not a user action, and clears the stack
   with a `history` event; it then re-runs `validate`, which adopts a
   restored error only when its sheet, range, type and author match a draft
   (ids alone never match: a restored person's error with a reused id is
   never overwritten).
8. **Stale marks (W-01 DoD 15):** with no `derive` plugin, a formula cell whose
   formula reads a changed cell (`formulaRefs`) is "may be stale".

### Decision — `<sheetpane-excel>`

9. **The element** registers on import where `customElements` exists; open
   shadow root; plain DOM. Attributes `pane`, `src` (URL — read with a GET,
   nothing is sent — data URL or base64), `mode`, `display` (`tab` ·
   `popup`), `open`, `author`, `plugins`; properties `workbook`, `errors`,
   `errorTypes`, `file`, `mode`, `open`, `src`; methods `load()`, `export()`,
   `select()`, `getErrors()`, `setErrors()`, `undo()`, `redo()`,
   `shortcuts()`, `column()`; attribute `header-row` (default 1); events
   `sheetpane-load`, `-change {sheet, ref, kind, was, now}`, `-errors
   {errors, plugins}`, `-select {sheet, ref, range, column, value}` (`range`
   when more than one cell is selected; it fires when the selection settles —
   a drag fires once, on release), `-editstart
   {…, value}` (cancellable: the cell stays read-only), `-input {…, draft,
   was}`, `-beforechange {…, was, now}` (cancellable: the value is refused
   before the change map, undo, derive or validate see it), `-editcancel`,
   `-sheet {sheet}`, every payload naming `column: {index, letter, header}`
   (W-26, the events verdict); `-mode`, `-history`,
   `-close`, `-export {blob, kind, name, guarded, format, converted,
   original?}` (cancelable: the Download control downloads only when no
   listener prevents it; `original: true` when it hands back the file as
   opened; `converted` when the format differs from the upload's), all
   bubbling and
   composed. An action's event fires once, on the element where it happened;
   an action with no element fires on the pane's first sheet. Setting `src`
   to `null`, `undefined` or `''` removes the attribute (React 19 sets
   properties); setting `workbook` applies the element's `mode` to it, as
   connecting does; `export(options?, { format?, sheet? })` converts when the
   format differs (`store.exportFile`: `.xlsx` → `.csv` is one sheet's
   `latestRows()`, `.csv` → `.xlsx` one sheet with numeric text as numbers,
   the upload's base name kept). `package.json` declares `dist/index.js` a side effect, so a
   bundler keeps `import '@sheetpane/grid'` and its registration.
9a. **Committed test hooks (W-41)** — public API a host's tests rely on;
    renaming one is a breaking change: cells `role="gridcell"` with
    `data-sp-ref="B3"`; sheet tabs `role="tab"` with `data-sp-sheet`; the cell
    bar input `data-sp="cell-input"`; `data-sp="download"`,
    `"download-menu"`, `"undo"`, `"redo"`, `"flag"` (the docked Flag issue);
    the context menu `data-sp="menu"` (`role="menu"`), the callout
    `data-sp="callout"`, the inline form `data-sp="composer"` and its
    `data-sp="add-error"`; in `<sheetpane-errors>` each row
    `data-sp-error="<id>"` and `data-sp-ref="<sheet>!<range>"`, its
    `data-sp="resolve"`, the form's `data-sp="add-error"`, and the form fields
    `data-field="type" | "message" | "expected"`; the column headers
    `data-hc="<index>"`, row headers `data-hr="<index>"`, the corner
    `data-hall` and the status line's totals `data-sp="totals"` (W-46).
    `@sheetpane/testing`
    (SR-TESTING) uses only these, roles and labels.
10. **Layout:** toolbar (file, kind and size, View/Edit, open counts, find,
    zoom, undo, redo, freeze, change count, **Download** — a neutral split
    button in View and Edit (W-34): the main part in the upload's format with
    the change count as a neutral badge; **▾** (`aria-label="Choose download
    format"`) opens a `role="menu"`: Download as .xlsx / .csv, the upload's
    first and marked *default*, a line under the other saying what it holds,
    then — under a separator — each plugin's `exportOptions` as
    `menuitemcheckbox`es; Esc returns focus to ▾ — keyboard help, close in a pop-up), cell bar (ending in the
    docked selection actions, decision 13), the format row, the grid,
    sheet tabs (`.xlsx` only; hidden sheets italic), status line. States: the
    upload drop zone (file, link, base64), reading, "Can’t open this file",
    "Password protected" (no unlocking — the reader cannot decrypt).
11. **The grid:** DOM cells, rows absolutely placed, only the visible rows
    (±20) and — past 60 columns — the visible columns; merged ranges drawn
    once, also when they start above or left of the window; column headers,
    row headers, frozen rows and frozen columns are `position: sticky`. Rows
    are 28 px, headers 24 px, the row-header column 52 px, at 100 %. **Zoom
    scales the geometry and the font size**, not a CSS transform (see
    *Alternatives*). Column widths come from the file (Excel character units
    × 7 + 5 px), else from the text in the first 200 rows of a CSV.
11a. **The cell bar edits a draft:** Enter, Tab and blur commit it through
    `sheetpane-beforechange`; Esc restores it (`sheetpane-editcancel`).
    Paste (Ctrl/⌘+V, Edit) writes tab- and line-separated text from the
    active cell: `beforechange` once per cell, refused cells skipped, the
    rest one undo step (`store.setCells`); one value pasted over a range fills
    every cell of it the same way (W-46). Delete or Backspace over a range
    clears every filled cell through `beforechange`, refused cells skipped,
    one undo step. Over 1,000,000 cells nothing is pasted, and the status line
    says why. There is no fill gesture yet.
11b. **Range selection (W-46):** the selection is drawn by **one layer**, never
    per cell — over the range a fill (`--sp-accent-soft`) with the active cell
    left unfilled (an even-odd hole), one 2 px `--sp-accent` border on the
    range's own edges, and the active cell's 2 px ring; the copied range a
    dashed border. The scrolling part sits in `.sellayer` (above cell and
    conditional fills, below pins, marks and pictures, and below plugin
    `cell` controls); across frozen panes it splits — the frozen-column part
    sticks left in the layer, the frozen-row parts are bands inside the frozen
    rows. A selection change re-creates no cell: only the layer, the header
    tints (`--sp-accent-soft` with an accent edge on the spanned columns and
    rows), `aria-selected` on rendered cells, the cell bar and the status
    line change. **The pointer:** mouse and pen use Pointer Events with
    pointer capture — the drag survives leaving the grid; within 24 px of the
    scrolling pane's edge, or past it, the grid autoscrolls, faster the
    further out; the layer redraws once per frame and the store hears of the
    drag once, on release (Esc restores the selection from before it). A
    range that partly covers a merge grows to cover it. A press on a plugin
    mark or a right-click is not a drag. A finger pans; its tap selects; a
    range then shows two round handles (24 px) to extend it from the other
    corner. **Headers:** a column header selects the column, a row header the
    row, the corner the sheet; dragging across headers or Shift+click
    extends; the active cell is the first visible cell. While dragging, the
    cell bar shows `6R × 3C`; when a drag or a key extension settles, a polite
    live region says "B3 to D8, 18 cells". **Totals:** with two or more cells
    selected the status line shows `Count n · Sum x · Average y` over the
    numeric cells (Count alone with no number), in the active cell's number
    format when a `format` plugin is installed, else locale grouping —
    computed when the selection settles, never per frame. One range at a
    time: Ctrl/⌘+click ranges and a fill handle are not built.
12. **Keyboard (APG grid):** focus stays on the `role="grid"` element and
    `aria-activedescendant` names the active cell; arrows, Shift+arrows,
    Home/End, Ctrl+Home/End, PageUp/PageDown; Ctrl/⌘+arrow jumps to the edge
    of the data (Excel's rule), with Shift extends there; Ctrl+Space selects
    the column, Shift+Space the row; Ctrl/⌘+A the data region, again the
    sheet; Shift+Backspace collapses to the active cell; inside a range Enter,
    Shift+Enter, Tab and Shift+Tab move the active cell within it and wrap;
    otherwise Enter or F2 edits; a printable
    key replaces the cell; Delete clears (a range: decision 11a); F flags; Esc
    cancels the innermost thing — a drag, a menu, the form, find, the copied
    outline — or closes the pop-up; Ctrl/⌘+Z, Ctrl+Y, ⌘+Shift+Z; Ctrl/⌘+C copies;
    Shift+F10 and the Menu key open the selection actions (decision 13).
    `aria-rowcount` / `aria-colcount` give the sheet's true size.
13. **Review — nothing floats over the cells (W-31):** the selection actions
    are **docked at the right end of the cell bar** — Flag issue with its F
    hint (Edit, a cell with no error), the `selbar` plugin controls (Edit),
    then **⋯** (View and Edit) opening Copy ref and Copy value — **Copy
    values** for a range, written as `text/plain` TSV and a `text/html`
    table so Excel and Sheets paste a grid (over 1,000,000 cells nothing is
    copied); Copy ref gives `B3`, `B3:D8`, `B:D`, `4:12` or the sheet's name
    (W-46); the group
    hides while the cell-bar draft is edited and while composing, and at a
    narrow cell bar (≤ 720 px) the plugin buttons fold into ⋯ before Flag
    issue moves. **Right-click, Shift+F10 and the Menu key** on a cell select
    it and open the same actions as a `role="menu"` just under it (Flag
    issue · Copy ref · Copy value · the `selbar` controls); arrows move, Enter
    runs, Esc closes and returns focus to the grid; the browser's menu is
    suppressed on cells only. A copy without a secure context says so in the
    status line. **Download** (decision 10): the main part's file is the
    original bytes when untouched (no change, and no review a plugin would
    write), else `export()` with the menu's plugin options, the change count
    on the button and in its tooltip. Also: numbered pins (✓ when resolved) and row glyphs ✕ ! i; the callout (Found →
    Should be, message, tags, Resolve/Reopen, Delete, previous/next); Flag
    issue sets `composing` and the inline form opens **only when no
    `<sheetpane-errors>` is connected to the pane** (contract decision 4).
14. **Placement:** `display="popup"` moves the root into a modal `<dialog>`
    (`open` shows it); Esc and the close button close it, dispatch
    `sheetpane-close` and return focus.
15. **Font (L5):** no font family anywhere; tokens are `--sp-*` on `:host`;
    every control is `font: inherit`; a change of the host's font shows at
    once. The cell text size is `--sp-cell-font-size` (default `.93em`).
15a. **Theme (W-29):** both elements take `theme` = `light` (the default) ·
    `dark` · `auto` (follows `prefers-color-scheme`), also a `theme`
    property. `TOKENS` (light) and `DARK_TOKENS` (every colour, as hex — no
    `color-mix()` at runtime) are exported; the tokens are `ground`,
    `surface`, `sunken`, `cell`, `head`, `grid`, `line`, `line-strong`, `ink`,
    `ink-2`, `ink-3`, `accent`, `accent-ink`, `accent-soft`, `pass`, `fail`,
    `warn` and `changed` (each with `-soft`), `note`, `ref-1`…`ref-3`,
    `on-solid`, `hit`, `hit-current`, the radii and two shadows. The grid's
    CSS names no colour literal. A host's `--sp-*` on the element wins.
    **The file's colours are data:** a `decorate` result (styles, condfmt,
    chart fills) renders as saved in both themes. Contrast in both themes:
    text 4.5:1 on its ground; glyphs, pins, the changed mark, reference
    colours and the focus ring 3:1 on the cell.
15b. **Cell layout:** a cell is a one-column flex box holding its text in
    `<span class="v">`, so `text-align`, wrapping and `vertical-align` (mapped
    to `justify-content`) from `decorate` show; the state tints (range,
    find hits, error marks) are `::before` overlays above a `decorate` fill,
    never instead of it; the changed corner carries a cell-coloured outline.
16. **`beforeunload`** warns while the pane holds changes.

### Decision — the plugin host (W-14)

17. **A plugin** is `{ id, provides, after?, format?, decorate?, derive?,
    validate?, overlay?, exportPatch?, controls?, exportOptions? }`
    (`exportOptions`: `{ key, label, default }` switches shown in the Download
    menu, reaching `exportPatch` as `ctx.exportOptions[key]` — W-34). `format` and `derive`
    have one provider per pane (a second throws, naming both); a provided hook
    without its function throws; `decorate` providers run in `after` order,
    later winning per property, and a result naming `font-family` throws;
    `validate` errors keyed by plugin, sheet, range and type — a
    `workbook`- or `host`-authored error resolves itself when the cell passes
    and reopens when it fails again (W-18, W-27; people's errors never do); `file` errors never do;
    `overlay` items are placed in sheet space under the pins with a
    `Geometry`; `exportPatch` runs inside `patchXlsx` after the core.
18. **Registration:** `registerPlugin(id, factory)` (a package does it on
    import); the `plugins` attribute names the enabled ids — an unknown id
    throws; the set is fixed per pane at creation.
19. **Slots:** controls `{ id, slot, group, label, icon?, shortcut?, mode,
    isActive?, disabled?, labelFor?, run?, text?, appliesTo?, options?,
    value?, choose?, cellOptions? }` (a button's `aria-label` and `title`
    both name its shortcut) render as labelled buttons — or a labelled `<select>`
    when the control has `options` and `choose` — in group
    order — `format-row` (Edit only, shown only when a plugin or the host's
    light-DOM `<slot name="format-row">` puts something in it), `selbar`
    (docked in the cell bar and an item in the context menu, decision 13),
    `cellbar`, `status` (text), `cell` (a mark in cells `appliesTo` accepts),
    `overlay`. Duplicate ids throw. Shortcuts run from the grid and are listed
    in the keyboard help. A `cell` control with `cellOptions` opens a menu of
    choices at the cell; picking calls `choose` (W-18's list arrow). A
    control with `text` and no `run` outside `status` renders as read-only
    dashed text (W-16's `fx` in View), absent when the text is empty.
19a. **Overlay items** are rendered once per `sheet|id` and kept while the
    workbook stays; loading a workbook drops every one. Each pass re-reads an
    item's `alt` (its name may change) and `role` (`img`, the default, or
    `group` for an item holding controls); `passThrough` lets pointer events
    reach the cells below. The `Geometry` keeps growing past the drawn
    columns (64 px a column), and the grid widens to the far cell of every
    drawing anchor (up to 26 columns past the data).
19b. **Machine-authored errors** (`author` `workbook`, `file` or `host`) are
    read-only in both elements; `workbook` and `host` ones resolve themselves
    when the cell passes and reopen with `found` refreshed; their pin is a
    square ⚠ at the range's right edge; `BUILTIN_TYPE_NAMES` names their
    types. `validate` re-runs on every sheet after every change and after
    `derive`. A typed formula reads as its derived result. The grid
    re-exports `@sheetpane/export`'s `shiftFormula` for plugins whose rules
    are written against a range's top-left (validation, condfmt). The grid widens to
    the columns validation and conditional-format ranges name (up to 26 past
    the data). Alt+↓ opens a cell control's menu.
20. **Derived cells** are drawn with a mark and never enter the change map or
    the count.

### Decision — column rules (W-27)

22. **Column rules** (events verdict decisions 5–14) are the pane's, set by
    `<sheetpane-excel>`'s `columns`, `validate` and `onInvalid` (attribute
    `on-invalid`) or `store.setColumnRules({ columns, validate, onInvalid,
    headerRow })`; `header-row` gives the titles. They run as a **built-in
    `validate` provider** (`host-rules`, outside the frozen plugin set);
    their errors are `type: 'column-rule'`, `author: 'host'`, `expected` the
    rule in words (`describeRule`), the message naming the column and the
    rule (`Age: must be at least 18 (min)`) unless the rule gives one.
22a. **Vocabulary:** `required`, `type` (`text` · `number` · `integer` ·
    `date` · `boolean`), `min`, `max`, `minLength`, `maxLength`, `pattern`
    (not tested over 10,000 characters; on the element an invalid one throws
    at once, in a rules file it is a note), `oneOf`, `noneOf` (values never
    valid), `equals` (the one valid value; a blank fails it), `unique`,
    `message`, `note` (for the maintainer, never the message), `severity`,
    `onInvalid` (W-33 added `noneOf`, `equals`, `note`). Titles match trimmed
    and case-insensitive, an exact title first. A title the file lacks is one
    `note`; a duplicated title checks the first column plus one `note`.
22b. **Findings are cached per cell** and updated for the cells a commit or
    undo touches (a `unique` column re-checks the rows sharing the old and
    new value; a title-row edit re-runs everything), so `validate` stays
    cheap. **`load`** checks every row in 8 ms slices with the progress in
    the status line (`store.ruleProgress`). **`input`** (`store.checkInput`)
    runs 150 ms after typing stops: an outline and a message at the cell bar,
    nothing stored. **`commit`:** `flag` stores and adds an error; `block`
    (`store.ruleBlocks`, checked inside the element's `beforechange` gate)
    refuses the value and fires `sheetpane-editcancel {reason: 'blocked',
    message}` — only a JSON rule or a synchronous result can block.
22c. **`validate(ctx, signal)`** runs for every cell of a titled column;
    `ctx.rowValues` is keyed by title and an edit asks its whole row again; a
    newer check on a cell aborts the older (`signal`) and a stale result is
    dropped. Setting the rules again re-checks every row and removes host
    errors no longer produced; people's errors are never touched; a rule
    never edits a cell. `<sheetpane-errors>`' author filter shows "Column
    rules" ("Rules file" when a rules file is in force).
22d. **The rules file (W-33):** a JSON document `{ version: 1, sheets: {
    "*" | <sheet name>: { headerRow?, columns?, cells? } } }` — `"*"` for
    every sheet, a named sheet's rule for the same title winning, `cells` by A1
    cell or range (`type: 'cell-rule'`, a cell rule over more than 10,000
    cells checked only where the sheet has data). Given as the `rules`
    property or read from `rules-src` (a GET, like `src` — B-030 applies
    alike); setting either re-checks every row. It compiles into the same
    `host-rules` provider (no second checker): merged over the element's
    `columns` (the file's rule wins for a title, with a note). Checked by hand,
    no schema library: an unknown key, word, type or version, a sheet, title or
    cell the workbook lacks, a bad ref or pattern is one `note` each (keyed, so
    several share a cell — `ErrorDraft.key`); an unknown version applies no
    rule; nothing throws. `@sheetpane/grid/rules.schema.json` (JSON Schema
    2020-12) ships for editors. The load phase yields on `requestIdleCallback`
    (idle-time chunks), reads cells by position and allocates nothing per cell
    it passes.
22e. **`flagging="off"` (W-33)** (also the `flagging` property; the pane's
    `store.flagging`): no Flag issue in the cell bar or the context menu, no
    `F` key or its help line, no composer (a host's `compose()` is cancelled),
    no callout card; a cell's error mark stays and selecting it marks its row
    in `<sheetpane-errors>`. Default `on`.

### Decision — freeze panes (W-24)

20a. **`setChanges(list)`** applies many plugin-kind changes as one undo step
    (a format applied to a range).
21a. **Merged ranges are core:** `store.merges(sheet)` is the file's merges
    with `merge` changes applied (key `sheet!#merge:A1:C1`, `now` true or
    false; `setMerge()` makes one, undoable); the grid draws them; export
    rewrites that sheet's `<mergeCells>` (SR-EXPORT). A plugin's merge
    control only calls `setMerge()`.
21b. **Formula input:** with a `derive` plugin installed, a typed value
    starting `=` is a change of kind `formula` (W-16 evaluates and exports it);
    without one it is text. With one, the cell bar's input in Edit holds the
    cell's formula (`store.formula()`, `store.input()`), and retyping the
    file's own formula restores the cell. A `DerivedChange` with `clear: true`
    removes a cell's derived entry.
21. The reader's `freeze` is the starting point; Freeze / Unfreeze in Edit
    freezes the rows above and the columns left of the selected cell, as a
    change of kind `freeze` with its own undo entry — a toolbar button, not a
    format-row control. Export writes `<pane>` through `patchXlsx`'s `freeze`
    option (SR-EXPORT). Arrow keys move through frozen and scrolling cells as
    one grid.

**The element contract's machine form (W-37):** `custom-elements.json`
(Custom Elements Manifest 2.1.0, at the package root and exported) is
generated from the source by `scripts/build-manifest.mjs` — the tags from
`define()`, attributes from `observedAttributes` plus `theme` (set only
through `:host([theme])`), the class TSDoc's Attributes list, `@fires`,
`@slot` (`format-row`; `selbar` is a plugin control slot, not an HTML slot)
and `@csspart` (excel: `root` `toolbar` `cellbar` `format-row` `status`
`dialog`; errors: `root`), public members from the built `.d.ts`, and the
`--sp-*` tokens with their defaults. From it come VS Code HTML/CSS custom
data and JetBrains `web-types.json` (in `dist/`), and the framework typings
`@sheetpane/grid/jsx` (React 19), `/vue`, `/svelte` and `/solid` (type-only;
the `onInvalid` property is left out of framework props, which read `on…` as
listeners — the `on-invalid` attribute does its job). `test/manifest.test.ts`
fails when the manifest, the typings or the editor data drift from the code.
Angular uses `CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA` (README); there is no Angular package.

**Codes (W-40):** `LoadState` and `sheetpane-load`'s refusal carry `spCode`; a blocked edit's `sheetpane-editcancel` carries `code: 'SP-6003'`; every rules note (22d) carries `code` (SP-60xx); a plugin hook's failure is logged as SP-3012 to SP-3014 (SR-CODES).

### Consequences

- **Enforced today** (`just test-pkg grid`, Chromium per push, WebKit and
  Firefox nightly): store tests (changes, undo with a fast-check property and
  the cap, errors, export round-trip property, freeze, stale marks); element
  tests (contract, states, edit, export, flag, keyboard, font, pop-up, axe on
  View and Edit); plugin-host tests (a fake plugin per hook, the throwing
  rules, slots, shortcuts, the no-plugin grid); undo across elements; freeze
  rendering; the L7 sync test; `actions.test.ts` (W-31: nothing floats
  after a click, the docked order in View and Edit, folding at a narrow
  width, the context menu by mouse and keyboard, the copy notice, one
  Download button, an untouched workbook downloaded byte for byte);
  `selection.test.ts` (W-46: the layer's geometry for a cell, a range, a
  frozen split and a merge; no cell re-created on a selection change (a
  MutationObserver); a drag told to the store once; autoscroll past the
  edge; header and corner clicks; every key; the copied TSV and HTML; a
  range Delete as one undo step; one value pasted over a range; the totals;
  `aria-selected`; the announcement; axe with a range in View and Edit; a
  5 s drag with autoscroll on 250,000 rows — 301 frames, worst 16.8 ms at a
  16.7 ms vsync, none dropped, Chromium 156 headless, 10 cores, load average
  ~4, reported); `theme.test.ts` (every token has a hex dark
  value, the contrast table in both themes, the attribute restyling chrome
  while a `decorate` fill stays as saved, a host override winning);
  `rules.test.ts` (the four-column example: every rule kind, commit, undo,
  `unique`, `setErrors`, sync and async `validate` with aborts, headers,
  `header-row`, rules changed after load, the input phase, flag and block in
  the element, the Column rules filter, 250,000 rows); `rules-file.test.ts`
  (W-33: `*` vs named sheets, columns, cells and ranges, `equals`, `noneOf`,
  the document's notes, an unknown version, merging with `columns`,
  `rules-src`, the JSON Schema against the README example and the demos'
  file, `flagging="off"` end to end, 250,000 rows).
- **Measured** (Arpit's MacBook, headless Chromium 156, 10 cores, 2026-10-18):
  the 250,000-row CSV loads in 173–194 ms; a 5-second scroll at 900 px per
  frame paints 301 frames, none dropped, no long task — with and without two
  frozen rows. Headless and programmatic, not a wheel in headed Chrome.
- **Measured — column rules** (Arpit's MacBook, headless Chromium 156, load
  average ≈ 5, 2026-10-18): a 250,000-row CSV with four rules (required,
  pattern + unique, integer range, oneOf) — read 250 ms, then every row
  checked in 1.3 s across 79 painted frames, the longest gap 44 ms (the
  `unique` index is built in one go).
- **Measured — the rules file** (the same machine, load ≈ 2.5): the README
  file over 250,000 rows — from `Accounts.csv` (read 107 ms) every row checked
  in 0.72 s over 44 frames, the longest gap 18 ms; from `.xlsx` (read 5.6 s)
  0.88 s, 18 ms. An earlier build that read the text of every cell and kept a
  `Set` per distinct value showed one 140–410 ms collection pause; both were
  removed.
- **Owed:** files saved by Excel, Google Sheets, LibreOffice and Numbers, opened
  by the grid and read with their frozen panes — W-30 (the decider's files).
- **SR-LAW-6's veto command lists one hit:** the `src` loader's `fetch(` in
  `packages/grid/src/excel/element.ts` — a read, with nothing sent (backlog
  B-030).

### Alternatives considered

- **Zoom by CSS `transform`** (grid verdict decision 1) — rejected in the
  build: sticky headers and frozen panes inside a transformed layer are placed
  by the main thread while the compositor scrolls, so they jitter. Scaling the
  geometry keeps `position: sticky` exact; re-rendering the window is cheap.
- Roving `tabindex` on cells — rejected for `aria-activedescendant`: the
  virtualiser replaces cells while scrolling and would drop focus.
- One element per cell kept between frames — rejected: string rendering of
  the window measured well inside the frame budget.
- A provider element — rejected by the contract verdict.

### Reference (required)

- [`packages/grid/src/`](../packages/grid/src/) · [`packages/grid/test/`](../packages/grid/test/)
- [`work/compare/grid-rendering.compare.md`](../work/compare/grid-rendering.compare.md) · [`workbook-and-error-contract.compare.md`](../work/compare/workbook-and-error-contract.compare.md) · [`plugins.compare.md`](../work/compare/plugins.compare.md)

### Veto condition

**Reopen this decision if:** two elements on one pane are seen out of step, a
plugin needs a seventh hook, or the 250,000-row scroll drops frames on the
reference machine.

**How to check it:** `just test-pkg grid`

<!-- source: records/0106_ERRORS.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/main/records/0106_ERRORS.md) -->

# SR-ERRORS — <sheetpane-errors>

## §1 — For humans

**The reviewer's checklist, anywhere on the page.** The host puts
`<sheetpane-errors pane="q3">` beside the sheet, in a side column, in another
tab or inside a pop-up. It lists every error flagged on the workbook — what
was found, what it should be — and holds the form that **Flag issue** opens.

**It is never out of step.** It keeps nothing of its own: an error added,
resolved or deleted here shows in the sheet at once, and the reverse (L7).
There is no "linked" chip and no export footer — it is always linked.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    S[("the pane's workbook")] --> L["list: filter · pick · Show in sheet · Resolve · Delete"]
    S --> F["New error form (when Flag issue fires)"]
    L --> S
    F -->|Add error| S
    L -->|sheetpane-reveal| H["host switches tab / opens the pop-up"]
```

<details>
<summary><b>ASCII twin</b> — the same diagram, for terminals and diffs</summary>

```text
   ( pane's workbook ) --> list (filter, pick, Show in sheet, Resolve, Delete) --> workbook
                       --> New error form (Flag issue) --Add error--> workbook
   list --sheetpane-reveal--> host switches tab / opens the pop-up
```

</details>

---

## §2 — For agents

### Context

W-02 asked for the error component, always linked to the sheet. The schema,
the store and the contract are the contract verdict's and
[SR-GRID](0105_GRID.md)'s; this record owns the element.

### Decision

1. **The element** registers on import; attributes `pane`, `readonly`,
   `author`, `plugins`, `theme` (SR-GRID decision 15a); properties `workbook`, `errors`, `errorTypes`,
   `readOnly`, `theme`; methods `getErrors()`, `setErrors(list, { plugins? })`; events
   `sheetpane-errors {errors, plugins}`, `sheetpane-change`,
   `sheetpane-select`, `sheetpane-history`, `sheetpane-reveal {error}` —
   bubbling, composed; an action's event fires on the element where it
   happened.
2. **No private copy:** every render reads the store. Connecting registers the
   element with the store, so Flag issue opens the form here and not in the
   sheet; disconnecting releases it.
3. **The list:** "n open"; severity filter (All · ✕ · ! · i, each with its
   count) and — when errors come from more than people — an author filter
   (People · Workbook rules · Column rules — "Rules file" when the pane has
   a rules file, its rows then grouped by sheet — · File comments); rows open first then resolved,
   by number; each row shows the number (✓ when resolved), the type's name,
   Found → Should be, the range and severity, and tags (cell changed ·
   resolved · matches suggestion · stale). Picking a row selects its cell
   (selection syncs) and expands it: the message, author and time, **Show in
   sheet**, Resolve / Reopen, Delete.
4. **Show in sheet** selects the cell and dispatches `sheetpane-reveal
   {error}`, so the host can switch tab or open the pop-up.
5. **The form** (while the pane is composing, in Edit, and never when the
   pane is `flagging="off"` — SR-GRID 22e): the cell, Found (the
   uploaded text), Column (the header text found above, and the letter), Row
   (number and first value); type chips from `errorTypes` (each with its
   default severity); What’s wrong; What it should be; **Also change the cell
   to this value**; severity Error / Warning / Note with its help line; the
   chosen type's example; Add error (⌘/Ctrl+↵) and Cancel (Esc). A
   `duplicate-row` error covers the whole row.
6. **`errorTypes`** defaults to the seven types and Other from the board
   `Edit-Examples` (`DEFAULT_ERROR_TYPES`, SR-GRID).
7. **`readonly`** hides the form, Resolve, Delete, Undo and Redo — a sign-off
   screen. Errors authored `workbook`, `file` or `host` are always read-only
   (SR-GRID decision 19b) and named from `BUILTIN_TYPE_NAMES` when the
   host's `errorTypes` does not name their type.
8. **A saved review** restored with a different plugin set shows the
   "formatted differently" notice (plugins verdict decision 3).
9. **Undo / Redo** buttons and Ctrl/⌘+Z, Ctrl+Y, ⌘+Shift+Z act on the pane's
   one stack (W-23).
10. **Font (L5):** no font family; every control is `font: inherit`.
    Severity is a glyph and a colour, never colour alone.

11. **Codes (W-40, SR-CODES):** `SheetpaneError` gains an optional `code`
    (`SP-xxxx`, additive to v1); a machine-authored note from the rules engine
    always sets it, and the expanded row shows it beside the author and time.

12. **Test hooks (W-41):** rows carry `data-sp-error` and `data-sp-ref`; Resolve `data-sp="resolve"`; the form's Add `data-sp="add-error"` (SR-GRID decision 9a lists them all).

### Consequences

- **Enforced today:** `packages/grid/test/errors.test.ts` (form, list,
  filters, reveal, readonly, `errorTypes`, events, notice, font, axe) and the
  L7 sync test in both mount orders with the errors element inside a
  `<dialog>`; the undo-across-elements test in `plugins.test.ts`.

### Alternatives considered

- A linked / not-linked chip and an export footer — removed by the decider
  (2026-10-18): the element is always linked, and export belongs to the sheet.

### Reference (required)

- [`packages/grid/src/errors/element.ts`](../packages/grid/src/errors/element.ts)
- [`work/compare/workbook-and-error-contract.compare.md`](../work/compare/workbook-and-error-contract.compare.md)

### Veto condition

**Reopen this decision if:** the errors element is ever seen showing an error
the sheet does not, or the reverse.

**How to check it:** `just test-pkg grid -t "always in sync"`

<!-- source: records/0107_IMAGES.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/main/records/0107_IMAGES.md) -->

# SR-IMAGES — @sheetpane/images

## §1 — For humans

**The pictures in a workbook show where the author put them.** With
`@sheetpane/images` on a pane, every picture a sheet anchors — a logo, a
signature, a photo — is drawn over the grid at its cells, scrolls with them
and sits under the error pins. It is view only: pictures are never changed,
and export keeps them exactly as they were.

**Nothing is decoded until it is needed.** A picture is read from the file
only when it scrolls near the screen; a format the browser cannot show (EMF,
WMF) gets a labelled frame instead.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    I["@sheetpane/import: drawings (anchors + media paths)"] --> P["images(): overlay hook"]
    G["the grid's Geometry"] --> P
    P --> O["OverlayItem: rect + <img> (blob: URL, lazy) or a frame"]
    O --> V["drawn under the pins, in sheet space"]
```

<details>
<summary><b>ASCII twin</b> — the same diagram, for terminals and diffs</summary>

```text
   import: drawings (anchors + media) --+
   the grid's Geometry -----------------+--> images(): overlay --> rect + <img> (lazy blob: URL) or a frame --> under the pins
```

</details>

---

## §2 — For agents

### Context

W-20 asked for the first `overlay` provider; the plugins verdict made
pictures a plugin and view only. The reader exposes drawing anchors and the
media parts (SR-IMPORT decision 2).

### Decision

1. **`images()`** → `{ id: 'images', provides: ['overlay'] }`; importing the
   package registers `images` (`sideEffects` names the entry). No `./ui`
   entry; one `status` control: "N pictures · M preview unavailable".
2. **Items:** each `picture` drawing of the sheet is one `OverlayItem`
   (charts and shapes are skipped; a picture without media or with no area
   is skipped). Ids carry a workbook generation, so a cached element is never
   reused across workbooks. `alt` and the image's `alt` come from `descr`,
   else the name.
3. **Anchors** (`src/anchors.ts`, public, DOM-free — `@sheetpane/charts`
   imports it): 9,525 EMU per pixel; `twoCell` from/to with offsets, `oneCell`
   from + `ext`, `absolute` `pos` + `ext`, placed in the **grid's** `Geometry`
   (28 px rows; hidden rows and columns shown, as the grid shows them), not in
   Excel's row heights. An offset is clamped to its own cell.
4. **Media** (`src/media.ts`, the one file that makes object URLs): read
   through `book.part()` only when the item nears the viewport
   (IntersectionObserver, 300 px margin); the format sniffed from the bytes,
   the extension as fallback; PNG, JPEG, GIF, BMP, WebP and SVG shown through
   `<img>` (never inline SVG); one URL per part.
5. **No preview:** EMF, WMF, TIFF, bytes that do not decode and a missing part
   show a frame "name — preview unavailable" at the anchor's size, without
   reading the bytes when the extension already says so.
6. **Lifetime:** every URL is revoked, once, when the pane loads another
   workbook or a load fails; a decode still running then makes no URL.
7. **Interaction:** in Edit a click on a picture selects the cell under the
   click; in View it does nothing.
8. **Export:** nothing — patch mode copies drawing and media parts byte for
   byte (SR-EXPORT). Deleting rows does not re-anchor pictures (there is no
   row deletion in v1).

### Consequences

- **Enforced today:** `just test-pkg images` — 29 tests (anchor arithmetic;
  rects against the rendered cells for every anchor type and at 150 % zoom;
  decode of each raster format; the EMF frame; URL revocation; click to
  select), Chromium per push, WebKit locally green.
- **Owed:** pictures from files saved by Excel and LibreOffice, and positions
  compared with Excel's own rendering — W-30 (the decider's files). Because the
  grid's rows are 28 px, a picture in a file with taller or shorter rows sits
  differently than in Excel (decision 3).
- **A store that is dropped without loading another workbook keeps its URLs
  until the page goes** — the plugin contract has no dispose signal.

### Alternatives considered

- Excel's row heights and hidden rows for placement — rejected: the grid does
  not draw them, and a picture must sit on the cells the user sees.
- `data:` URLs — rejected: the bytes would live as strings for the page's life.
- Inline SVG — rejected: file-supplied markup in the page.
- Decoding at load — rejected: a 20 MB photo should cost nothing off screen.

### Reference (required)

- [`packages/images/src/`](../packages/images/src/) · [`packages/images/test/`](../packages/images/test/)
- [`work/compare/plugins.compare.md`](../work/compare/plugins.compare.md) — the `overlay` hook.

### Veto condition

**Reopen this decision if:** a picture's frame stops matching the cells its
anchor names in the grid, or a URL outlives its workbook.

**How to check it:** `just test-pkg images`

---

- [`packages/images/src/index.ts`](../packages/images/src/index.ts) · [`anchors.ts`](../packages/images/src/anchors.ts) · [`media.ts`](../packages/images/src/media.ts)

**Project docs**

<!-- source: records/0108_VALIDATION.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/main/records/0108_VALIDATION.md) -->

# SR-VALIDATION — @sheetpane/validation

## §1 — For humans

**The file's own rules find the wrong cells before a person does.** A
workbook that says "Units must be a whole number above 0" or "Status is one of
Core, Income, Cap" gets every breaking cell listed in `<sheetpane-errors>` as
a warning from the workbook, on load and after every edit.

**They clear themselves.** Fix the cell and the warning resolves; break it
again and it reopens. They are the workbook's, so a person cannot resolve or
delete them. A list rule gives the cell a ▾ in Edit with the allowed values.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    R["<dataValidations> (import)"] --> V["validation(): validate hook"]
    S["the pane's cells (live)"] --> V
    V -->|one warning per failing cell, author workbook| E["the error list · ⚠ pins"]
    U["ui(): ▾ list arrow · status count"] --> S
```

<details>
<summary><b>ASCII twin</b> — the same diagram, for terminals and diffs</summary>

```text
   <dataValidations> + live cells --> validation(): validate --> one warning per failing cell (author: workbook)
                                                                  --> error list, ⚠ pins
   ui(): list arrow ▾ (sets the cell), status count
```

</details>

---

## §2 — For agents

### Context

W-18 asked for the workbook's validation rules to land in the error pane; the
plugins verdict put them on the `validate` hook as workbook-authored errors
(SR-GRID decision 17).

### Decision

1. **`validation({ severity? })`** → `{ id: 'validation', provides: ['validate'] }`;
   `@sheetpane/validation` registers it, `@sheetpane/validation/ui` registers
   it with `ui()` (`validation-ui`: a `cell` list arrow and a `status` count).
   No runtime dependency.
2. **One error per failing cell:** `type: 'validation'`, severity `warning`
   (the host may choose another), `author: 'workbook'`, `range` = the cell,
   `found` = its current text (`(blank)` when empty), `expected` = the rule in
   words, `message` = the rule's `errorTitle: error` (either alone), else the
   rule in words. When a cell breaks several rules, the first counts.
3. **Rule types:** `whole`, `decimal`, `date`, `time`, `textLength` with all
   eight operators (default `between`, inclusive); `list` from a literal, a
   range, another sheet's range, a defined name, or the x14 form; `custom`
   only through a `derive` provider exposing a synchronous `evaluate(formula,
   { sheet, ref })`, relative references shifted per cell —
   `@sheetpane/formulas` provides it (SR-FORMULAS decision 8).
4. **Operands:** numbers, quoted text, `DATE` / `TIME` with numeric
   arguments, cell references (relative parts shift from the rule's first
   cell, through `@sheetpane/export`'s `shiftFormula`, re-exported by the
   grid) and defined names; anything else skips the rule and counts it.
5. **Values:** number rules need a number (`whole` an integer); text dates are
   not parsed; `textLength` uses the stored value's length; a list matches
   text ignoring case and a number by value. Blank cells pass with
   `allowBlank`. Only the used range (data plus changed cells) is checked.
   `showErrorMessage="0"` rules still check.
6. **Lifecycle (SR-GRID):** errors appear on load, re-check on every sheet
   after every change and after `derive`, resolve themselves when the cell
   passes and reopen (with `found` refreshed) when it fails again; they are
   read-only, drawn with a square ⚠ pin at the cell's right edge, filterable
   as "Workbook rules", named "Workbook rule".
7. **Skipped rules:** `skippedRules(book | store)` returns what was not
   checked and why (`custom`, `operand`, `operator`, `type`, `source`); the
   status line shows "n validation warnings · k rules not checked". It is not
   in `sheetpane-load`'s detail — the plugin contract has no way to add to a
   core event (B-032).
8. **List arrow:** in Edit, on cells a `list` rule covers — even past the data,
   the grid widens to the columns rules name — by mouse or Alt+↓; the choices
   are re-read live; a pick sets the cell (undoable). `showDropDown` (Excel's
   "hide the arrow") is read by the importer and not yet honoured.

### Consequences

- **Enforced today:** `just test-pkg validation` — 30 tests (every type and
  operator, list sources, x14, relative operands, live limits, resolve /
  reopen / undo, the arrow and its menu, the shared error pane with the
  author filter, a `custom` rule evaluated by IronCalc through
  `@sheetpane/formulas`), plus SR-GRID's core tests for read-only rows, the ⚠ pin and
  cross-sheet re-validation.
- **Owed:** a fixture with every rule type saved by Excel — W-30.

### Alternatives considered

- A formula engine of its own for operands — rejected: it would duplicate W-16.
- Flagging blanks under whole-column rules — rejected: a million rows.
- Severity from Excel's `errorStyle` — rejected: the spec fixes `warning`; the
  host chooses.

### Reference (required)

- [`packages/validation/src/`](../packages/validation/src/) · [`packages/validation/test/`](../packages/validation/test/)
- [`work/compare/plugins.compare.md`](../work/compare/plugins.compare.md) — `validate`.

### Veto condition

**Reopen this decision if:** a cell that breaks a supported rule is not
listed, or a listed workbook error stays open after the cell passes.

**How to check it:** `just test-pkg validation`

---

## References

*Every source this record cites, gathered in one place. An archived document
is never listed here.*

**Records** — [SR-GRID](0105_GRID.md) · [SR-ERRORS](0106_ERRORS.md) · [SR-IMPORT](0104_IMPORT.md)

**Code**

<!-- source: records/0109_NUMFMT.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/main/records/0109_NUMFMT.md) -->

# SR-NUMFMT — @sheetpane/numfmt

## §1 — For humans

**Numbers look the way Excel shows them.** Without this plugin the grid
formats dates, percentages and fixed decimals and shows anything else as
stored. With it, every format a workbook uses — currency, accounting,
fractions, elapsed time, conditional sections, locales — renders as in Excel.

**And a reviewer can change one.** In Edit a dropdown and ± decimals set a
cell's format; the change is held in memory like any other, undoable, and
export writes it into the file.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    C["a numeric cell + its format code"] --> F["numfmt(): format hook → numfmt 4.0.1"]
    F -->|text| G["the grid"]
    F -->|library rejects the code| S["core subset (fallback, counted)"]
    U["ui(): dropdown · ± decimals"] -->|numFmt change| X["exportPatch: <numFmt> + <xf>, cells repointed"]
```

<details>
<summary><b>ASCII twin</b> — the same diagram, for terminals and diffs</summary>

```text
   numeric cell + code --> numfmt(): format --> numfmt 4.0.1 --> text in the grid
                                         \--> rejected code: the core subset (counted)
   ui(): dropdown, ± decimals --> numFmt change --> exportPatch: <numFmt> + <xf>, cells repointed
```

</details>

---

## §2 — For agents

### Context

W-15 asked for the full ECMA-376 format grammar through the
[`numfmt`](https://github.com/borgar/numfmt) library (MIT, zero
dependencies), replacing the core subset (SR-IMPORT decision 4) when
installed — the plugins verdict's `format` hook.

### Decision

1. **`numfmt(options?)`** → `{ id: 'numfmt', provides: ['format',
   'decorate', 'exportPatch'] }`; `ui()` (`numfmt-ui`) carries the controls.
   Importing `@sheetpane/numfmt` registers `numfmt` alone; `@sheetpane/numfmt/ui`
   registers `[numfmt(), ui()]`. The headless entry never imports the UI.
   Runtime: the peer `@sheetpane/grid` and `numfmt@4.0.1`, pinned.
2. **The code** for a cell is the user's `numFmt` change, else its
   `cellXfs[s].numFmtId` — the file's `<numFmts>` entry first, else the
   library's built-in for that id in the locale (so ids 5–8, 14–22, 41–44
   follow it, as in Excel).
3. **Output:** finite numbers only; out-of-range dates show `########`;
   `General` follows Excel's 11-character rule.
4. **1904:** a code that shows a year, month or day gets the serial shifted by
   1,462 days; elapsed `[h]` formats are not shifted.
5. **Locale:** `options.locale`, else `document.documentElement.lang` read
   when formatting (guarded for Node); `-IN` territories group `3,2`.
6. **Fallback:** a code the library rejects returns nothing, so the core
   subset shows the cell; the cell is counted in `plugin.fallbacks()`. The
   count is not in `sheetpane-load`'s detail (backlog B-032).
7. **`decorate`** only sets `white-space: pre` for codes with `_`, `*` or `?`
   padding — never a font.
8. **UI:** a `format-row` dropdown (General · Number · Currency · Accounting ·
   Date · Time · Percentage · Fraction · Scientific · Text · Custom…) and ±
   decimals; a choice applies to the selection's numeric cells as **one undo
   step** (`setChanges`), each a `numFmt` change whose `was` is the file's own
   code; Custom… asks for a code (`ui({ ask })`, default `prompt`) and
   refuses an invalid one. The change lives in the cell's `numFmt` slot
   (`sheet!#numFmt:A1`, SR-GRID decision 3), so a value edit and a format on
   one cell are two changes. The cell bar keeps showing the raw value.
9. **Export:** `exportPatch` appends deduplicated `<numFmt>` (new ids from
   max(163, existing) + 1; a built-in code uses its id) and `<xf>` entries — a
   copy of the cell's old xf with the new `numFmtId` — and repoints each
   changed cell's `s`, inserting a missing `<c>` or `<row>`.

### Consequences

- **Codes (W-40, SR-CODES):** SP-5101 (a selection too large to format, a warning), SP-5102 / SP-5103 (no usable style sheet on export).
- **Enforced today:** `just test-pkg numfmt` — 42 tests (every built-in id
  and 50 custom codes through load → text; 1904; fallback; locales `de-DE`,
  `en-IN`; the dropdown, ranges, ± decimals, Custom…; export and read-back;
  package shape and the headless boundary). The table also found five bugs
  in the core subset; two are fixed (month-only codes, serial 0) and three
  are recorded as limits in SR-IMPORT.
- **Owed:** expected values captured from Excel itself (the table follows
  Excel's documented output) — W-30.
- **The reading verdict's "1 in 100" trigger** compares misreads; the one
  fixture cell where the subset and the library differ (`[$€-407]#,##0.00`)
  is a code the subset declines and shows raw, not a misread.

### Alternatives considered

- `addLocale` for `en-IN` — rejected: global state shared by every pane.
- A copy of the core subset for fallback — rejected: returning nothing reuses
  the core's.
- `[Red]` colours through `decorate` — left for a follow-up (dark-theme
  contrast, W-29).

### Reference (required)

- [`packages/numfmt/src/`](../packages/numfmt/src/) · [`packages/numfmt/test/`](../packages/numfmt/test/)
- [`work/compare/plugins.compare.md`](../work/compare/plugins.compare.md) — the `format` hook.

### Veto condition

**Reopen this decision if:** the library misformats more than 1 in 100
numeric cells across the real-app fixtures (W-30), or a code Excel accepts is
refused.

**How to check it:** `just test-pkg numfmt`

---

**Code**

- [`packages/numfmt/src/index.ts`](../packages/numfmt/src/index.ts) · [`fmt.ts`](../packages/numfmt/src/fmt.ts) · [`patch.ts`](../packages/numfmt/src/patch.ts) · [`ui.ts`](../packages/numfmt/src/ui.ts)

**Project docs**

- [`work/compare/plugins.compare.md`](../work/compare/plugins.compare.md) · [`work/reference/design/boards/Plugin-Numfmt.dc.html`](../work/reference/design/boards/Plugin-Numfmt.dc.html)

<!-- source: records/0110_STYLES.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/main/records/0110_STYLES.md) -->

# SR-STYLES — @sheetpane/styles

## §1 — For humans

**Cells look the way the file formats them.** Without this plugin the grid
draws every cell plain. With it, fills, bold, italic, underline, colours,
sizes, borders and alignment show as saved — in the host's own font, always.

**And a reviewer can restyle them.** In Edit a format row (and Bold · Fill ·
Merge on the selection bar) restyles the selection; each action is one change
per cell, one undo step, and export writes it into the file.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    X["cellXfs[s] → fonts · fills · borders · alignment"] --> D["styles(): decorate → allow-listed CSS"]
    C["the reviewer's style change (sheet!#style:A1)"] --> D
    D --> G["the grid (file colours kept in both themes)"]
    U["ui(): format row · selbar"] -->|style change, one undo step| C
    C --> E["exportPatch: <font>/<fill>/<border>/<xf> appended, s repointed"]
```

<details>
<summary><b>ASCII twin</b> — the same diagram, for terminals and diffs</summary>

```text
   cellXfs[s] (fonts, fills, borders, alignment) --> styles(): decorate --> allow-listed CSS --> grid
   reviewer's style change (sheet!#style:A1)      --/
   ui(): format row, selbar --style change, one undo step--> change map
   change map --> exportPatch: <font>/<fill>/<border>/<xf> appended, cells' s repointed
```

</details>

---

## §2 — For agents

### Context

W-17 asked for the styles plugin on the plugins verdict's `decorate` hook,
with the format row the Plugin-Styles board draws. Merges are core (SR-GRID);
the number format is SR-NUMFMT's.

### Decision

1. **`styles({ fileStyles? })`** → `{ id: 'styles', provides: ['decorate',
   'exportPatch'] }`; `ui(options?)` (`styles-ui`) carries the controls.
   Importing `@sheetpane/styles` registers `styles` alone;
   `@sheetpane/styles/ui` registers `[styles(), ui()]`. The headless entry
   never imports the UI. No runtime dependency; `@sheetpane/grid` is a peer.
2. **`decorate`** reads `cellXfs[s]` → `fonts`, `fills`, `borders`,
   `alignment` and returns only `background-color`, `color`, `font-weight`,
   `font-style`, `font-size`, `text-decoration`, `text-align`,
   `vertical-align`, `white-space` and `border-top/right/bottom/left` —
   **never `font-family`** (the host refuses one, SR-GRID 17). Colours: ARGB,
   theme with Excel's tint (the file's theme, else Office's), indexed (the
   file's `<indexedColors>`, else the 64-colour default), `auto`.
3. **The default font's size and colour are the host's:** only a size or
   colour that differs from the workbook's default font is drawn (size as
   `sz / default` of the grid's size), so a plain cell stays plain in both
   themes. A filled cell with automatic text gets the workbook's default ink.
   Patterns blend by density; a gradient shows its midpoint; diagonal
   borders, indent and rotation are not drawn.
4. **File colours are data** (SR-GRID 15a): they render as saved in light and
   dark; the grid's state tints sit above them (SR-GRID 15b).
5. **The change** is kind `style` in the cell's style slot
   (`sheet!#style:A1`, SR-GRID 3); `now` is a `StylePatch` (`clear`, `b`,
   `i`, `u`, `strike`, `color`, `fill`, `border`, `align`, `valign`,
   `wrap`). Fields the file already shows are dropped; a cell back to its file
   look has no change; `clear` drops the file's font, fill, border and
   alignment and keeps the number format.
6. **UI:** `format-row` groups text (Bold `Mod+B`, Italic `Mod+I`, Underline
   `Mod+U`, Strikethrough `Mod+5`) · colour · fill · border · align (left,
   centre, right with `Mod+Shift+L/E/R`; top, middle, bottom; Merge/Unmerge)
   · wrap · clear (`Mod+\`); `selbar` (docked in the cell bar and in the right-click menu, SR-GRID 13) adds Bold, Fill and Merge/Unmerge. Every
   action restyles the selection as **one undo step** (`setChanges`). Merge
   calls the core's `setMerge` (kind `merge`), is labelled Merge or Unmerge,
   and is disabled on a CSV or a single unmerged cell. `ui({ colours, fills,
   highlight })` sets the swatches; the default fills keep the changed mark at
   3:1.
7. **Export:** `exportPatch` appends deduplicated `<font>`, `<fill>`,
   `<border>` and `<xf>` entries (counts updated, every other byte kept),
   repoints `s` on each changed cell (adding `<c r s/>` and `<row>` where
   missing), and creates `styles.xml` with its relationship and content type
   when the package has none. Untouched cells keep their `s`; a workbook
   without style changes is left byte for byte. A CSV is never restyled.
8. **For condfmt (W-19):** the colour and CSS helpers (`resolveColor`,
   `applyTint`, `paletteOf`, `fontCss`, `fillCss` with `{ dxf: true }`,
   `borderCss`, `alignmentCss`, `dxfCss`, `ALLOWED_PROPS`, `allowListed`)
   are exported.

### Consequences

- **Enforced today:** `just test-pkg styles` — 46 tests (colours: rgb, theme
  and tint, indexed; decorate from the ExcelJS fixture property by property
  and from hand-made `styles.xml` for every border style, alignment, font and
  fill; the allow-list and the L5 veto over the package; the format row in
  View and Edit, every group, shortcuts, one undo step; merges; the core
  layout showing alignment and wrap with tints above a fill; contrast of the
  changed mark on every default fill; export round-trips, dedup, missing
  `styles.xml`, byte-for-byte when untouched).
- **Owed:** a fixture of every fill, font and border combination **saved by
  Excel** — W-30.

### Alternatives considered

- One change per cell for value and style — replaced by per-kind slots
  (SR-GRID 3): a value edit and a restyle of one cell are two changes.
- Drawing the default font's size and colour — rejected: a dark host would
  get dark-on-dark text in every plain cell.

### Reference (required)

- [`packages/styles/src/`](../packages/styles/src/) · [`packages/styles/test/`](../packages/styles/test/)
- [`work/compare/plugins.compare.md`](../work/compare/plugins.compare.md) — the `decorate` hook

### Veto condition

**Reopen this decision if:** a cell in a real-app fixture (W-30) renders a
fill, font or border property differently from Excel, or any decorate result
names a font family.

**How to check it:** `just test-pkg styles`

<!-- source: records/0111_FORMULAS.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/main/records/0111_FORMULAS.md) -->

# SR-FORMULAS — @sheetpane/formulas

## §1 — For humans

**Edit a number, and the totals follow.** Without this plugin a formula cell
shows the value Excel saved, marked stale once its inputs change. With it,
IronCalc recalculates every formula that depends on the edit; those cells are
marked ⟳ and are never counted as the reviewer's changes.

**A reviewer can type a formula.** In Edit the cell bar holds the cell's
formula; typing `=` makes a formula change that evaluates at once and is
written into the file with its new value.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    S["the store (changes + file)"] -->|derive: load / change| F["formulas(): IronCalc model (a cache)"]
    F -->|cells whose value changed| D["derived (⟳, not changes)"]
    D --> G["the grid · validation · status"]
    F -->|exportPatch| X["<f> + new <v>, fullCalcOnLoad=1"]
```

<details>
<summary><b>ASCII twin</b> — the same diagram, for terminals and diffs</summary>

```text
   store (changes + file) --derive--> formulas(): IronCalc model (a cache)
   model --cells whose value changed--> derived (marked, never changes) --> grid, validation, status
   model --exportPatch--> <f> + new <v>, fullCalcOnLoad="1"
```

</details>

---

## §2 — For agents

### Context

W-16 asked for recalculation on the plugins verdict's single-provider
`derive` hook, with IronCalc (MIT/Apache-2.0) as the engine.

### Decision

1. **`formulas({ preload?, wasm? })`** → `{ id: 'formulas', provides:
   ['derive', 'exportPatch'] }` plus `ready()`, `cycles()`, `unsupported()`,
   `stateOf()`, `built()`; `ui(engine?)` (`formulas-ui`) carries the overlay
   and the controls. Importing `@sheetpane/formulas` registers `formulas`;
   `@sheetpane/formulas/ui` registers `[formulas(), ui()]`. Runtime: the peer
   `@sheetpane/grid` and `@ironcalc/wasm@0.9.0`, pinned.
2. **Lazy:** IronCalc is loaded by a dynamic `import()` on the first `derive`
   with a formula to calculate — a workbook with none never loads it until one
   is typed; `preload: true` warms it; `wasm` names its bytes or URL (Node).
   A failed load is retried on the next call.
3. **L9 — the model is a cache:** each cell's input is read from the store
   (a change, else the file's formula, else its value); the model is rebuilt
   when the workbook object changes; only computed values are read back.
   Only reachable cells are loaded (formulas, the ranges they and defined names
   reference); `INDIRECT` or `OFFSET` loads everything; a new formula loads
   its ranges when typed. `_xlfn.`, `_xlws.`, `_xlpm.` prefixes are stripped
   for the engine.
4. **Derive:** on load, only cells whose computed value differs from the
   saved one; on a change, every formula whose value changed and every typed
   formula. A file formula back at its saved value, and a typed formula
   reverted away, return `clear: true` (SR-GRID 21b), so ⟳ and export mean
   "recalculated". Calls queue; calls behind a running recalculation share one
   evaluation. Numbers compare at a 1e-14 relative tolerance; `null` equals
   `''`. Values are read at 15 significant digits.
5. **Errors:** `#DIV/0!`, `#REF!`, `#N/A` are values; a half-typed formula
   never throws (it shows IronCalc's `#ERROR!`). A cycle shows 0, as Excel
   does, is listed by `cycles()`, marked ↻ and named in the status line. A
   file formula IronCalc cannot calculate (`#NAME?`, `#SPILL!` or an engine
   error where Excel saved something else) keeps its saved value, is marked ≈
   and listed by `unsupported()` until it becomes computable.
6. **Export:** typed formulas become `<f>` + `<v>` (`t="e"`, `"str"`, `"b"`
   as needed); recalculated file formulas get a new `<v>` with their `<f>`
   (shared formulas included) kept; `fullCalcOnLoad="1"`. An untouched
   workbook's parts are byte-identical.
7. **UI:** `cellbar` — in View, `fx =…` as read-only text; in Edit the grid's
   own input holds the formula (SR-GRID 21b); `status` — Sum · Avg · Count of
   the selection, `⟳ N cells recalculated`, circular references; `cell`
   marks ⟳ (recalculated), ↻ (cycle), ≈ (unsupported); `overlay` — coloured,
   labelled outlines of the referenced ranges while a formula is edited
   (drawn as four edges, so cells stay clickable).
8. **`evaluate(formula, { sheet, ref })`** returns one formula's value
   synchronously, through a scratch cell (the sheet's last cell) set,
   evaluated, read and cleared — the workbook is never touched. It serves
   `@sheetpane/validation`'s `custom` rules (SR-VALIDATION decision 3); a
   workbook with a `custom` validation rule, or a conditional-format
   expression, formula operand or formula threshold (W-19), builds the model
   even without a formula cell.
   `undefined` until the model is built or while a recalculation is queued.

### Consequences

- **Codes (W-40, SR-CODES):** a failed recalculation is logged as SP-5201, an engine that did not load as SP-5202.
- **Enforced today:** `just test-pkg formulas` — 34 tests (derive on load
  and change, undo, revert, paste, cross-sheet and quoted names, defined
  names, CSV, cycles, errors, unsupported; export of typed and recalculated
  formulas and read-back; the cell bar, status and marks in a real
  `<sheetpane-excel>`; lazy load — no `.wasm` request before the first
  formula; preload; the parity and perf runs), plus SR-VALIDATION's
  `custom`-rule test through `evaluate()`.
- **Measured** (Arpit's MacBook, headless Chromium 156, 10 cores, under
  load from sibling agents): 250,000 rows with 10,000 formulas — the plugin
  adds about 0.4 s to a 6.1 s read (lightest run), one edit 40–48 ms; the
  `.wasm` loads in 34 ms. Parity: 3/3 formula cells of the W-13 fixtures,
  113/116 in a hand-written function probe (misses: `AGGREGATE`, `XLOOKUP`
  over array constants, `TEXTJOIN` with an empty literal — the test fails if
  the list changes).
- **Owed:** parity against **Excel-saved** fixtures (W-30, DoD 7's ≥ 99 %);
  perf on the reference machine against an `.xlsx` budget; reporting a cycle
  in `sheetpane-load`/`-change` detail (backlog B-032; today the status line
  and `cycles()`); 1904-date workbooks (IronCalc knows only 1900 — date
  functions over serials are off by 1,462 days); array and spilled formulas
  fall back to unsupported (the reader does not expose `t="array"`).
- The A1 and XML helpers duplicate `@sheetpane/export`'s small ones, to keep
  the grid the only peer.

### Alternatives considered

- Loading every non-empty cell — rejected: 2.6 s for 1.25 M cells and every
  evaluation slower.
- Reading values through IronCalc's General format — rejected: ~10
  significant digits.
- Returning every formula cell on load — rejected: ⟳ would mark every
  formula.
- An editable `fx` button in the cell bar — replaced by the grid's own input
  holding the formula (one place to edit a cell).

### Reference (required)

- [`packages/formulas/src/`](../packages/formulas/src/) · [`packages/formulas/test/`](../packages/formulas/test/)
- [`work/compare/plugins.compare.md`](../work/compare/plugins.compare.md) — the `derive` hook

### Veto condition

**Reopen this decision if:** IronCalc's value differs from Excel's cached
value in more than 1 in 100 formula cells across the real-app fixtures
(W-30), or a workbook without formulas requests the `.wasm`.

**How to check it:** `just test-pkg formulas`

<!-- source: records/0112_COMMENTS.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/main/records/0112_COMMENTS.md) -->

# SR-COMMENTS — @sheetpane/comments

## §1 — For humans

**What colleagues wrote in Excel shows in the review.** A cell's note or
comment thread arrives in the error list as a *File comment* — read-only,
filterable, shown at its cell.

**And the review goes back into the file.** On export, every error becomes an
Excel comment thread at its cell — the message, then *Should be* as a reply,
marked done when resolved — so someone without sheetpane reads the review in
Excel. On by default; the host can switch it off (the decider, 2026-10-18).

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    F["file: threadedComments · comments (notes) · persons"] -->|validate| E["errors author 'file' — read-only"]
    R["the review's errors"] -->|exportPatch| W["threadedCommentN · commentsN · vmlDrawingN · persons, rels, content types"]
    O["comments({ write:false }) / export({ comments:false })"] -.->|off| W
```

<details>
<summary><b>ASCII twin</b> — the same diagram, for terminals and diffs</summary>

```text
   file: threaded comments, notes, persons --validate--> errors (author 'file', read-only)
   review's errors --exportPatch--> threadedCommentN, commentsN, vmlDrawingN, persons + rels, content types
   comments({ write: false }) or export({ comments: false }) --> nothing written
```

</details>

---

## §2 — For agents

### Context

W-22 asked for comments both ways; the decider ruled writing on by default
with a host switch (2026-10-18). The error schema and the read-only rule for
`file` errors are SR-GRID's (decision 19b).

### Decision

1. **`comments({ write? })`** → `{ id: 'comments', provides: ['validate',
   'exportPatch'] }` and a read-only `lastExport: { written, skipped }`.
   Importing the package registers `comments`. No `./ui`; no runtime
   dependency; `@sheetpane/grid` is the only peer. String XML only — no
   `DOMParser`, no `document` — so it runs in Node.
2. **Read:** one draft per commented cell, `{ type: 'comment', severity:
   'note', author: 'file', found: <uploaded text or (blank)>, expected: '',
   message, status: 'open' }`. The message is the thread's first comment,
   its replies in file order, then the cell's note, each line led by
   `Name: ` (not twice). Excel's `tc=` placeholder notes are skipped; thread
   entries this review wrote are skipped.
3. **Write:** every error not authored `file`, at the top-left cell of its
   range. First comment `<id> · <Severity> · <Type name> · Found: <found>`,
   newline, the message; `expected` as a reply `Should be: <expected>`. All
   errors on one cell share one thread, `done="1"` only when every one is
   resolved. On a cell with someone's thread the errors join it as replies; on
   a cell holding a legacy note nothing is written and the error is reported
   `note-at-cell` in `lastExport.skipped` (the file author's note is never
   rewritten).
4. **Parts:** `xl/threadedComments/threadedCommentN.xml`, `xl/commentsN.xml`
   (author `tc={root}`, the placeholder text), `xl/drawings/vmlDrawingN.vml`
   (one hidden Note shape per cell, a free `o:idmap` block),
   `<legacyDrawing>` in schema position, `xl/persons/person.xml` (one person
   per author, `providerId="None"`); every rel and content type. Existing
   parts are **extended, never replaced**; a sheet whose parts cannot be
   parsed is left as is (`unreadable-part`).
5. **Ids:** a thread entry's id is the version-5 UUID of
   `sheetpane:<id>:<createdAt>` (`…#expected` for the reply); a person's, of
   `sheetpane-person:<name>`. A second export of the same review replaces its
   own entries in place; replies added in Excel are kept and re-pointed.
6. **Switches:** `write: false` for good; `ctx.exportOptions.comments ===
   false` (`<sheetpane-excel>.export({ comments: false })`, SR-GRID decision
   6) for one export — then the parts are byte-identical to the input. The
   plugin declares `exportOptions: [{ key: 'comments', label: 'Write review
   as Excel comments', default: true }]`, so the Download menu shows the
   switch (W-34; none when `write: false`).
7. **No font** is written: the legacy `<t>` is plain and the VML names none.

### Consequences

- **Codes (W-40, SR-CODES):** SP-5801 (a comment part with no container), SP-5802 (not a worksheet), SP-5803 (comments not written for a sheet).
- **Enforced today:** `just test-pkg comments` — 26 tests (notes and threads
  from the ExcelJS fixture and hand-written packages; read-only rows,
  author filter; the four parts, rels, content types and `legacyDrawing`
  order; extending existing parts; joining a thread; the note-at-cell skip;
  both switches byte-identical; export → reload → `setErrors` → export
  giving the same ids and counts; every written part well-formed; package
  shape and the Node-safe boundary).
- **Owed:** opening the exported fixture in Excel 365, Excel 2019 and
  LibreOffice (DoD 4) and fixtures saved by Excel with notes, threads and
  both — W-30, the decider's; validating the parts against the OOXML schema
  (backlog B-033). Unverified until then: whether Excel links the note to its
  thread by the `tc=` author alone (no `xr:uid` is written), the `dT` format
  (UTC, hundredths, no `Z`) and the computed VML anchors.
- Author names land in the file as personal data.
- The type name comes from `DEFAULT_ERROR_TYPES` and `BUILTIN_TYPE_NAMES`;
  a host's own `errorTypes` (on the element, not the store) are written by id.
- A plugin cannot report export warnings to the host's events; `lastExport`
  stands in (backlog B-032).

### Alternatives considered

- Reading `done` threads as `resolved` — kept `open`, as the DoD says; a
  ruling may change it.
- Converting a note to a thread, or appending to it, for an error on a note
  cell — rejected: it rewrites the file author's content.
- An id from `id` alone — rejected: ids restart at ERR-0001 each session.
- `crypto.subtle` for the UUID hash — rejected: `validate` is synchronous.

### Reference (required)

- [`packages/comments/src/`](../packages/comments/src/) · [`packages/comments/test/`](../packages/comments/test/)
- [`work/compare/plugins.compare.md`](../work/compare/plugins.compare.md)

### Veto condition

**Reopen this decision if:** Excel or LibreOffice reports a repair, or drops
a comment, on a file this plugin wrote (W-30).

**How to check it:** `just test-pkg comments`
