<!-- source: records/0113_CHARTS.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/main/records/0113_CHARTS.md) -->

# SR-CHARTS — @sheetpane/charts

## §1 — For humans

**A chart shows where Excel puts it.** Each chart in the workbook appears at
its cells: a frame naming its title, its type and its series, with **Show
source cells** to select the data it plots. The common types — bar, column,
line, pie, doughnut, scatter — are drawn; the rest stay a frame that says why.

**And it says when the review changed its data.** Edit a plotted cell and the
chart shows *data changed — Excel will redraw*. With the formulas plugin the
drawing follows the live cells; the file's chart part is never rewritten.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    P["drawingN.xml → c:chart → chartN.xml (read once, lazily)"] --> M["model: groups, series, refs, caches, colours"]
    M --> F["stage 1 frame: title · type · series · Show source cells"]
    M --> S["stage 2 SVG: bar · column · line · pie · doughnut · scatter"]
    C["store: changes / derived"] -->|tag, live values| S
    S --> O["overlay item at the anchor (scales with zoom)"]
```

<details>
<summary><b>ASCII twin</b> — the same diagram, for terminals and diffs</summary>

```text
   drawingN.xml -> c:chart -> chartN.xml (read once, lazily) -> model (groups, series, refs, caches, colours)
   model -> stage 1 frame (title, type, series, Show source cells)
   model -> stage 2 SVG (bar, column, line, pie, doughnut, scatter) <- store changes / derived (tag, live values)
   SVG -> overlay item at the anchor, scaled with zoom
```

</details>

---

## §2 — For agents

### Context

W-21 asked for charts on the plugins verdict's `overlay` hook, in two
stages, with no chart library (L2 rules one out as a dependency the reviewer
does not need). Anchors are SR-IMAGES' arithmetic.

### Decision

1. **`charts({ draw? })`** → `{ id: 'charts', provides: ['overlay'] }`;
   `draw: false` keeps every chart a frame. `ui()` (`charts-ui`) adds a
   `status` line naming the source under the selection (or "N charts") and
   the Mod+Shift+U shortcut for Show source cells. Importing
   `@sheetpane/charts` registers `charts`; `/ui` registers `[charts(),
   ui()]`. Peers: `@sheetpane/grid` and `@sheetpane/images` (`anchorRect`,
   `cellAt`); no runtime dependency.
2. **Items:** one per `kind: 'chart'` drawing with a chart part; the id
   carries a workbook generation; the rectangle is SR-IMAGES' anchor
   arithmetic in the grid's geometry. The item is a `group` (it holds a
   button) named by the title once the part is read, else the drawing's
   description or name; the drawing inside is `role="img"` with a `<title>`.
3. **Reading:** on first render through `book.part()`, once per workbook,
   cached; DOMParser by local name. A missing or malformed part gives a
   labelled frame. Title: rich text, else the title reference's cache, else
   the only series' name, else "Chart". Type label from the plot-area
   element, `barDir` and `grouping` ("column + line" for a combination).
4. **Show source cells** selects the union of the plotted ranges when they
   tile one rectangle, else the first series' values (a selection is one
   rectangle — backlog B-034); across sheets; disabled when the data is
   literal.
5. **The tag** "data changed — Excel will redraw" shows while a `value` or
   `formula` change lies in a range the chart reads (names, categories,
   values), drawn in the SVG's title band so it scales with zoom.
6. **Stage 2** draws exactly one group of bar, column (clustered, stacked,
   100 %), line, pie, doughnut or scatter that is not a pivot chart; area,
   radar, 3-D, combination and pivot charts stay frames saying why. Values:
   the cached points, or the live cells (`store.value`) when a `derive`
   plugin is installed (`data-values` says which). Own SVG: a `viewBox` the
   anchor's size, no font named, every file string escaped, colours checked
   as `#RRGGBB`; nice ticks (1, 2, 2.5, 5 × 10ⁿ); pies from 12 o'clock plus
   `firstSliceAng`, clockwise.
7. **Colours:** explicit `solidFill` (srgb, scheme, sys with
   lumMod/lumOff/tint/shade), else the theme's accents by `c:idx`, else
   Office's. File colours are data: the same in both themes (SR-GRID 15a).
8. **Export:** nothing — patch mode copies the chart parts byte for byte.
9. **Edit:** a click on the frame away from its button selects the cell
   under it.

### Consequences

- **Codes (W-40, SR-CODES):** a malformed chart part is logged as SP-5701, a part with no chart as SP-5702.
- **Enforced today:** `just test-pkg charts` — 43 tests (the model of every
  type; frames at their anchors; Show source cells; the tag and undo; stage 2
  against the series' values — bar lengths proportional, line points linear,
  slice angles, scatter positions; colours; live values through a `derive`
  provider; zoom; the accessible names; the chart part byte-identical on
  export), and SR-GRID's geometry and overlay tests.
- **Owed:** fixtures with each type **saved by Excel** — W-30; a run with
  the real `@sheetpane/formulas` (the live path is the store's, tested with a
  generic `derive` provider).
- Not drawn: data labels, trendlines, axis titles, secondary, log and date
  axes. Placement uses the grid's 28 px rows (SR-IMAGES).
- Contract gaps — multi-area selection, `selbar` `appliesTo`, context for
  `text()`, a dispose signal — are backlog B-034.

### Alternatives considered

- A chart library — ruled out by L2 and the bundle a reviewer does not need.
- An HTML title band over a letterboxed SVG, or a CSS transform with a
  ResizeObserver — rejected: neither scales exactly with zoom.
- Selecting the bounding box of non-adjacent ranges — rejected: it selects
  cells the chart does not read.

### Reference (required)

- [`packages/charts/src/`](../packages/charts/src/) · [`packages/charts/test/`](../packages/charts/test/)
- [SR-IMAGES](0107_IMAGES.md) — anchors

### Veto condition

**Reopen this decision if:** a frame stops matching its anchor's cells, a
drawn mark disagrees with its series value, or a chart part changes on
export.

**How to check it:** `just test-pkg charts`

**Code**

- [`packages/charts/src/index.ts`](../packages/charts/src/index.ts) · [`model.ts`](../packages/charts/src/model.ts) · [`svg.ts`](../packages/charts/src/svg.ts) · [`refs.ts`](../packages/charts/src/refs.ts) · [`colors.ts`](../packages/charts/src/colors.ts) · [`ui.ts`](../packages/charts/src/ui.ts)

**Project docs**

<!-- source: records/0114_CONDFMT.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/main/records/0114_CONDFMT.md) -->

# SR-CONDFMT — @sheetpane/condfmt

## §1 — For humans

**Cells light up the way Excel lights them.** A workbook's conditional
formats — "over 1,000 in red", a colour scale, data bars, duplicates, top 10,
a formula rule — are drawn on the cells they cover, and change as the
reviewer edits. Nothing here writes a rule: it shows what the file says.

**Colour never speaks alone.** Hovering a coloured cell names the rule
("Conditional: greater than 1000 · F2:F5"); the status line counts the
file's rules and says how many are not shown.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    F["file: conditionalFormatting + dxfs"] --> R["rules, one priority order per sheet"]
    S["store: values, changes, derived"] --> E["evaluate (cached per snapshot, targeted drops)"]
    R --> E
    E -->|decorate, after styles| G["the grid: fill · colour · weight · bar"]
    X["formulas.evaluate()"] -.->|expression rules| E
    E --> U["ui(): hover legend · cell bar · status count"]
```

<details>
<summary><b>ASCII twin</b> — the same diagram, for terminals and diffs</summary>

```text
   file: conditionalFormatting + dxfs --> rules (one priority order per sheet)
   store values, changes, derived ----> evaluate (cached per snapshot, targeted drops)
   formulas.evaluate() ...............> evaluate (expression rules)
   evaluate --decorate, after styles--> grid (fill, colour, weight, data bar)
   evaluate --> ui(): hover legend, cell bar, status count
```

</details>

---

## §2 — For agents

### Context

W-19 asked for conditional formatting as a second `decorate` provider after
`@sheetpane/styles` (SR-STYLES), render only; expression rules through
`@sheetpane/formulas` (SR-FORMULAS decision 8).

### Decision

1. **`condfmt()`** → `{ id: 'condfmt', provides: ['decorate'], after:
   ['styles'] }`: a rule's dxf overrides the static style per property.
   `ui()` (`condfmt-ui`) adds the legend and the count. Importing
   `@sheetpane/condfmt` registers `condfmt`; `/ui` registers `[condfmt(),
   ui()]`. Peers: `@sheetpane/grid` and `@sheetpane/styles` (`dxfCss`,
   `allowListed`, colours); no runtime dependency.
2. **Rules drawn:** `cellIs` (all eight operators), `containsText`,
   `notContainsText`, `beginsWith`, `endsWith`, `containsBlanks`,
   `notContainsBlanks`, `containsErrors`, `notContainsErrors`,
   `duplicateValues`, `uniqueValues`, `top10` (top/bottom, percent, ties
   included; percent is floor(n·rank/100), at least 1), `aboveAverage`,
   `colorScale`, `dataBar`, `expression`. **Skipped and counted:** `iconSet`
   (needs glyphs), `timePeriod`, unknown or malformed rules.
3. **Comparison** follows Excel: numbers < text < logicals, text without
   case, a blank as 0 or empty text; duplicates count text without case and
   never blanks.
4. **Priority** is one order per sheet across every block (file order breaks
   ties); a higher rule wins each property it sets and a lower one fills the
   rest; a matching `stopIfTrue` rule stops the walk; multi-area `sqref` is
   one range.
5. **Drawing:** a dxf through styles' `dxfCss` + `allowListed` (never a font
   family); a colour scale as `background-color`, 2 or 3 colours interpolated
   in sRGB with `min`, `max`, `num`, `percent`, `percentile`, `formula`
   thresholds; a data bar as a `background-image` gradient from `minLength`
   (10) to `maxLength` (90) %. A rule fill with no text colour keeps the
   static style's colour, else `fonts[0]`'s, else black. These colours are
   the file's data: the same in both themes (SR-GRID 15a); state tints and
   error rings sit above them (SR-GRID 15b).
6. **Formulas** — `expression`, formula operands, formula thresholds — run
   through the `derive` provider's synchronous `evaluate()`, shifted from the
   first range's top-left (`shiftFormula`, re-exported by the grid); without
   one they are skipped with reason `formula`. `skippedRules(store)` →
   `{ rules, shown, skipped[] }`.
7. **Live, cached:** range statistics per sheet and `sqref`, results per
   cell, keyed on the snapshot's `book`, `changes` and `derived`; a change
   drops the changed cells, every cell of a range whose statistics hold one,
   and every result that read another cell; a `#style:` change drops only its
   cell; a new workbook resets all.
8. **UI:** hovering a rule-coloured cell shows `Conditional: <the rule in
   words>` and its range (an overlay with `passThrough`); the cell bar names
   the selected cell's rules; `status`: "n conditional rules from the file"
   (· k not shown).

### Consequences

- **Enforced today:** `just test-pkg condfmt` — 44 tests (one hand-made
  fixture per rule type compared cell by cell through the plugin and a real
  `<sheetpane-excel>`; priority and `stopIfTrue`; scales and bar widths;
  expressions through the real `@sheetpane/formulas`, including a workbook
  without a formula cell; live re-evaluation counted; the order against
  styles, in both registration orders; the legend, the count and error rings
  over rule fills; L5; the package shape and the headless boundary).
  Mutation runs on the evaluator (stopIfTrue, statistics drop, volatile drop)
  each failed tests.
- **Owed:** a fixture per rule type **saved by Excel** — W-30.
- Not drawn: x14 data-bar extensions (negative colour, axis, solid fill,
  `showValue`), icon sets; a dxf's `<b val="0"/>` is lost at import.
- The hover legend reads the grid's cell elements (`data-r`, `data-c`): the
  plugin host has no per-cell hover text (backlog B-034); controls get no
  store, so the plugin keeps one per workbook from `decorate`.

### Alternatives considered

- Recomputing statistics per cell, or dropping the whole cache on any change
  — rejected for cost.
- A `title` through `decorate` — not on the allow-list; a `cell` control
  mark — its label is fixed and it would mark every coloured cell.
- Icon sets in v1 — they need glyphs.

### Reference (required)

- [`packages/condfmt/src/`](../packages/condfmt/src/) · [`packages/condfmt/test/`](../packages/condfmt/test/)
- [SR-STYLES](0110_STYLES.md) decision 8 — the helpers

### Veto condition

**Reopen this decision if:** a cell in a real-app fixture (W-30) is coloured
differently from Excel by a rule type listed as drawn, or a rule fill hides a
sheetpane mark.

**How to check it:** `just test-pkg condfmt`

**Code**

- [`packages/condfmt/src/index.ts`](../packages/condfmt/src/index.ts) · [`rules.ts`](../packages/condfmt/src/rules.ts) · [`evaluate.ts`](../packages/condfmt/src/evaluate.ts) · [`ui.ts`](../packages/condfmt/src/ui.ts)

**Project docs**

- [`work/compare/plugins.compare.md`](../work/compare/plugins.compare.md) · [`work/reference/design/boards/Plugin-CondFmt.dc.html`](../work/reference/design/boards/Plugin-CondFmt.dc.html)

<!-- source: records/0115_FIXTURES.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/main/records/0115_FIXTURES.md) -->

# SR-FIXTURES — @sheetpane/fixtures

## §1 — For humans

**Test files you don't have to make.** A host, a demo or a test loads a known
workbook and knows what is in it: its sheets, its titles, the features it
exercises, the errors the rules sample produces on it.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    M["scripts/make.mjs (writeZip)"] --> F["files/: showcase · rules · edge · csv"]
    M --> J["fixtures.json + src/manifest.ts + src/urls.ts"]
    F --> A["url() · path() · bytes() · info()"]
    J --> A
    A --> T["tests · demos · @sheetpane/testing"]
```

<details>
<summary><b>ASCII twin</b> — the same diagram, for terminals and diffs</summary>

```text
   scripts/make.mjs (writeZip) --> files/ (showcase, rules sample, edge cases, csv dialects)
                               --> fixtures.json, src/manifest.ts, src/urls.ts
   files + manifest --> url(), path(), bytes(), info() --> tests, demos, @sheetpane/testing
```

</details>

---

## §2 — For agents

### Context

W-42 asked for the samples scattered across `examples/` and the plugins' test
helpers to become one package any runner can load (W-32 made the showcase).

### Decision

1. **The package** has no dependencies (`@sheetpane/export` is a
   devDependency of the generator only) and ships `dist/` and `files/` —
   the one exception to SR-BUILD decision 7's `dist`-only rule, so that
   `url()` reaches the files from `src/` and `dist/` alike. `./files/*` is
   exported.
2. **The files** — `showcase.xlsx`, `showcase.rules.json`, `edge/` (empty,
   hidden sheet, non-ASCII names, merged, 1904, formula errors, a legacy
   `.xls`, not a ZIP), `csv/` (comma, semicolon, tab, BOM, quoted, formula
   guard) — are written by `scripts/make.mjs`, never hand-zipped, and are the
   same byte for byte on every run (`writeZip`'s fixed timestamps). The
   250,000-row case is `hugeCsv(rows)`, not a file.
3. **The manifest** `files/fixtures.json` (and `src/manifest.ts`, generated
   beside it) lists per file its kind, `appSaved` (null for hand-built), its
   sheets with titles, its features, and for the rules sample the cells it
   fails; refused files are `kind: "refused"`.
4. **The API:** `url(name)` (one literal `new URL('../files/…',
   import.meta.url)` per file in the generated `src/urls.ts`, so every
   bundler copies each — a template string reaches no subfolder),
   `path(name)` (Node), `bytes(name)` (disk in Node, `fetch` elsewhere, typed
   without Node's types), `info(name)`, `MANIFEST`, `hugeCsv(rows)`.
5. **Used by** both demos (the gallery and the Rules file tab) and the grid's
   rules-file test; `@sheetpane/testing` (W-41) loads from here.

### Consequences

- **Enforced today:** `pnpm exec vitest run --project fixtures --project
  node` — every listed file read in Chromium matches its sheets and titles;
  refused files are refused; the hidden sheet and 1904 read as listed; the
  rules sample on the showcase fails exactly the listed cells; `path()` and
  `bytes()` in Node; `hugeCsv()`. `pack-check` checks the `./files/*` folder.
- **Owed:** files saved by Excel, Google Sheets, LibreOffice and Numbers,
  with `appSaved` naming the app and version — W-30 (DoD 5). The import
  package's ExcelJS fixtures stay with their generator (ExcelJS is that
  package's devDependency).

### Alternatives considered

- Fixtures inside `dist/` only — rejected: `url()` from `src/` (the
  workspace's `source` condition) would point at nothing.
- One template `new URL(\`../files/${name}\`, import.meta.url)` — rejected:
  Vite rewrites it into a one-level glob and subfolders resolve to nothing.

### Reference (required)

- [`packages/fixtures/`](../packages/fixtures/) · [`packages/fixtures/scripts/make.mjs`](../packages/fixtures/scripts/make.mjs)

### Veto condition

**Reopen this decision if:** a listed file stops matching its manifest, or the
generator writes different bytes from the same source.

**How to check it:** `just fixtures && git diff --exit-code packages/fixtures/files`

---

is never listed here.*

**Records** — [SR-BUILD](0102_BUILD.md) · [SR-GRID](0105_GRID.md) · [SR-LAW-3](0005_LAW-3-xlsx-and-csv-only.md)

**Code**

- [`packages/fixtures/src/index.ts`](../packages/fixtures/src/index.ts) · [`packages/fixtures/scripts/make.mjs`](../packages/fixtures/scripts/make.mjs)

<!-- source: records/0116_SKILLS.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/main/records/0116_SKILLS.md) -->

# SR-SKILLS — @sheetpane/skills

## §1 — For humans

**A host's agent knows sheetpane.** One command copies sheetpane's skills into
a repository, so Claude Code, Kiro and Codex embed, load, export, review, rule,
theme, test and extend sheetpane from the same text — each skill pointing back
to the record it summarises.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    P["@sheetpane/skills: skills/ · entry/ · bin/"] --> I["npx sheetpane-skills install"]
    I --> C[".claude/skills · CLAUDE.md block · .claude/agents"]
    I --> K[".kiro/skills · steering · .kiro/agents"]
    I --> X[".agents/skills · AGENTS.md block"]
    T["test/skills.test.ts"] -.drift check.-> P
```

<details>
<summary><b>ASCII twin</b> — the same diagram, for terminals and diffs</summary>

```text
   @sheetpane/skills (skills/, entry/, bin/) --npx sheetpane-skills install--> .claude/, .kiro/, .agents/ (+ marked blocks)
   test/skills.test.ts checks every skill against the elements' source
```

</details>

---

## §2 — For agents

### Decision

1. **The package** ships `skills/`, `entry/`, `bin/` only, has no
   dependencies and no build, and is a `dependency` of export, import, grid
   and all eight plugins at the lockstep version — SR-BUILD decision 7's
   second exception. `@sheetpane/grid` exposes the same `sheetpane-skills`
   bin (`src/skills-bin.ts` forwards to `@sheetpane/skills/bin`), because
   package managers link only direct dependencies' bins.
2. **The skills:** 23 folders `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` — 21 for hosts, two
   for contributors (`sheetpane-file-work-item`, `sheetpane-records`), and the
   router `sheetpane`. Frontmatter is the subset all three tools read: `name`
   (= folder), `description` (≤ 250 characters, saying when to use it **and
   when not**), optional `license` and `metadata` (`audience`). A `SKILL.md`
   is ≤ 200 lines. A skill links to its records on GitHub (so the links work
   once installed elsewhere) and never restates a rule as its own
   (SR-LAW-0).
3. **Entry files:** `entry/claude.md` and `entry/agents.md` — a ≤ 30-line
   block between `<!-- sheetpane:start -->` / `<!-- sheetpane:end -->`;
   `entry/kiro-steering.md` (`inclusion: fileMatch`); `entry/claude-agent.md`
   and `entry/kiro-agent.json` (a `sheetpane-integrator`, the Kiro one listing
   the skills as `skill://` resources).
4. **The installer** `bin/sheetpane-skills.mjs` (Node ≥ 20, no dependencies,
   no `postinstall`): `install` / `uninstall`, `--claude --kiro --codex
   --all`, `--skip` / `--only` (groups or skills), `--skills-only`,
   `--no-mcp`, `--dry-run`, `--force`, `--cwd`. With no tool flag it installs
   for the tools whose folders exist. It edits only the marked blocks of
   `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md`, refuses to overwrite a file changed since it
   wrote it unless `--force`, and records every path in
   `.sheetpane-skills.json` so `uninstall` removes exactly those.
4a. **The MCP server entry (W-39, SR-MCP decision 8):** unless `--no-mcp` or
   `--skills-only`, install also registers `@sheetpane/mcp` (`npx -y
   @sheetpane/mcp`) — the `sheetpane` key of `mcpServers` in `.mcp.json`
   (Claude Code) and `.kiro/settings/mcp.json` (Kiro), every other key kept;
   a `# sheetpane:start` … `# sheetpane:end` block holding
   `[mcp_servers.sheetpane]` in `.codex/config.toml` (Codex). A config that is
   not a JSON object, an entry edited since install, or a
   `[mcp_servers.sheetpane]` outside the block is refused without `--force`;
   `uninstall` removes the entry, and the file only when install created it
   and nothing else is left.
5. **The drift check** (`test/skills.test.ts`) reads every skill and fails on
   a frontmatter key outside the subset, a `name` ≠ folder, a description over
   250 characters or without its "not for", a `SKILL.md` over 200 lines, a
   link that does not resolve, or an event, element attribute or member that
   the elements' source does not have (derived from `observedAttributes`, the
   classes' members and the events the packages fire).
6. **Dogfood:** this repository installs its two contributor skills for all
   three tools (`--only contributor --skills-only`); its own `CLAUDE.md` is
   governed by SR-WORK-DOCS and is not written by the installer.

### Consequences

- **Enforced today:** `test/skills.test.ts` — the drift check per skill and
  the installer in temp repositories (each tool and all, re-run no-op,
  hand-edit refused without `--force`, the block replaced with the text
  outside kept, uninstall restoring the repo, `--dry-run`, `--skip
  contributor`, Windows paths); `test/packages.test.ts` (the package shape
  and its font scan of `skills/`, `entry/`, `bin/`); `pack-check`.
- **Owed:** one real prompt per tool from the packed tarballs — the
  decider's (W-35 DoD 8). Skill 18 (`sheetpane-frameworks`) was written with
  W-37's typings; `sheetpane-react` points at `@sheetpane/grid/jsx`.

### Alternatives considered

- A `postinstall` that writes skills — rejected: pnpm blocks lifecycle
  scripts by default, and writing into a repository unasked is wrong.
- Reading skills from `node_modules` — none of the three tools does.
- Relative record links — rejected: they break once the skills sit in
  another repository.

### Reference (required)

- [`packages/skills/`](../packages/skills/) · [`test/skills.test.ts`](../test/skills.test.ts)

### Veto condition

**Reopen this decision if:** a skill names an API the elements do not have, or
`uninstall` leaves a file `install` wrote.

**How to check it:** `pnpm exec vitest run --project repo test/skills.test.ts`

<!-- source: records/0117_CODES.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/main/records/0117_CODES.md) -->

# SR-CODES — stable error codes

## §1 — For humans

**An error you can look up.** `SP-3012: header row 2 not found — …/ERRORS.md#sp-3012`
tells a host — or an agent — what happened and where the fix is. Codes are
permanent: a code is never reused or renumbered.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    R["CODES (packages/export/src/codes.ts)"] --> H["spError · spMessage · codeOf"]
    H --> T["throws · console · notes · load refusals · blocked edits"]
    R --> D["docs/ERRORS.md (index generated)"]
    C["test/error-codes.test.ts + lock"] -.checks.-> T & D & R
```

<details>
<summary><b>ASCII twin</b> — the same diagram, for terminals and diffs</summary>

```text
   CODES (export/src/codes.ts) --> spError, spMessage, codeOf --> throws, console, notes, load refusals, blocked edits
   CODES --> docs/ERRORS.md (index generated)
   test/error-codes.test.ts + error-codes.lock.json check all three
```

</details>

---

## §2 — For agents

### Decision

1. **Every message sheetpane shows a host carries `SP-` and four digits:**
   thrown errors, `console.warn` / `console.error`, rules-engine `note`
   errors, refused loads, event details that carry a reason.
2. **Ranges:** 1xxx import · 2xxx export (21xx `download()`) · 3xxx grid ·
   4xxx `<sheetpane-errors>` · 5xxx plugins (5100 numfmt, 5200 formulas,
   5300 styles, 5400 validation, 5500 condfmt, 5600 images, 5700 charts,
   5800 comments) · 6xxx column rules and the rules file · 7xxx mcp
   (W-39: SP-7001…7007, the MCP server's tool errors — SR-MCP decision 7;
   `@sheetpane/mcp` also reports the 60xx rules notes `check_rules` finds).
3. **Never reuse:** a code is never renumbered or removed; a dead one stays in
   `CODES` with `retired: true`; `test/error-codes.lock.json` is append-only.
4. **The registry** is `CODES` in `packages/export/src/codes.ts` (the leaf
   every package depends on): titles and severity only — the long text lives
   in the docs. Plugins read it through `@sheetpane/grid`'s re-export.
5. **One helper:** `spMessage(code, detail)` →
   `SP-xxxx: <title> — <detail> (<docs>#sp-xxxx)`; `spError` builds an Error
   carrying `code`, `spCode`, `spDetail`; `codeOf(x)`, `detailOf(x)`,
   `codeUrl(code)`.
6. **Where the code lives:** `spCode` on every thrown error; where `code` was
   free it is the SP code (plain errors, `SheetpaneError.code`, the
   `sheetpane-editcancel` detail); where `code` is already a typed reason
   (`ExportError`, `ImportError`, `LoadState`) it stays and `spCode` sits
   beside it. Messages keep their old text after the code.
7. **`docs/ERRORS.md`:** one entry per code (`### SP-xxxx`): meaning, likely
   cause, fix, the record it comes from; its index is generated from `CODES`
   and compared by the test (`SP_WRITE_ERRORS_DOC=1` rewrites it).

### Consequences

- **Enforced today:** `test/error-codes.test.ts` (87) scans `packages/*/src`
  for a throw (outside a three-line, reasoned allow-list), a console line not
  built by `spMessage`, or a rules note without a code; checks ranges, the
  lock, a docs entry per code and none without one, and the index. 73 codes at
  W-40.
- Hosts that matched message text keep working; they should move to `spCode`
  / `codeOf()`.
- Consumers: the troubleshoot skill (W-35) and the MCP `explain_code` tool
  (W-39) read `CODES`.

### Alternatives considered

- Replacing `.code` with the SP code — rejected: it breaks the typed reasons
  the grid, hosts and tests read.
- A generator script under `scripts/` — rejected: the test renders and
  compares the index.
- A code per throw site for `ExportError` / `ImportError` — not yet: one code
  per typed reason, the docs list each reason's causes; finer codes can be
  added without reusing any.

### Reference (required)

- [`packages/export/src/codes.ts`](../packages/export/src/codes.ts) · [`docs/ERRORS.md`](../docs/ERRORS.md) · [`test/error-codes.test.ts`](../test/error-codes.test.ts)

### Veto condition

**Reopen this decision if:** a code is reused or renumbered, or a message
reaches a host without one.

**How to check it:** `pnpm exec vitest run --project repo test/error-codes.test.ts`

- [`packages/export/src/codes.ts`](../packages/export/src/codes.ts) · [`test/error-codes.test.ts`](../test/error-codes.test.ts) · [`test/error-codes.lock.json`](../test/error-codes.lock.json)

<!-- source: records/0118_TESTING.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/main/records/0118_TESTING.md) -->

# SR-TESTING — @sheetpane/testing

## §1 — For humans

**A host's tests read like what a reviewer does:** `await sp.edit('B2', '42');
expect(await sp.readDownload()).toHaveCell('Sheet1!B2', 42)` — in Playwright and
in Vitest browser mode, through the hooks the grid promises to keep.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    T["the host's test"] --> P["@sheetpane/testing/playwright — sheetpane(page)"]
    T --> D["@sheetpane/testing/dom — sheetpane(element)"]
    P & D --> H["roles · labels · data-sp-* (SR-GRID 9a)"]
    P & D --> R["readFile · changesBetween · matchers"]
```

<details>
<summary><b>ASCII twin</b> — the same diagram, for terminals and diffs</summary>

```text
   host test --> sheetpane(page) [Playwright] | sheetpane(element) [Vitest browser]
             --> only roles, labels and data-sp-* hooks (SR-GRID 9a)
             --> readFile, changesBetween, valueAt, matchers (toHaveCell, toHaveError)
```

</details>

---

## §2 — For agents

### Decision

1. **The package** has three entries: `.` (`readFile`, `changesBetween`,
   `valueAt`, `matchers`, the driver types), `./playwright` (`sheetpane(page,
   { excel?, errors? })`) and `./dom` (`sheetpane(element, { errors? })`).
   Dependencies `@sheetpane/import` and `@sheetpane/skills`;
   `@playwright/test` and `vitest` are optional peers — Playwright's Page and
   Locator are typed structurally, never imported.
2. **One API** for both drivers: `waitForLoad`, `ref`, `select`, `edit`,
   `paste`, `flag`, `resolve`, `undo`, `switchSheet`, `download`,
   `readDownload`, `errors`, `value`, `text`. A cell is `B3`, `Sheet1!B3` or
   `{ column, row, sheet? }` (the title read from the element's
   `header-row`).
3. **Only committed hooks:** roles, labels and SR-GRID decision 9a's
   `data-sp-*` attributes — never CSS classes. A hook the helpers need is
   added to that list first.
4. **Acting as a person:** clicks, the cell bar, a paste event, the Download
   button (Playwright's download event; in the DOM driver `sheetpane-export`
   is captured and the browser's save prevented); `flag` fills the form where
   it opens (SR-GRID decision 13) and waits for it to close.
5. **Reading back:** `readFile` reads through `@sheetpane/import` in a page
   and in Node alike — the import package reads `.xlsx` without `DOMParser`
   since W-39 (SR-IMPORT decision 8), so the values-only Node reader this
   package carried at first is gone: one reader.
6. **Dogfood:** `scripts/demo-check.mjs` drives the review steps (load, flag,
   resolve, edit, Download read back) with these helpers.

### Consequences

- **Enforced today:** `--project testing` (the DOM driver, every helper, in
  Chromium; Firefox and WebKit nightly) and `--project node` (the Playwright
  driver against the HTML demo; the Node reader on `@sheetpane/fixtures`'
  showcase); `demo-check`.
- **Owed:** each starter template ships one test using these (W-43).

### Alternatives considered

- Requiring a DOM shim in Node to read `.xlsx` — rejected. A values-only
  reader of its own served until the import package read `.xlsx` in Node
  (W-39); two readers of one format was the cost, now paid off.
- Locating by CSS classes — rejected: restyling would break every host's tests.

### Reference (required)

- [`packages/testing/`](../packages/testing/)

### Veto condition

**Reopen this decision if:** a helper needs a CSS class, or a hook in SR-GRID 9a
changes name without a major version.

**How to check it:** `pnpm exec vitest run --project testing --project node`

**Code**

- [`packages/testing/src/playwright.ts`](../packages/testing/src/playwright.ts) · [`dom.ts`](../packages/testing/src/dom.ts) · [`read.ts`](../packages/testing/src/read.ts)

<!-- source: records/0119_MCP.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/main/records/0119_MCP.md) -->

# SR-MCP — @sheetpane/mcp

## §1 — For humans

**An agent asks; sheetpane answers from what ships.** `npx @sheetpane/mcp`
starts a server any MCP client can use. Every answer is computed — from the
custom-elements manifest, the import package, the grid's rules checker, the
error docs and the skills — never generated, so the same question always gets
the same answer.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["agent (Claude Code, Kiro, Codex)"] -- "stdio, JSON-RPC" --> S["sheetpane-mcp"]
    S --> D["describe_api — custom-elements.json"]
    S --> I["inspect_workbook · draft_rules — @sheetpane/import"]
    S --> C["check_rules — the grid's checkDocument"]
    S --> E["explain_code — docs/ERRORS.md"]
    S --> F["find_skill — @sheetpane/skills"]
```

<details>
<summary><b>ASCII twin</b> — the same diagram, for terminals and diffs</summary>

```text
   agent --(stdio, JSON-RPC, MCP 2026-07-28)--> sheetpane-mcp
       describe_api      <- custom-elements.json (W-37)
       inspect_workbook  <- @sheetpane/import (reads .xlsx in Node)
       draft_rules       <- @sheetpane/import
       check_rules       <- @sheetpane/grid checkDocument
       explain_code      <- docs/ERRORS.md
       find_skill        <- @sheetpane/skills descriptions
```

</details>

---

## §2 — For agents

### Context

Agents writing host code guessed attribute and event names, and could not
see inside a workbook or a rules file before wiring them. W-39 gives them a
server to ask.

### Decision

1. **The package** `@sheetpane/mcp`, bin `sheetpane-mcp`, Node ≥ 20. Runtime
   dependencies `@sheetpane/import`, `@sheetpane/grid` (its rules checker and
   code registry, both Node-safe — SR-LAW-8) and `@sheetpane/skills`; nothing
   else. Its build copies `docs/ERRORS.md`, the grid's `custom-elements.json`
   and a plugin table (from each plugin's `package.json`) into `dist/`.
2. **Hand-written protocol, no SDK** (`work/compare/mcp-server.compare.md`):
   JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio, one message per line; stdout carries protocol
   messages only. **Tools only** — no resources, prompts, sampling, roots or
   logging.
3. **Revision 2026-07-28, stateless:** no handshake is needed; a request's
   `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion"]` names the revision;
   `server/discover` returns `supportedVersions` and `capabilities`; every
   result carries `resultType: "complete"` and
   `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo"]`; `tools/list` is cacheable
   (`ttlMs`, `cacheScope: "public"`) and lists the tools in one fixed order.
   A version the server does not support → error −32022 with
   `{ supported, requested }`.
4. **Older clients:** `initialize` (2025-11-25 and 2025-06-18) is answered
   with that revision, and a request without the version `_meta` is answered
   the 2025 way (no `resultType`, no cache fields). JSON-RPC batches (removed
   in 2025-06-18) are an invalid request; a notification gets no reply.
5. **The tools**, each input schema JSON Schema 2020-12, `additionalProperties:
   false`:
   - `describe_api(name)` — an element, attribute, member, event (with or
     without `on`), `--sp-*` property, slot, part or plugin → its manifest
     entry (which carries the TSDoc) and its record link — an element before
     a same-named event (`sheetpane-errors` is both), a member's own `kind`
     kept as `memberKind`; near names when nothing matches (a name holding
     the ask, or a name of four letters or more the ask holds).
   - `inspect_workbook(path)` — sheets, rows × columns, dimension, the
     header-row guess (the first of the top ten rows whose two or more filled
     cells are all text), titles, each column's type (text, number, integer,
     date — by its number format — boolean, mixed, empty), blanks, up to 12
     distinct values, merges, freeze, counts of formulas, validations,
     conditional formats, pictures, charts and notes, and the plugins the file
     would use.
   - `draft_rules(path, sheet?)` — a W-33 rules file: per titled column
     `required` when it has no blanks, its type, `oneOf` for a text column of
     2–12 distinct values; `draft: true` and a note to review it; problems
     (no title, duplicate title, mixed types) listed.
   - `check_rules(rules, path?)` — the grid's `checkDocument` (the same 60xx
     notes the grid gives), each rule in words (`describeRule`); with a
     workbook, SP-6022 for a sheet it lacks, SP-6023 for a title no header row
     has, SP-6024 for a duplicate title — matched as the grid matches
     (trimmed, case-insensitive; the sheet's `headerRow`, else `*`'s, else 1).
   - `explain_code(code)` — title and severity from the registry; meaning,
     cause and fix from `docs/ERRORS.md`; the link.
   - `find_skill(task)` — words of the task against each skill's name (×3)
     and description, the "Not for …" clause left out; the top three.
6. **Read-only and bounded:** paths come from the agent and are only read;
   `.xlsx` and `.csv` only (SR-LAW-3, the import package refuses the rest);
   256 MB at most; no network, no writes.
7. **Errors:** a bad input is a tool result with `isError: true`, its text an
   SP code first — the reader's own (SP-10xx) or the server's SP-7001…7007 —
   never a crash; an unknown tool is −32602, an unknown method −32601.
8. **Registration:** `sheetpane-skills install` (SR-SKILLS) adds the server
   — `{ "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@sheetpane/mcp"] }` — under the
   `sheetpane` key of `.mcp.json` (Claude Code) and
   `.kiro/settings/mcp.json` (Kiro), and as a marked
   `[mcp_servers.sheetpane]` block in `.codex/config.toml` (Codex, trusted
   projects); `--no-mcp` leaves it out.

### Consequences

- **Enforced today:** `packages/mcp/test/mcp.node.test.ts` (`--project
  node`) — the protocol over a spawned server (discover, legacy initialize,
  list, call, every error), the schemas, golden outputs per tool on the
  showcase and the rules sample (`UPDATE_GOLDEN=1` rewrites them), bad input
  as tool errors; `test/skills.test.ts` for the registration; the error-code
  registry for 7xxx.
- **Not done:** a run against the MCP Inspector — it is an interactive tool;
  the spawned-server test stands in for it.

### Alternatives considered

- The official TypeScript SDK — rejected for now: several runtime
  dependencies for a server with six read-only tools; see the compare doc.
- Resources for the docs and records — rejected: tools answer a question;
  a resource dump is what `llms-full.txt` already is.

### Reference (required)

- [`packages/mcp/`](../packages/mcp/) · [MCP 2026-07-28 schema](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/blob/main/schema/2026-07-28/schema.ts)

### Veto condition

**Reopen this decision if:** a second transport (HTTP) or resources/prompts
are wanted, or the 2026-07-28 revision changes what a stateless request must
carry.

**How to check it:** `pnpm exec vitest run --project node packages/mcp`

<!-- source: records/0120_CREATE.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/main/records/0120_CREATE.md) -->

# SR-CREATE — create-sheetpane

## §1 — For humans

**One command, a running app that is tested and agent-ready:** `npm create
sheetpane@latest` asks for a folder, a framework, the skills and the MCP
server, and writes an app that shows a sheet and its errors panel, loads a
sample workbook with a rules file, and has one test that passes.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    C["npm create sheetpane"] --> T["templates/_shared + templates/&lt;t&gt;"]
    T --> I["install (npm · pnpm · yarn)"]
    I --> S["sheetpane-skills install (+ MCP server)"]
    S --> A["dev · build · preview · test"]
```

<details>
<summary><b>ASCII twin</b> — the same diagram, for terminals and diffs</summary>

```text
   npm create sheetpane -> copy _shared + <template>, fill placeholders
       -> install -> sheetpane-skills install [--skip contributor] [--no-mcp]
       -> dev / build / preview / test (Playwright on @sheetpane/testing)
```

</details>

---

## §2 — For agents

### Decision

1. **The package** is unscoped `create-sheetpane` — `npm create <name>` runs
   `create-<name>` — the one package outside `@sheetpane/` (SR-BUILD decision
   7's exception). It ships `bin/` and `templates/`, has no dependencies, no
   build and no `postinstall`, and moves in lockstep with the rest.
2. **The CLI** (`bin/create-sheetpane.mjs`, Node ≥ 20): a folder, `--template`
   (`vanilla` · `react` · `next` · `vue` · `angular` · `svelte`), `--skills
   all | host | none`, `--mcp` / `--no-mcp`, `--pm npm | pnpm | yarn` (default:
   the one that ran it), `--no-install`, `--yes`. It asks only at a terminal.
   It refuses a non-empty folder, writes nothing outside it, renames
   `_gitignore`, fills `__SHEETPANE_<KEY>__` placeholders — the version from
   its own `package.json` — then installs and runs `sheetpane-skills install
   --all` (`--skip contributor` for `host`, `--no-mcp` when asked).
3. **Every template is the same app:** `<sheetpane-excel>` (Edit) and
   `<sheetpane-errors>` on one `pane`, side by side; the sheet again behind a
   pop-up button (`display="popup"`); `showcase.xlsx` and its rules file
   copied from `@sheetpane/fixtures` into `public/` by `scripts/sample.mjs`
   before dev and build; one Playwright test on `@sheetpane/testing` (load, a
   rules finding, an edit read back from the download); the W-37 typings
   (`/jsx` for React and Next, `/vue`, `/svelte`); Angular through
   `CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA`; Next.js client-only (`next/dynamic`, `ssr:
   false`); a README pointing at the skills and the MCP server. No font
   (SR-LAW-5).
4. **Versions:** frameworks pinned exactly to what `create-check` built and
   tested; TypeScript 6.0.3 in the templates (Angular 22 and svelte-check
   need < 6.1). Every dependency is free and open source (SR-LAW-2).
5. **The check** (`scripts/create-check.mjs`, `just create-check [templates]`,
   and a CI job over the six): packs every package, runs the CLI from its own
   tarball, points `@sheetpane/*` at the tarballs, installs, runs the skills
   installer (and checks it wrote the skills, `.mcp.json` and `AGENTS.md`),
   builds and runs the template's test. A template that cannot pass is
   dropped, never shipped broken.

### Consequences

- **Enforced today:** `test/create.test.ts` (27: every template scaffolded
  with `--yes --no-install`, placeholders filled, the refusals, the install
  and skills commands per package manager with a stubbed runner);
  `create-check` per template in CI; `pack-check`.
- **Known:** Angular 22 needs Node ^22.22.3 or ^24.15.0 — the template's
  `engines`, a CLI note and its README say so.
- **Owed:** StackBlitz links per template (W-44 DoD 2).

### Alternatives considered

- `@sheetpane/create` (`npm create @sheetpane`) — kept as the fallback name;
  the unscoped one is the shorter command.
- Downloading templates from the repository at run time — rejected: the
  templates ship in the tarball, so the version matches and nothing is
  fetched but the install.

### Reference (required)

- [`packages/create-sheetpane/`](../packages/create-sheetpane/) · [`scripts/create-check.mjs`](../scripts/create-check.mjs)

### Veto condition

**Reopen this decision if:** a template fails `create-check` on a framework
release and cannot be fixed by a version bump, or a host needs a template the
six do not cover.

**How to check it:** `just create-check`

## References

*Every source this record cites, gathered in one place. An archived document
is never listed here.*
